flow.flex.brief: A fluent flexbox Node class for Flow: build nodes, chain style setters and compute their layout.

flow.flex.calculate_layout.brief:
Run the layout engine on a node tree without creating a Node instance.
Convenience function for callers using plain Lua table element trees.

flow.flex.Node.new.brief:
Create a new FlexNode with initial properties.
All fields have sensible defaults; only key is typically required.

flow.flex.Node.insert_child.brief:
Insert a child node at a given index (1-based, default = append).
Chainable — returns self.

flow.flex.Node.remove_child.brief:
Remove a child node by reference. No-op when child is not found.
Chainable — returns self.

flow.flex.Node.get_child.brief:
Return the child at a 0-based index (Yoga API convention).
Index 0 returns the first child.

flow.flex.Node.get_child_count.brief: Return the total number of children.

flow.flex.Node.set_style.brief: Set an arbitrary style property by key. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.get_style.brief: Read an arbitrary style property by key.

flow.flex.Node.set_width.brief: Set the fixed width in pixels. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_height.brief: Set the fixed height in pixels. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_width_percent.brief: Set the width as a percentage of the parent's width. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_height_percent.brief: Set the height as a percentage of the parent's height. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_min_width.brief:
Store a minimum width constraint in pixels. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not enforce it.

flow.flex.Node.set_min_height.brief:
Store a minimum height constraint in pixels. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not enforce it.

flow.flex.Node.set_max_width.brief:
Store a maximum width constraint in pixels. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not enforce it.

flow.flex.Node.set_max_height.brief:
Store a maximum height constraint in pixels. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not enforce it.

flow.flex.Node.set_flex_direction.brief: Set the main-axis direction for children. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_flex_grow.brief: Set how much this node grows to fill available space on the main axis. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_flex_shrink.brief:
Store the flex shrink factor. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_flex_basis.brief:
Store the flex basis value. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_justify_content.brief: Set how children are distributed along the main axis. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_align_items.brief: Set how children are aligned on the cross axis. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_align_self.brief: Override the parent's align_items for this node only. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_gap.brief: Set the gap between children in pixels. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_padding.brief: Set padding on one or more edges. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_padding_percent.brief: Set padding on one or more edges as a percentage of parent size. Chainable.

flow.flex.Node.set_margin.brief:
Store margin on one or more edges in pixels. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_margin_percent.brief:
Store margin on one or more edges as a percentage of parent size. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_border.brief:
Store border width on one or more edges in pixels. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_position.brief:
Store position offsets on one or more edges in pixels. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_position_type.brief:
Store the position type (static / relative / absolute). Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_flex_wrap.brief:
Store the flex wrap behavior. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_overflow.brief:
Store the overflow behavior. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_display.brief:
Store the display mode. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_aspect_ratio.brief:
Store the aspect ratio (width / height). Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_direction.brief:
Store the text direction for this subtree. Chainable.
Kept for API compatibility; the current layout engine does not consume it.

flow.flex.Node.set_measure_func.brief:
Attach a custom measure function to this node.
The measure function is called by the layout engine to determine intrinsic
content size (e.g. for text or image elements). Not used by the default
flow/layout.lua but reserved for compatibility with future extensions.

flow.flex.Node.calculate_layout.brief:
Run the layout engine on this node tree and store results in node.layout.
After calling this, use get_computed_* or get_layout() to read the results.

flow.flex.Node.get_layout.brief: Return the full layout result table ({x, y, w, h}) after calculate_layout().

flow.flex.Node.get_computed_left.brief: Return the computed left edge (x) of this node in layout space.

flow.flex.Node.get_computed_top.brief:
Return the computed top edge (y + h) of this node in layout space.
Note: layout uses bottom-left origin, so "top" = y + height.

flow.flex.Node.get_computed_width.brief: Return the computed width of this node in pixels.

flow.flex.Node.get_computed_height.brief: Return the computed height of this node in pixels.

def_behavior_tree.brief:
Event-driven behavior trees for NPC logic. Register node templates once with
`registerTemplates`, create a tree over a payload with `new`, and call `run`: each
node moves on only when the one before it reports success or failure, and a tree can
start from any node id, so an active node saved with a game can be resumed on load.

def_behavior_tree.new.brief:
Creates a tree that runs a registered tree template with no payload, so its task
callbacks receive `undefined`. Register the templates with `registerTemplates` first.

def_behavior_tree.Task.brief:
The lowest-level node, which has no children and runs your behavior code through
its template's `start`, `run` and `finish`. Its type name is `"Node"`.

def_behavior_tree.Composite.brief:
The archetype the four composites build on. Not a template type itself: use
`Sequence`, `Selector`, `Random` or `RandomWithChances`.

def_behavior_tree.Sequence.brief:
A composite that runs its children in order, the next one when the last succeeds.
It fails as soon as a child fails, and succeeds when the last child succeeds.

def_behavior_tree.Selector.brief:
A composite that runs its children in order, the next one when the last fails. It
succeeds as soon as a child succeeds, and fails when every child fails.

def_behavior_tree.Random.brief:
A composite that runs one child picked at random, by the tree's `rng` over
`1` to the child count, and reports that child's result.

def_behavior_tree.RandomWithChances.brief:
A composite that runs one child picked by weight: the tree's `rng` draws from `1` to
`100`, and each child's `chance` is its share of that range, so the chances should
add up to `100`. To weight a node registered by name, wrap it in a `ChanceDecorator`.

def_behavior_tree.Decorator.brief:
The archetype the five decorators build on. Not a template type itself: use one of
the decorators.

def_behavior_tree.InvertDecorator.brief: A decorator that reports the opposite of its child's result.

def_behavior_tree.AlwaysFailDecorator.brief: A decorator that fails whatever its child reports.

def_behavior_tree.AlwaysSucceedDecorator.brief: A decorator that succeeds whatever its child reports.

def_behavior_tree.RepeatUntilFailDecorat.brief:
A decorator that runs its child again each time it succeeds, and succeeds once the
child fails. A good root node.

def_behavior_tree.ChanceDecorator.brief:
A decorator that passes its child's result through, so a node registered by name
can carry a `chance` inside a `RandomWithChances`.

def_behavior_tree.registerTemplates.brief:
Registers the tree templates, giving every node of each tree under `TREES` its own
id. Call it once, before `new` creates any tree.

def_behavior_tree.getTreeTemplate.brief: Returns a registered tree template's nodes, indexed by node id.

def_behavior_tree.Registry.brief: The registry the tree templates are stored in.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.run.brief: Starts the tree at a node. Does nothing while the tree is `running`.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.restart.brief: Starts the tree at a node whether or not it is `running`.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.setActive.brief: Sets the node the tree is at, without running it.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.getNode.brief: Returns a node of this tree by id.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.success.brief: Finishes the root node and stops the tree. Called when the root succeeds.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.fail.brief: Finishes the root node and stops the tree. Called when the root fails.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.getRandom.brief: Returns a number from the tree's `rng`.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.name.brief: The registered tree this tree runs, from `config.tree_name`.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.payload.brief: The payload every task callback receives.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.running.brief: Whether the tree is running: set by `run` and `restart`, cleared when the root finishes.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.activeNod.brief: The node the tree is at, unset until the first `run` or `restart`. Save its `id` to resume later.

def_behavior_tree.BehaviorTree.rng.brief: The number generator `Random` and `RandomWithChances` draw with.

def_behavior_tree.TreeNode.id.brief: The node's id in its tree, from `1` at the root. Pass it to `run` or `restart`.

def_behavior_tree.TreeNode.name.brief:
The template's name for a node registered under `NODES`, followed by
` | <type name>` for one that is not a task; the type name for an inline node.

def_behavior_tree.TreeNode.chance.brief: The template's `chance`, if it gave one.

def_behavior_tree.TaskTemplate.chance.brief: This node's share of `1` to `100`, read only when a `RandomWithChances` lists it.

def_behavior_tree.TaskControl.success.brief: Reports the task as succeeded, which moves the tree on.

def_behavior_tree.TaskControl.fail.brief: Reports the task as failed, which moves the tree on.

def_behavior_tree.CompositeTemplate.chan.brief: This node's share of `1` to `100`, read only when a `RandomWithChances` lists it.

def_behavior_tree.DecoratorTemplate.chan.brief: This node's share of `1` to `100`, read only when a `RandomWithChances` lists it.

asobi.realtime.brief:
The realtime connection a client creates as `client.realtime`: one websocket that
authenticates the session, carries matchmaking, matches, worlds, chat, votes and
extension calls, and keeps a registry of the entities the server syncs.

asobi.realtime.new.brief:
Creates the realtime connection for a client. `create` calls it, so a project reaches the
connection as `client.realtime`.

asobi.realtime._is_auth_close.brief:
Internal. Whether a close or error reason means the session's token was rejected:
`connect`'s socket callback and `_handle_message` call it to choose `auth_expired`.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.on.brief:
Registers a handler for an event. A name `RealtimeEvents` does not list raises an error,
and handlers for one event run in the order they were registered. The reply to a request
made with a callback goes to that callback rather than to an event.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.connect.brief:
Opens the websocket and authenticates with the client's access token. Set
`request_binary_wire` and `request_datagram` before calling it, and register handlers
first. Does nothing while connected.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.update.brief:
Drains the datagram plane, and is a no-op without one. Call it once per frame from
`update` when `request_datagram` is set.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.disconnect.brief: Closes the datagram plane and the websocket.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.reauth.brief:
Re-authenticates the open socket with the client's current access token, after a token
refresh. Does nothing when not connected.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.join_match.brief: Joins a match by id. A running match accepts joiners while it has room.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.find_or_create_m.brief:
Joins a live match of `mode`, creating one when there is none. The server resolves it,
so simultaneous callers converge on one match. Needs an asobi server 0.86.0 or later.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.send_match_input.brief: Sends input to the current match.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.add_to_matchmake.brief:
Queues for a match with the matchmaker. Register `matchmaker_queued`, `error` and
`matchmaker_failed` first, or a failure goes unnoticed.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.quick_play.brief: Queues for a match with the matchmaker, as `add_to_matchmaker` does.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.remove_from_matc.brief: Takes a ticket out of the matchmaker.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.send_chat_messag.brief: Sends a message to a chat channel.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.ping.brief: Measures the round trip of one heartbeat.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.rpc.brief: Calls a server extension's RPC method. Calls may answer out of order.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.find_or_create_w.brief:
Joins an open world of `mode`, creating one when there is none. The server resolves it,
so simultaneous callers converge on one world.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.join_or_host.brief: Joins an open world of `mode` or hosts a new one, as `find_or_create_world` does.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.send_world_input.brief: Sends input to the current world.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._datagram_open.brief:
Internal. Opens the datagram plane: `_handle_message` calls it on `session.connected`
when `request_datagram` is set.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._datagram_stop.brief: Internal. Closes the datagram plane: `disconnect` and a failed open call it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._apply_pose.brief: Internal. Applies one datagram pose to `entities`: `update` calls it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._datagram_endpoi.brief:
Internal. Splits the `host:port` endpoint a datagram mint answers with: `_datagram_open`
calls it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._send_session_co.brief:
Internal. Sends `session.connect` with the access token: the open socket and `reauth`
call it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._send.brief:
Internal. Sends a frame with a correlation id and no callback: `leave_match`, `join_chat`
and the other methods that take no callback call it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._send_with_callb.brief:
Internal. Sends a frame and records its callback for the reply: the methods taking a
callback call it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._send_fire_and_f.brief:
Internal. Sends a frame with no correlation id: `send_match_input`, `send_world_input`,
`send_chat_message` and `send_heartbeat` call it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._apply_entity_up.brief: Internal. Applies one entity delta to `entities`: `_dispatch_tick` calls it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._dispatch_tick.brief:
Internal. Applies a `world.tick` or `match.state` frame and fires its events:
`_handle_message` and `_handle_binary` call it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._reconcile_keyfr.brief: Internal. Removes the entities a keyframe left out: `_dispatch_tick` calls it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._request_resync.brief: Internal. Asks the server for a zone's keyframe after a gap: `_dispatch_tick` calls it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._handle_binary.brief: Internal. Decodes a binary `world.tick` frame: `_handle_message` calls it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime._handle_message.brief: Internal. Routes one websocket message: the socket's callback calls it.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.client.brief: The client this connection belongs to.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.entities.brief:
Every synced entity's whole state, keyed by entity id. Emptied when a world is joined or
left.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.local_player_id.brief: The signed-in player's entity id, set once `connected` fires.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.request_binary_w.brief: Set before `connect` to ask for the binary `world.tick` encoding.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.wire.brief: The encoding the server granted, read once `connected` fires.

asobi.realtime.Realtime.request_datagram.brief:
Set before `connect` to also open the datagram plane, which carries entity positions
over UDP. It never opens on HTML5, and the websocket keeps carrying everything either way.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.error.brief:
An `error` frame, or `{ error }` with the websocket's message when the socket fails. A
frame whose `reason` rejects the access token fires `auth_expired` as well.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.connected.brief:
`session.connected`: the session is authenticated, and `local_player_id` and `wire` are
set. Send game messages only after this fires.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.match_stat.brief:
`match.state`: a match state snapshot. A `{ tick, updates }` frame has already updated
`entities` and fired the entity events and `tick`.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.match_matc.brief: `match.matched`: the matchmaker placed the player in a match, carrying its `match_id`.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.matchmaker.brief: `match.matchmaker_failed`: the match could not start, carrying a `reason`.
`matchmaker.queued`: the matchmaker accepted the ticket, carrying `ticket_id` and `players_needed`.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.chat_joine.brief: `chat.joined`: the player joined a chat channel.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.chat_left.brief: `chat.left`: the player left a chat channel.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.chat_messa.brief: `chat.message`: a message in a joined channel.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.game_messa.brief:
`game.message` or `module.message`: a message from the game module. The server sends
both names for each message, and the event fires for whichever the connection saw first.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.game_error.brief:
`game.error` or `module.error`: an error from the game module. The server sends both
names for each error, and the event fires for whichever the connection saw first.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.module_eve.brief: `module.event`: a named push from a server extension, carrying `event` and `data`.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.world_tick.brief:
`world.tick`: a world frame. It has already updated `entities` and fired the entity
events and `tick`.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.world_join.brief: `world.joined`: the player joined a world. `entities` is emptied first.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.world_left.brief: `world.left`: the player left the world. `entities` is emptied first.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.world_ack.brief:
`world.ack`: the highest input `seq` the server consumed. It fires only for inputs sent
with a `seq`.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.auth_expir.brief:
The server rejected the access token: the socket closed, or an `error` frame arrived,
for a revoked, invalid or idle-timed-out session. Sign in again rather than retrying.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.disconnect.brief: The socket closed for any other reason, `"closed"` when it gave none.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.entity_add.brief: An entity entered `entities`, with its full initial state.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.entity_upd.brief:
An entity changed. `state` is its whole merged state, never a partial one, and `changed`
names the fields that changed.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.tick.brief: A `world.tick` or `match.state` frame was applied, after its entity events.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.match_even.brief:
A `match.<name>` frame that a match script sent with `game.broadcast(name, payload)`.
Frames asobi itself sends keep their own events.

asobi.realtime.RealtimeEvents.world_even.brief:
A `world.<name>` frame that a world script sent with `game.broadcast(name, payload)`.
Frames asobi itself sends keep their own events.

asobi.realtime.WorldAck.tick.brief: The world tick the input was consumed by.

asobi.realtime.WorldAck.seq.brief: The highest `seq` passed to `send_world_input` that the server has consumed.

asobi.realtime.JoinOptions.ctx.brief: Passed untouched to the game module's join callback, such as a room code or a team pick.

asobi.realtime.ListOptions.has_capacity.brief: Only sessions with room for another player.

asobi.realtime.MatchmakerOptions.propert.brief: Properties the matchmaker groups tickets by.

asobi.realtime.RpcError.code.brief: The error code, `"internal"` when the server sent none.

asobi.realtime.RpcError.message.brief: A message for people, which may be reworded at any time.

gamepush.core.experiments.brief: GamePush experiments: the player's experiments and cohort checks.

gamepush.core.experiments.map.brief: The experiments the player takes part in, keyed by experiment tag; empty when none.

gamepush.core.experiments.list.brief: The same as `map`, kept for backward compatibility.

gamepush.core.experiments.has.brief: Whether the player is in a cohort of an experiment.

defarmy.brief:
Groups game objects (soldiers) into armies, places them in a built-in or customized
pattern, and moves and rotates each army as a group. Create an army with `army_create`
and a soldier for each game object with `soldier_create`, then call `soldier_move`
from each soldier's `update` and apply the position and rotation it returns.

defarmy.army_create.brief:
Creates a group of game objects (an army) with the given member padding and pattern,
and returns its id. `PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED` requires `pattern_func`, which upstream
asserts, and every other pattern ignores it. Any value outside `PATTERN` fails an
assert.

defarmy.army_members.brief:
Returns the ids of the soldiers in an army. The list is the army's own, so editing
it edits the army.

defarmy.army_remove.brief: Removes an army and releases its members, which stay as soldiers in no army.

defarmy.army_update_pattern.brief:
Changes an army's pattern and rearranges its members at once. `PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED`
requires `pattern_func`, which upstream asserts, and every other pattern ignores it.

defarmy.army_update_stickiness.brief: Changes whether an army's members are glued to their places in it.

defarmy.army_debug_draw.brief:
Draws an army's center and facing for one frame, by posting `draw_line` to
`@render:`. Call it every frame to keep it shown.

defarmy.soldier_create.brief: Creates a soldier and returns its id, joining it to an army when `army_id` is given.

defarmy.soldier_join_army.brief: Moves a soldier into an army, out of the army it was in.

defarmy.soldier_leave_army.brief:
Takes a soldier out of its army and rearranges the members left. A soldier in no
army is left as it is. At `v1` the rearrangement raises a Lua error when the soldier
was the army's last member, so call `army_remove` instead in that case.

defarmy.soldier_remove.brief:
Removes a soldier completely, rearranging the army it was in. `soldier_move` then
returns `undefined` for both values. At `v1` the rearrangement raises a Lua error
when the soldier was the army's last member, so call `army_remove` first in that
case.

defarmy.soldier_debug_on.brief:
Turns on a soldier's debug marks: each `soldier_move` call then posts `draw_line` to
`@render:` to mark the position the soldier is heading for with a cross.

defarmy.soldier_debug_off.brief: Turns off a soldier's debug marks.

defarmy.soldier_move.brief:
Calculates a soldier's next position and rotation, moving it toward its place in its
army. A soldier in no army keeps `current_position`. Returns `undefined` for both
values once the soldier is removed:
`const [position, rotation] = defarmy.soldier_move(id, go.get_position(), speed)`.

defarmy.PATTERN.brief:
The army patterns `army_create` and `army_update_pattern` take. The five named
patterns place the soldiers in built-in shapes. `CUSTOMIZED` takes its rows from the
`pattern_func` passed beside it.

in.cursor.brief: Cross-platform input handling for Defold: keyboard, mouse, gamepad, touch, and on-screen controls.

minit.brief:
Publishes an HTML5 game to the Minit platform. Each call talks to the `window.minit`
runtime the host injects into the page, through `html5.run`. Call `loading_done` once
the game is ready to show and `report_result` once when it ends. Outside an HTML5
build every call prints or returns a fixed result, so each is safe to call anywhere.

minit.loading_done.brief:
Signals the host that the game is booted and ready to show. The host keeps the game
hidden until this is called. Outside an HTML5 build it prints `loadingDone`.

minit.report_result.brief:
Submits the game's final result. Call it exactly once, when the game ends: the host
ignores a repeat call, and the SDK warns about it. A higher score ranks better by
default. For a time-sorted game (`resultSorting` `fastestTime` or `slowestTime` in
`meta.json`) the score is in seconds, never milliseconds, and fractions are allowed.
Outside an HTML5 build it prints the score.

minit.get_config_value.brief:
Reads a game config value from the page URL's query parameters (`?difficulty=hard`).
Declare each key the game reads in the `config` array of its `meta.json`. The key
`userData` is reserved and always returns the default. Outside an HTML5 build it
returns the default.

minit.get_user_data.brief:
Returns this player's single stored slot, which `report_result` writes through its
`user_data` option. Reads the host's `window.minit.userData`, else the `?userData=`
URL parameter when the host injected none, else returns `undefined`. A stored empty
value returns `""`, distinct from `undefined`. Outside an HTML5 build it returns
`undefined`.

minit.should_show_tutorial.brief:
Returns whether to run the first-play tutorial. `?tutorial=1` or `?tutorial=true`
forces it on and `?tutorial=0` or `?tutorial=false` forces it off; otherwise it
returns `false` only when the host reports that the player has played the game
before. Outside an HTML5 build it returns `true`.

minit.get_motion_quality.brief:
Returns the effects quality to run at. `?motionQuality=full` or
`?motionQuality=reduced` wins; next comes the host's `window.minit.motionQuality`
when it is one of the two; otherwise it returns `"reduced"` when
`prefers_reduced_motion` returns `true`, else `"full"`. Outside an HTML5 build it
returns `"full"`.

minit.prefers_reduced_motion.brief:
Returns whether the player or the operating system prefers reduced motion.
`?reducedMotion=1` or `?reducedMotion=true` forces `true` and `?reducedMotion=0` or
`?reducedMotion=false` forces `false`; next comes the host's
`window.minit.prefersReducedMotion` when it is a boolean; otherwise it returns
whether the browser matches the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query, or
`false` when the browser cannot tell. Outside an HTML5 build it returns `false`.

minit.get_device_tier.brief:
Returns the player's device tier. `?deviceTier=` set to `low`, `medium`, `high` or
`unknown` wins; next comes the host's `window.minit.deviceTier` when it is one of
the four; otherwise it returns `"unknown"`, which is also its result outside an
HTML5 build.

minit.is_viewable.brief:
Returns whether the game is visible to the player right now: the host's
`window.minit.isViewable()` when it has one, else whether `document.visibilityState`
is `visible`. It reads the value again on every call. Outside an HTML5 build it
returns `true`.

minit.on_viewable_change.brief:
Calls `fn` each time the game's viewability changes, starting from its value at
subscribe time, and returns a function that unsubscribes `fn`. Lua polls the value
every 0.25 s, so a change arrives up to about 250 ms late. Subscribing the same `fn`
again returns its existing unsubscribe, and unsubscribing twice is safe. An error
`fn` raises is printed and does not stop the other subscribers. The poll runs on a
`timer` that belongs to the script that subscribed last and stops with it, so
subscribe from a script that outlives the subscription and unsubscribe in its
`final`. Outside an HTML5 build `fn` is never called and the returned function does
nothing.

flow.ui.brief: Flow's gui_script renderer: mounts onto a script's self, renders an element tree to runtime GUI nodes and routes input to it.

flow.ui.register.brief:
Register a custom element type definition.
Every element type string ("box", "text", "button", etc.) must be registered
before it can appear in a UI tree. The definition describes how to create,
update, and interact with the corresponding Defold GUI node.

Required fields in def:
create_node(el) -> userdata — creates and returns a new gui node

Optional fields in def:
apply(self, el, node, alpha) — update node visuals each frame
is_visible(el) -> boolean — custom visibility check
is_hittable(el) -> boolean — custom hit-test eligibility
is_scroll_container -> boolean — marks element as scroll root
clips_children -> boolean — node is used as parent for children
capture_descendant_hits -> boolean — returns self instead of child on hit
is_backdrop_click_target -> boolean — receives backdrop click events
get_text_anchor(el) -> "left"|"center"|"right" — text pivot anchor for positioning
hover_begin(self, el, deps) — called when pointer enters element
hover_end(self, el, deps) — called when pointer leaves element
press_begin(self, el, deps) — called when element is pressed
press_update(self, el, is_hot, deps) — called while dragging over element
press_end(self, el, activated, deps) — called on release
on_wheel(self, el, delta, deps) — called on mouse wheel
on_drag_start(self, el, x, y, t, deps) — called when drag begins
on_drag_move(self, el, x, y, t, deps) — called each drag frame
on_drag_end(self, el, action, t, deps) — called when drag ends
update_anim(el, dt, deps) -> bool,bool — per-frame animation tick
render_extras(self, el, prefix, alpha, deps) — render auxiliary nodes
collect_extra_keys(el, prefix, keys, deps) — declare extra cached node keys
get_child_extra_offset_y(el) -> number — additional Y offset for children

flow.ui.get_size.brief:
Return the logical GUI display size (same as the [display] settings).

flow.ui.mount.brief:
Initialize the renderer state on a gui_script self table.
Must be called once in gui_script init() before any other ui calls.
Creates self.ui with an empty node cache, redraw flag, and debug toggle.

flow.ui.set_debug.brief:
Enable or disable debug logging for input and hit-testing.
When enabled, every touch press emits debug logs through `flow.log`
under the `ui.input` context.

flow.ui._set_layout_space_unsafe.brief:
Internal: switch between "window" and "gui" layout spaces.
In "window" mode, layout is computed in physical pixels and nodes are
scaled back to GUI space via _scale_x/_scale_y. This gives pixel-perfect
rendering on high-DPI displays. Not intended for direct consumer use.

flow.ui.request_redraw.brief:
Request a renderer redraw so the next M.update() call triggers a full re-render.
Call this whenever the data driving the UI tree changes and you want the
screen to reflect the new state immediately.

flow.ui.request_tree_redraw.brief:
Request a redraw for an element tree so renderer_core.update() re-renders it.
Use this when you hold a reference to a tree and want to force a re-layout
without going through the full renderer self table.

flow.ui.update.brief:
Update the renderer: re-layout and re-apply all nodes if the tree or
display size has changed since the last frame.
Internally delegates to renderer_core.update() with the full dependency bundle.

flow.ui.hit_test.brief:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Perform a point hit-test against the current element tree.
Coordinates must be in GUI space (as received from on_input action.x/y).
Returns the deepest hittable element whose layout bounds contain the point,
or nil if nothing was hit.

flow.ui.on_input.brief:
Route a Defold input action to the appropriate element.
Handles touch press/move/release, scroll wheel, and drag gestures.
Call this from gui_script on_input(); returns true if the input was consumed.

flow.ui.update_animations.brief:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Advance all per-element animations by one frame (dt seconds).
Iterates the current tree and calls each element's update_anim handler.
Requests a redraw when at least one element is still animating.
Call this every frame from gui_script update() before M.update().

flow.ui.render.brief:
Force a full layout + render pass using the given tree and dimensions.
Bypasses redraw gating — always re-computes and re-applies all nodes.
Prefer M.update() for normal frame rendering; use M.render() when you
need to guarantee an immediate re-render (e.g. after a window resize event
detected in on_input).

flow.ui.render_if_size_changed.brief:
Re-render only if the display size has changed since the last render pass.
Cheaper than M.update() — no redraw-flag check, just a size comparison.
Returns true when a re-render was performed.

dissolve_fx.brief:
A dissolve effect for sprites. Add a `noise` and a `ramp` image to the sprite's atlas
and set `dissolve_fx/materials/sprite.material` as the sprite's material, then call
`init` from the script's `init`. The noise drives the dissolve and the ramp colors its
burning edge.

dissolve_fx.find_uvrect.brief:
Finds an image in the sprite's atlas and returns its uv rect in texture space as four
values: center x, center y, width and height:
`const [x, y, w, h] = dissolve_fx.find_uvrect("#sprite", "noise")`.
Upstream asserts that `image_id` is a string, that the atlas holds the image, and that
the image is not trimmed (trim mode off, 8 uvs). With `scale_mode`, the width and
height are also divided by the size of the sprite's current animation, so the vertex
shader can map the noise from local positions.

dissolve_fx.init.brief:
Sets the sprite's `noise_uvrect` and `ramp_uvrect` from the two images in its atlas.
The sprite must use the `dissolve_fx/materials/sprite.material` material. The effect
is then driven by the sprite's `dissolve.z` property, the size of the burning edge,
and `dissolve.w`, from `0` to `1`, through `go.set` and `go.animate`:
`go.animate("#sprite", "dissolve.w", go.PLAYBACK_LOOP_PINGPONG, 1, go.EASING_LINEAR, 3)`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.brief:
Real-time shadows from one light source, the sun, and many point light sources,
wired into a render script. Call `init(self)` from the render script's `init`,
`update(self)` from its `update`, and `draw_upscaled(self)` after drawing the world
when a post effect is on (see `light_and_shadows/render/default.render_script`, the
lines marked `-- L_S Injection`). The settings fields are read every frame. Vector
fields are mutated in place; assigning a new value to any other field goes through a
cast, since a namespace import is read-only:
`(light_and_shadows as { fxaa: boolean }).fxaa = true`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.dof.brief: Turns depth of field on or off.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.rend.brief:
Returns the render target named `name`, creating it with a color buffer and, unless
`no_depth` is set, a depth texture. A target that exists at another size is resized.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.set_.brief: Sets an orthographic shadow projection, used for directional light. `init` sets one.

Sets a perspective shadow projection, cast in the direction of `sun_dir` in
`light_and_shadows.constants`. Experimental.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.init.brief:
Sets up the shadow map, the orthographic shadow projection and the render
constants on the render script. Call it from the render script's `init`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.upda.brief:
Writes the sun, the point light sources, the ambient and fog values and the camera
values from `light_and_shadows.constants` into the render constants. `update` calls it.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.rend.brief:
Draws every object tagged `shadow` into the shadow map. `update` calls it while
`shadow` is on. The render script's `self.predicates` must carry `shadow`,
`shadow_local`, `shadow_instanced`, `shadow_instanced_billboard`,
`shadow_instanced_textured`, `shadow_skinned_instanced` and `shadow_skinned`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.upda.brief:
Updates the light constants, draws the shadow map, and creates or resizes the main
and blur render targets a post effect needs. Call it from the render script's
`update`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.draw.brief:
Blurs the main render target when depth of field or blur is on, then draws it to the
screen, with FXAA when `fxaa` is on. Call it after the world is drawn to the main
render target. The render script's `self.predicates` must carry `upscale`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.shad.brief: Whether the sun casts shadows. The default is `true`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.upsc.brief:
Whether the main render target is upscaled. When on, every object is first rendered
to a render target no larger than the project settings size, which is then placed on
the screen with linear scaling. Add `light_and_shadows/props/render_target_quad.go`
to the main scene to use it. The default is `false`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.fxaa.brief: Whether FXAA anti-aliasing is applied to the final image. The default is `false`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.mix.brief: Whether depth of field is on. `dof` sets it. The default is `false`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.disc.brief: The alpha below which the sprite shader discards semitransparent pixels. The default is `0.5`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.get_.brief: Whether the reference render script reads the near and far Z planes from the camera component into `light_and_shadows.constants`. Set it to `false` to set `near_z` and `far_z` by hand. The default is `true`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.blur.brief: Whether the game scene is blurred, so an unblurred GUI can be drawn on top. It uses the same render target as upscaling. The default is `false`.
How strong the blur is, `1` to `10`. The default is `2.5`.
How much the blur render target is reduced in size, for speed. The default is `2`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.dept.brief: The shadow depth bias. Too high a bias detaches shadows from their objects; too low a bias causes shadow acne. The default is `0.0004`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.max_.brief: How many point light sources the shader processes at once, at most `16`. The default is `8`.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.rt_l.brief: Every render target `render_target` created, keyed by name.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.poly.brief: The polygon offset applied while drawing the shadow map. Raise it to reduce shadow acne; lower it if shadows detach from their casters.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.zoom.brief: The zoom `update` computed for upscaling, `1` when `upscale` is off.

light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows.DofO.brief: How strong the blur effect is, `2` to `10`. Omitted, `blur_power` keeps its value.
How wide the focus zone is, `0.1` to `4`. Omitted, `focus_range` in `light_and_shadows.constants` keeps its value.

How much the blur render target is reduced in size, for speed; `1` to `2` is enough.
`dof` copies it with no fallback, so it is required: an options table without it
leaves `blur_resolution` nil and the next `update` fails.
Whether to upscale the main render target. `dof` sets `upscale` to `false` when it is omitted.

checkpoint.brief: Checkpoint is a library for reading from and writing to files in a Defold game engine project.

checkpoint.read.brief:
Loads a saved file. A path ending in `.json` is read as text and decoded with
`json.decode`; anything else is loaded with `sys.load`. On success the loaded
value is returned alone, so the error slot is absent; on any failure — the file
missing, unreadable, or holding invalid content — the first value is `false` and
the second is the error string. Name the saved shape through the type parameter
to avoid casting at the call site.

checkpoint.write.brief:
Saves a value, creating any missing directories along the path first. A path
ending in `.json` is encoded with `json.encode` and written as text and flushed
immediately; anything else is written with `sys.save`. Creating the directories
goes through `lfs`, so the project needs `britzl/defold-lfs` as a dependency;
this corpus does not type it.

checkpoint.exists.brief:
Whether a saved file exists. Returns a real boolean rather than the underlying
file attributes, so it reads directly as a condition. Goes through `lfs`, so the
project needs `britzl/defold-lfs` as a dependency.

checkpoint.list.brief:
Every saved file, found by walking the save directory breadth-first. Directories
are descended into rather than listed. Goes through `lfs`, so the project needs
`britzl/defold-lfs` as a dependency.

checkpoint.project_title.brief:
The `project.title` from game.project, read once when the module loads. It is
the name the save directory is derived from.

checkpoint.project_save_path.brief:
The absolute path of the project's save directory, resolved once when the
module loads. Every path the other members take is relative to it, and `list`
returns paths relative to it. Ends with a separator, e.g.
`/home/klaleus/.local/share/defold-checkpoint/`.

event.brief: The Event module, used to create and manage events. Allows to subscribe to events and trigger them.

event.create.brief:
Generate a new event instance. This instance can then be used to subscribe to and trigger events.
The callback function will be called when the event is triggered. The callback_context parameter is optional
and will be passed as the first parameter to the callback function. Usually, it is used to pass the self instance.
local e = event.create()
local e = event.create(function(self) print("ok") end, self)

event.is_event.brief:
Check if the table is an event instance.
if event.is_event(my_value) then
my_value:trigger()
end

event.set_logger.brief:
Customize the logging mechanism used by Event module. You can use **Defold Log** library or provide a custom logger.
By default, the module uses the `pprint` logger for errors.

event.set_mode.brief: Set the mode of the event module.

event.subscribe.brief:
Subscribe a callback to the event or other event. The callback will be invoked whenever the event is triggered.
The callback_context parameter is optional and will be passed as the first parameter to the callback function.
If the callback with context is already subscribed, the warning will be logged.
local function callback(self)
print("clicked!")
end
on_click_event:subscribe(callback, self)

-- Subscribe an event to another event
event_1 = event.create(callback)
event_2 = event.create()
event_2:subscribe(event_1) -- Now event2 will trigger event1

event.subscribe_once.brief:
Subscribe a callback for a single trigger. After the first trigger the callback is automatically unsubscribed.
on_click_event:subscribe_once(function(self) print("one-time click!") end, self)

event.unsubscribe.brief:
Remove a previously subscribed callback from the event.
The callback_context should be the same as the one used when subscribing the callback.
If there is no callback_context provided, all callbacks with the same function will be unsubscribed.
on_click_event:unsubscribe(callback, self)

event.is_subscribed.brief:
Determine if a specific callback is currently subscribed to the event.
The callback_context should be the same as the one used when subscribing the callback.
local is_subscribed = on_click_event:is_subscribed(callback, self)

event.trigger.brief:
Trigger the event, causing all subscribed callbacks to be executed.
Any parameters passed to trigger will be forwarded to the callbacks.
The return value of the last executed callback is returned.
The event:trigger(...) can be called as event(...).
on_click_event:trigger("arg1", "arg2")

-- The event can be triggered as a function
on_click_event("arg1", "arg2")

event.is_empty.brief:
Check if the event has no subscribed callbacks.
local is_empty = on_click_event:is_empty()

event.clear.brief:
Remove all callbacks subscribed to the event, effectively resetting it.
on_click_event:clear()

event.promise.next.brief:
Attach resolve and reject handlers to the promise.
Returns a new promise that will be resolved or rejected based on the handlers' return values.
load_data():next(function(data) return process(data) end):next(display):catch(show_error)

event.promise.catch.brief:
Attach a rejection handler to the promise. Equivalent to next(nil, on_rejected).
load_data():catch(function(err) print("Failed:", err) end)

event.promise.finally.brief:
Attach a handler that is called regardless of whether the promise is resolved or rejected.
The handler is called with the resolved value or rejection reason.
When context is provided, it is passed as the first argument.
The handler return value is ignored.
load_data():finally(function() hide_loading_spinner() end)

event.promise.is_pending.brief: Check if the promise is in pending state.

event.promise.is_resolved.brief: Check if the promise is in resolved state.

event.promise.is_rejected.brief: Check if the promise is in rejected state.

event.promise.is_finished.brief: Check if the promise is finished (either resolved or rejected).

event.promise.is_cancelled.brief: Check if the shared cancel_context was cancelled.

event.promise.cancel.brief:
Cancel in-progress work in this promise chain.
A pending promise is rejected with the cancelled reason and `on_cancel` runs.
A settled promise is left as-is; pending descendants linked via `next` / `append` / adopt
are still rejected, and they trigger the shared `on_cancel`.
If nothing is still pending, this is a no-op.
my_promise:cancel()

event.promise.append.brief:
Append a task to this promise's internal sequence without reassigning.
The task may return a value or a promise. If `task` is a promise, the pipeline waits for it
to finish and adopts its result. The incoming value is not forwarded into `task`
(same as `append(function() return task end)`).
Returns self for chaining.
Almost similar to `promise = promise:next(task)`, but without reassigning the promise.
pipeline:append(step1)
pipeline:append(step2)
pipeline:append(step3)
local last = pipeline:tail()
print("Is going to check status of", last:is_pending())

event.promise.tail.brief:
Get the current tail promise representing all appended work.
local last = pipeline:tail()
last:next(on_complete)

event.promise.reset.brief:
Reset the internal sequence to an already resolved promise.
pipeline:reset()
pipeline:append(new_step)

event.promise._reject_cancel_children.brief: Reject pending child promises when a settled promise is cancelled.

event.promise.state.brief: Current state of the promise (pending, resolved, rejected)

event.promise.value.brief: The resolved value or rejection reason

event.promise.on_cancel.brief: Event for cancellation cleanup subscriptions (shared across the promise chain)

event.queue.push.brief:
Push a new event to the queue. The event will exist until it's handled by a subscriber.
If there are already subscribers for this queue instance, they will be called immediately.
If multiple subscribers handle the event, all subscribers will still be called. The on_handle callback
will be called for each subscriber that handles the event.
my_queue:push(save_data)
my_queue:push(save_data, function() print("saved!") end)

event.queue.subscribe.brief:
Subscribe a handler to this queue instance. When an event is pushed to this queue,
the handler will be called. If there are already events in the queue, they will be processed immediately.
Return a non-nil value from the handler to mark the event as handled and remove it from the queue.
local function on_save(self, data)
do_save(data)
return true
end
my_queue:subscribe(on_save, self)

event.queue.subscribe_once.brief:
Subscribe a handler until it handles one event. The handler is invoked for each event in the queue until it returns non-nil (handles an event)
then it is automatically unsubscribed and will not be invoked again, even if more events remain in the queue.
my_queue:subscribe_once(function(self, data) return process(data) end, self)

event.queue.unsubscribe.brief:
Unsubscribe a handler from this queue instance.
my_queue:unsubscribe(on_save, self)

event.queue.is_subscribed.brief:
Check if a handler is subscribed to this queue instance.
local ok = my_queue:is_subscribed(on_save, self)

event.queue.process.brief:
Process all events in this queue immediately. Subscribers will not be called in this function.
Events can be handled and removed in event handler callback. If event is handled, it will be removed from the queue.
my_queue:process(function(self, data) return handle(data) end, self)

event.queue.process_next.brief:
Process exactly one queued event with a specific handler (subscribers will NOT be called).
If the handler returns non-nil the event will be removed from the queue.
local handled = my_queue:process_next(function(data) return handle(data) end)

event.queue.get_events.brief:
Get all pending events in this queue.
for _, event_data in ipairs(my_queue:get_events()) do
print(event_data.data)
end

event.queue.clear_events.brief:
Clear all pending events in this queue.
my_queue:clear_events()

event.queue.clear_subscribers.brief:
Clear all subscribers from this queue instance.
my_queue:clear_subscribers()

event.queue.is_empty.brief:
Check if this queue has no pending events.
if my_queue:is_empty() then
return
end

event.queue.has_subscribers.brief:
Check if this queue instance has no subscribed handlers.
if my_queue:has_subscribers() then
my_queue:push(data)
end

event.queue.clear.brief:
Remove all events and handlers from this queue instance, effectively resetting it.
my_queue:clear()

pigeon.brief: Easily and safely manage posting messages in Defold.

pigeon.define.brief:
------------------------
------------------------
------------------------
------------------------
Define a single message schema for runtime validation.
Built-in Defold/system message ids are always protected from redefinition.

pigeon.define_batch.brief:
Define multiple message schemas at once from a table of letter definitions.
Built-in Defold/system message ids are always protected from redefinition.

pigeon.subscribe.brief:
Subscribe to given message_id(s) and optionally add a hook called immediately on send.
Hook runs synchronously in the sender context (inside Pigeon.send) before msg.post,
and does not run in the receiver script.

pigeon.extend_subscription.brief: Add message subscriptions to an existing subscriber id.

pigeon.reduce_subscription.brief: Remove message subscriptions from an existing subscriber id.

pigeon.send.brief:
Send a message of given message_id with given message table to all subscribed subscribers.
Additionally, Pigeon checks in runtime if message is correct if defined.
If the message has a hook attached, it will be called immediately.

pigeon.send_to.brief:
Equivalent to Defold built-in `msg.post`. Sends a message of given message_id with an optional data in message table to a specified url.
Accepts the same target forms as `msg.post`: a `url` userdata, a url-like
`string` (e.g. "/gui#hud" or "#fragment"), or a `hash` game object id
(e.g. the id returned by `factory.create` or `go.get_id`).
Additionally, Pigeon checks in runtime if message is correct if defined.

pigeon.toggle_logging.brief:
Enable or disable logging functionality.
It only switches between default logging (printing to console) and not logging.
If you want to use dependency logging, you need to set dependency again after enabling logging.
The correctness of arguments is not checked! Use responsibly!

pigeon.set_dependency_module_log.brief:
Replace internal printing with logging from Log module.
It is suited for Log API, so if you want to provide your own module, follow the API,
or modify internal Pigeon calls for logging accordingly.
The correctness of arguments is not checked! Use responsibly!

light_and_shadows.constants.brief:
The light options the render script forwards into shader uniform constants. Scripts
such as `light_setting.script` and `sun.script` write them, and `light.update` and
the render script read them every frame. Vector fields are mutated in place
(`constants.fog.x = 20`); assigning a new value to a field goes through a cast, since
a namespace import is read-only.

light_and_shadows.constants.clear_color.brief: The color that clears the default render target, which is the background color. RGB in `0`..`1`.

light_and_shadows.constants.fog.brief: The minimum and maximum Z in camera view space between which the fog starts and ends, in `x` and `y`.

light_and_shadows.constants.ambient.brief: The ambient color, added after every light source is blended. `w` is the maximum value of each final color component.

light_and_shadows.constants.fog_color.brief: The fog color, usually the clear color. `w` is the fog density from `0` to `1`, where `0` is the densest.

light_and_shadows.constants.lights.brief:
The light sources, their world positions and colors. Only the first
`light_and_shadows.max_lights` reach the shader; missing ones are sent as zero
vectors.

light_and_shadows.constants.cam_position.brief: The camera world position, which the shader uses for specular light. `light.update` copies it from `light.cam_position`.

light_and_shadows.constants.cam_look_at_.brief: The point the camera looks at, the center of the shadow projection. `light.update` copies it from `light.cam_look_at`.

light_and_shadows.constants.sun_position.brief: The sun position, the one light source that casts shadows.

light_and_shadows.constants.sun_dir.brief: The sun direction, used for shadow casting with a perspective projection.

light_and_shadows.constants.shadow_color.brief: The inverted shadow color, subtracted where shadows fall. `light_and_shadows.update` sets `w` to `1` when `light_and_shadows.shadow` is on and `0` when it is off.

light_and_shadows.constants.cam_z.brief: The camera Z coordinate, the distance from the focus point. `light.update` copies it from `light.cam_z`.

light_and_shadows.constants.focus_range.brief: How wide the depth-of-field focus zone is. `light_and_shadows.dof` sets it from `focus_range`.

light_and_shadows.constants.near_z.brief: The camera near Z plane. The reference render script reads it from the camera while `light_and_shadows.get_far_near_z_from_camera` is `true`.

light_and_shadows.constants.far_z.brief: The camera far Z plane. The reference render script reads it from the camera while `light_and_shadows.get_far_near_z_from_camera` is `true`.

light_and_shadows.constants.LightEntry.p.brief: The world position. `w` carries the spotlight smoothness.

light_and_shadows.constants.LightEntry.c.brief: The color. `w` is the power after distance attenuation.

light_and_shadows.constants.LightEntry.d.brief: The spotlight direction; `w` above `0` turns the spotlight on. `light_and_shadows.update` sends a zero vector when it is absent.
The squared distance from the point the camera looks at.

flow.layout.brief: Flow's flexbox layout pass, which computes the position and size of every element in a tree.

flow.layout.compute.brief:
Compute layout for a node tree. Writes layout.x/y/w/h to every node
in the tree recursively, using bottom-left origin coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Measure all regular (non-overlay) children to sum fixed sizes and flex_grow weights.
2. Distribute remaining free space according to justify_content.
3. Place each child along the main axis, applying align_items / align_self on the cross axis.
4. Recurse into each child.
5. Layout overlay children (popup, bottom_sheet) at full parent bounds as a final pass.

pointer_lock.brief:
Mouse lock state and a virtual in-game cursor. Add `pointer_lock/pointer_lock.script`
to the bootstrap collection: it locks the cursor on a click and unlocks it on
`key_esc`, and keeps `locked` current. The cursor fields are plain module fields;
assigning one goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only:
`(pointer as { cursor_visible: boolean }).cursor_visible = true`.

pointer_lock.transform_input.brief:
Converts `on_input` arguments into the virtual in-game cursor system: sets
`action.x` and `action.y` to the cursor position, on the same table it returns, and
returns `undefined` as the action id unless the pointer is locked and the cursor is
visible. Call it first in `on_input`:
`[action_id, action] = pointer.transform_input(action_id, action)`.

pointer_lock.update_cursor_position.brief:
Moves the virtual cursor by the action's `dx` and `dy`, clamped to the display
size. Pass it a pointer-movement action, which carries both.

pointer_lock.update_lock_state.brief: Copies the window's mouse lock state into `locked`.

pointer_lock.DISPLAY_WIDTH.brief: The `display.width` project setting, read once when the module loads.

pointer_lock.DISPLAY_HEIGHT.brief: The `display.height` project setting, read once when the module loads.

pointer_lock.locked.brief:
Whether the pointer is locked. Read-only for a project: `pointer_lock.script` sets
it, and `update_lock_state` copies the window's mouse lock into it. Starts `false`.

pointer_lock.cursor_x.brief:
The X position of the virtual in-game cursor, between `0` and `DISPLAY_WIDTH`.
Starts at the middle of the display; `update_cursor_position` moves it.

pointer_lock.cursor_y.brief:
The Y position of the virtual in-game cursor, between `0` and `DISPLAY_HEIGHT`.
Starts at the middle of the display; `update_cursor_position` moves it.

pointer_lock.cursor_visible.brief:
Whether the virtual in-game cursor is shown. Starts `false`. `transform_input`
passes the action id through only while the pointer is locked and this is `true`.

pointer_lock.cursor_render_order.brief: The GUI render order of the virtual cursor, `15` being the top. Starts at `15`.

Sent to a screen's transition url when this screen is being popped and
should transition back out.

monarch.monarch.FOCUS_GAINED.brief: Sent to a screen's focus url when the screen gains focus.

monarch.monarch.FOCUS_LOST.brief: Sent to a screen's focus url when the screen loses focus.

monarch.monarch.SCREEN_TRANSITION_IN_STA.brief:
Sent to every url registered with `add_listener` when a screen begins
transitioning in, carrying `screen` and `previous_screen` ids.

monarch.monarch.register.brief:
Alias of {@link register_proxy}, kept for the pre-factory API.
Typed through the function it aliases so the two cannot drift apart.

ads_wrapper.platform.brief: Platform constants and a check for the running platform, for Ads Wrapper network settings.

ads_wrapper.platform.is_same.brief: Check if the platform is correct

ads_wrapper.platform.PL_ANDROID.brief: Android, as returned by `get` and checked by `is_same`.

ads_wrapper.platform.PL_IOS.brief: iOS, as returned by `get` and checked by `is_same`.

ads_wrapper.platform.PL_HTML5.brief: HTML5, as returned by `get` and checked by `is_same`.

ads_wrapper.platform.PL_OTHER.brief: Any other platform, as returned by `get` and checked by `is_same`.

ads_wrapper.platform.ads_network.is_supp.brief: Check if the environment supports admob api

ads_wrapper.platform.ads_network.is_init.brief: Check if the admob is initialized

ads_wrapper.platform.ads_network.is_rewa.brief: Check if the rewarded ads is loaded

ads_wrapper.platform.ads_network.is_inte.brief: Check if the interstitial ads is loaded
