platypus.create.brief:
Create a platypus instance.
This will provide all the functionality to control a game object in a
platformer game. The functions will operate on the game object attached
to the script calling the functions.

platypus.SEPARATION_SHAPES.brief:
Value for `collisions.separation` selecting shape separation. Platypus warns
at runtime that this mode is no longer supported and only raycast separation
is; the constant still exists.

wrap.node_list.brief:
Wraps several GUI nodes at once. `new` takes node ids, or names paired with ids or
nodes, and returns a table holding one `wrap.node` wrapper per name, optionally looking
each id up in a cloned tree first.

wrap.node_list.new.brief:
Wraps each node, keyed by its name. A Lua table mixing ids and named entries has no
TypeScript literal, so name every entry, an id under its own name.

sprite_repeat.brief: Sprite texture repeat (tiling) shader helper: reads a sprite's atlas animation and drives the repeat material's constants.

sprite_repeat.create.brief:
Reads an atlas animation's frames for a sprite that uses the repeat material,
and returns a handle that applies them. Apply the repeat material to the sprite
first, and disable sprite trim mode for the atlas images: every frame must have
exactly 8 UV values, or this asserts. Walks the atlas animation's frame list,
so it needs Defold 1.12.3 or later.

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.anim.brief:
Applies the first frame and the repeat factors to the sprite. When the
animation has more than one frame and a non-zero `fps`, starts a repeating
timer that steps through the frames.

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.stop.brief: Cancels the playback timer, if one is running.

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.fram.brief: Every frame of the animation, in playback order.

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.widt.brief: The animation's width, from the atlas.

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.heig.brief: The animation's height, from the atlas.

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.fps.brief: The animation's playback rate, from the atlas.

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.curr.brief: The 1-based index of the frame shown next. **⚠️ 1-based; passed to `sprite_repeat` unchanged.**

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.v.brief: The `uv_repeat` value: `x`/`y` the repeat factors, `z`/`w` the current frame's size.

sprite_repeat.SpriteRepeatAnimation.hand.brief: The `timer.delay` handle driving playback. Present only while a multi-frame animation plays.

sprite_repeat.RepeatFrame.uv_coord.brief: The frame's UV rectangle in the texture: `x`/`y` one corner, `z`/`w` the other.

sprite_repeat.RepeatFrame.w.brief: The frame's width in texture pixels.

sprite_repeat.RepeatFrame.h.brief: The frame's height in texture pixels.

sprite_repeat.RepeatFrame.uv_rotated.brief: `(0, 1, 0, 0)` when the atlas stores the frame rotated clockwise, else `(1, 0, 0, 0)`.

gamepush.core.events.brief: GamePush events: list them, join one and check whether it is active, with their events.

gamepush.core.events.join.brief: Joins an event. Raises when the table is missing.

gamepush.core.events.active_list.brief: The events the player is taking part in.

gamepush.core.events.is_joined.brief: Whether the player is taking part in an event.

wrap.go.brief:
A chainable wrapper around a game object. `new` stores a url, and each method calls the
`go.*` function of the same name with that url: setters return the wrapper, so calls
chain, and getters return what the engine does.

wrap.go.Go.get.brief: Returns a property of the game object, from `go.get`.

wrap.go.Go.set.brief: Sets a property of the game object with `go.set`.

wrap.go.Go.post.brief: Posts a message to the game object with `msg.post`.

wrap.go.Go.get_id.brief:
Returns the game object's id, from `go.get_id`. `go.get_id` takes a path string, so
call it only on a wrapper built from one.

wrap.go.Go.delete.brief:
Deletes the game object with `go.delete`. At `1.1.0` the deletion is always
recursive: upstream reads `recursive or true`, so `false` still deletes the children.

wrap.go.Go.animate.brief:
Animates several properties with `go.animate`, each to the value at the same index
of `to`, all with the same playback, easing, duration and delay.

wrap.go.Go.cancel_animations.brief: Cancels the game object's animations with `go.cancel_animations`.

wrap.go.Go.set_position.brief: Sets the game object's position with `go.set_position`.

wrap.go.Go.get_position.brief: Returns the game object's position, from `go.get_position`.

wrap.go.Go.add_position.brief:
Meant to add to each component of the position. At `1.1.0` it adds to a copy of the
position and leaves the game object unchanged; `add_position_x`, `add_position_y`
and `add_position_z` write the result.

wrap.go.Go.get_position_x.brief: Returns the x component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.get_position_y.brief: Returns the y component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.get_position_z.brief: Returns the z component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.set_position_x.brief: Sets the x component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.set_position_y.brief: Sets the y component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.set_position_z.brief: Sets the z component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.add_position_x.brief: Adds to the x component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.add_position_y.brief: Adds to the y component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.add_position_z.brief: Adds to the z component of the game object's position.

wrap.go.Go.get_rotation.brief: Returns the game object's rotation, from `go.get_rotation`.

wrap.go.Go.set_rotation.brief: Sets the game object's rotation with `go.set_rotation`.

wrap.go.Go.add_rotation.brief:
Meant to add to the x, y and z components of the rotation quaternion. At `1.1.0` it
adds to a copy of the rotation and leaves the game object unchanged.

wrap.go.Go.get_rotation_x.brief: Returns the x component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle.

wrap.go.Go.get_rotation_y.brief: Returns the y component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle.

wrap.go.Go.get_rotation_z.brief: Returns the z component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle.

wrap.go.Go.set_rotation_x.brief:
Sets the x component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle, and leaves the
other components as they are.

wrap.go.Go.set_rotation_y.brief:
Sets the y component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle, and leaves the
other components as they are.

wrap.go.Go.set_rotation_z.brief:
Sets the z component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle, and leaves the
other components as they are.

wrap.go.Go.add_rotation_x.brief: Adds to the x component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle.

wrap.go.Go.add_rotation_y.brief: Adds to the y component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle.

wrap.go.Go.add_rotation_z.brief: Adds to the z component of the rotation quaternion, not an Euler angle.

wrap.go.Go.get_scale.brief: Returns the game object's scale, from `go.get_scale`.

wrap.go.Go.set_scale.brief: Sets the game object's scale with `go.set_scale`.

wrap.go.Go.add_scale.brief:
Meant to add to each component of the scale. At `1.1.0` it adds to a copy of the
scale and leaves the game object unchanged; `add_scale_x`, `add_scale_y` and
`add_scale_z` write the result.

wrap.go.Go.get_scale_x.brief: Returns the x component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.get_scale_y.brief: Returns the y component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.get_scale_z.brief: Returns the z component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.set_scale_x.brief: Sets the x component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.set_scale_y.brief: Sets the y component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.set_scale_z.brief: Sets the z component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.add_scale_x.brief: Adds to the x component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.add_scale_y.brief: Adds to the y component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.add_scale_z.brief: Adds to the z component of the game object's scale.

wrap.go.Go.get_parent.brief: Returns the id of the game object's parent, from `go.get_parent`.

wrap.go.Go.set_parent.brief: Sets the game object's parent with `go.set_parent`.

wrap.go.Go.get_scale_uniform.brief: Returns the game object's uniform scale, from `go.get_scale_uniform`.

wrap.go.Go.get_world_position.brief: Returns the game object's world position, from `go.get_world_position`.

wrap.go.Go.get_world_rotation.brief: Returns the game object's world rotation, from `go.get_world_rotation`.

wrap.go.Go.get_world_scale.brief: Returns the game object's world scale, from `go.get_world_scale`.

wrap.go.Go.get_world_scale_uniform.brief: Returns the game object's uniform world scale, from `go.get_world_scale_uniform`.

wrap.go.Go.get_world_transform.brief: Returns the game object's world transform, from `go.get_world_transform`.

wrap.go.Go.url.brief: The game object's url, passed to every `go.*` call.

bridge.brief: Functions and constants for interacting with bridge

bridge.platform.id.brief: Identify the platform on which the game is currently running to customize features and settings accordingly.

bridge.platform.tld.brief: Retrieve the top-level domain of the platform to handle domain-specific configurations and behavior.

bridge.platform.language.brief: Get the language set by the user on the platform or the browser language if not provided by the platform, to localize game content.

bridge.platform.payload.brief: Embed auxiliary information into the game URL to pass additional data or settings when launching the game.

bridge.platform.launch_source.brief: Where the game was opened from - "notification" or "post" (one of the game's own posts, see bridge.social.create_post). nil when the platform did not say.

bridge.platform.data.brief: Everything the launch carries - the parameters the platform passed to the game and, when it was opened from one of the game's own posts, postId - the id of that post's config entry.

bridge.platform.send_message.brief: Send predefined messages to the platform to trigger specific actions or events, such as signaling that the game is ready.

bridge.platform.send_custom_message.brief: Send a custom message with an arbitrary id to the platform.

bridge.platform.is_audio_enabled.brief: Check if the audio is enabled on the platform.

bridge.platform.is_external_calls_suppor.brief: Check if external calls are supported on the platform.

bridge.platform.is_external_links_allowe.brief: Check if external links are allowed on the platform.

bridge.cross_promo.get_games.brief: Get the cross-promo games list. Resolves to an empty array when unsupported. Each game has the shape { id, name, url, icon_url, cover_url, payload }.

bridge.cross_promo.show.brief: Show the built-in cross-promo HTML overlay.

bridge.cross_promo.hide.brief: Hide the built-in cross-promo HTML overlay.

bridge.cross_promo.is_visible.brief: Check whether the cross-promo overlay is currently shown.

bridge.storage.get.brief: Retrieve stored data based on a key or multiple keys to restore player progress or settings.

bridge.storage.set.brief: Save data to the storage with a key to retain player progress or settings.

bridge.storage.delete.brief: Remove data from the storage by key to manage player data and settings effectively.

bridge.advertisement.show_banner.brief: Display a banner ad within your game to generate revenue through advertising.

bridge.advertisement.hide_banner.brief: Hide the currently displayed banner ad when it is no longer needed.

bridge.advertisement.banner_state.brief: Hide the currently displayed banner ad when it is no longer needed.

bridge.advertisement.is_banner_supported.brief: Check if the platform supports displaying banner ads. Use this to determine if you can include banner advertisements in your game.

bridge.advertisement.is_interstitial_sup.brief: Check if the platform supports displaying interstitial ads. Use this to determine if you can include interstitial advertisements in your game.

bridge.advertisement.is_rewarded_support.brief: Check if the platform supports displaying rewarded ads. Use this to determine if you can include rewarded advertisements in your game.

bridge.advertisement.show_interstitial.brief: Display an interstitial ad at appropriate moments, such as during level transitions or game over screens.

bridge.advertisement.interstitial_state.brief: Track the state of the interstitial ad to manage ad display and user experience.

bridge.advertisement.minimum_delay_betwe.brief: Minimum time interval between interstitial ad displays to comply with platform requirements and improve user experience.

bridge.advertisement.set_minimum_delay_b.brief: Set the minimum time interval between interstitial ad displays to comply with platform requirements and improve user experience.

bridge.advertisement.rewarded_state.brief: Monitor the state of the rewarded ad (loading, opened, closed, rewarded, failed) to manage the reward process.

bridge.advertisement.rewarded_placement.brief: Monitor the placement of the rewarded ad to manage the reward process.

bridge.advertisement.show_rewarded.brief: Display a rewarded ad and provide incentives to players for watching the entire ad.

bridge.advertisement.is_advanced_banners.brief: Check if the platform supports displaying advanced banner ads.

bridge.advertisement.advanced_banners_st.brief: Track the state of the advanced banners to manage ad display and user experience.

bridge.advertisement.show_advanced_banne.brief: Display advanced banners at appropriate moments of the game.

bridge.advertisement.hide_advanced_banne.brief: Hide the currently displayed advanced banners when they are no longer needed.

bridge.advertisement.check_ad_block.brief: Check if the ad blocker is enabled.

bridge.device.type.brief: Determine the type of device (mobile, tablet, desktop, tv) the game is being played on to adjust the game`s interface and performance settings.

bridge.player.is_authorization_supported.brief: Check if the platform supports player authorization to enable features that require user authentication, such as saving game progress or accessing social features.

bridge.player.is_authorized.brief: Verify if the player is currently authorized on the platform. This allows you to enable personalized features, such as saving high scores or providing user-specific content.

bridge.player.is_guest.brief: Check if the player is unauthorized or running as a guest.

bridge.player.id.brief: Get the player’s unique ID on the platform to manage user-specific data and settings. Use this ID to track player progress, achievements, and purchases.

bridge.player.name.brief: Retrieve the player's name to personalize the game experience. Display the name in leaderboards, friend lists, or when sending notifications and messages.

bridge.player.extra.brief: Get the extra information about player.

bridge.player.photos.brief: Get the count of player avatars available. Use this to manage and display user profile images effectively, such as showing the avatar in multiplayer lobbies or profile screens.

bridge.player.authorize.brief: Authorize the player on the platform to access protected features and personalize the game experience. For example, prompting the player to log in to save their progress or unlock social sharing features.

bridge.social.is_share_supported.brief: Check if the share functionality is supported on the platform.

bridge.social.share.brief: Use this to allow players to share game content or achievements on social media platforms.

bridge.social.is_join_community_supporte.brief: Check if the join community functionality is supported on the platform.

bridge.social.join_community.brief: Invite players to join your community. The data is taken from social.joinCommunity in playgama-bridge-config.json.

bridge.social.is_invite_friends_supporte.brief: Check if the invite friends functionality is supported on the platform.

bridge.social.invite_friends.brief: Allow players to invite their friends to play the game, helping to grow your player base organically.

bridge.social.is_create_post_supported.brief: Check if the create post functionality is supported on the platform.

bridge.social.create_post.brief: Use this to let players create posts about their achievements or updates directly from the game.

bridge.social.is_add_to_favorites_suppor.brief: Check if the add to favorites functionality is supported on the platform.

bridge.social.add_to_favorites.brief: Allow players to bookmark your game for easy access in the future.

bridge.social.is_add_to_home_screen_supp.brief: Check if the add to home screen functionality is supported on the platform.

bridge.social.add_to_home_screen.brief: Enable players to add a shortcut to your game on their home screen for quick access.

bridge.social.is_rate_supported.brief: Check if the rate game functionality is supported on the platform.

bridge.social.rate.brief: Encourage players to rate your game, providing valuable feedback and improving visibility.

bridge.social.is_post_reward_supported.brief: Check if rewards around posts created with create_post are supported on the platform.

bridge.social.get_post_reward.brief: Everything the player has coming from posts right now - the reward for the post the game was opened from and what the author earned from the players who came through their posts. Resolves to an empty array when there is nothing, so grant what you get and stay quiet otherwise. Each reward has the shape { id, amount, type }, where type is "visit" or "author".

bridge.payments.is_supported.brief: Check if in-game purchases are supported to offer items or upgrades within the game.

bridge.payments.purchase.brief: Allow players to buy items or upgrades in your game to enhance their gameplay experience.

bridge.payments.consume_purchase.brief: Consume purchased items, such as in-game currency, once they are used, to manage inventory and player progression.

bridge.payments.get_catalog.brief: Retrieve a list of all available in-game items that players can purchase to display in the game store.

bridge.payments.get_purchases.brief: Retrieve a list of items that the player has purchased to manage their inventory and provide access to purchased content.

bridge.achievements.get_achievements.brief: Returns the achievement list in JSON.

bridge.daily_rewards.get_rewards.brief: Returns the configured ordered list of reward ids as a JSON string.

bridge.daily_rewards.get_current_day.brief: Returns the 0-based index of the reward the player is currently on.

bridge.daily_rewards.get_current_reward.brief: Returns the id of the reward claimable today, or nil when nothing can be claimed.

bridge.daily_rewards.claim_current_rewar.brief: Claims the reward available today. Calls on_success when claimed, on_failure otherwise.

bridge.tasks.get_tasks.brief: Returns every active task across all groups, with live progress, as a JSON string.

bridge.tasks.add_progress.brief: Advances every active target whose id equals the given metric, clamped to the target amount.

bridge.tasks.claim_reward.brief: Claims a completed task's rewards. Calls on_success with true when claimed, false otherwise.

bridge.leaderboards.type.brief: Check the leaderboards type on the platform.

bridge.leaderboards.set_score.brief: Submit the player's score to the leaderboard to update their rank and position.

bridge.leaderboards.get_entries.brief: Retrieve entries from the leaderboard, including the player's rank and score, to display a comprehensive leaderboard.

bridge.remote_config.is_supported.brief: Check if remote configuration is supported to manage game settings without releasing updates.

bridge.remote_config.set_context.brief: Set dynamic game/player parameters used for config segmentation. Accumulates across calls; only used by platforms that support it.

bridge.remote_config.get.brief: Encourage players to rate your game, providing valuable feedback and improving visibility.

bridge.notifications.is_supported.brief: Check if scheduling notifications is supported on the current platform.

bridge.notifications.schedule.brief: Schedule a notification. The notification table has the shape { id, title, description, delaySeconds, image, callToAction, payload }, where id is mapped to the platform value in the config file. The payload of the notification the game was launched from is available via bridge.platform.payload().

bridge.notifications.cancel.brief: Cancel a previously scheduled notification with the given id.

bridge.notifications.cancel_all.brief: Cancel every notification scheduled by the game.

bridge.analytics.send.brief: Send a game event. The event name and the data are entirely up to the game — they are never matched against the SDK's own event names.

bridge.multiplayer.on.brief: Subscribe to multiplayer events. Use the bridge.EVENT_NAME.MULTIPLAYER_* constants. The callback receives: `multiplayer_state_changed` - state string (see bridge.MULTIPLAYER_STATE) `multiplayer_room_left` - reason string (see bridge.ROOM_LEAVE_REASON) `multiplayer_room_updated` - room table `multiplayer_player_joined` - player table `multiplayer_player_left` - player table `multiplayer_player_updated` - player table `multiplayer_host_changed` - new host player table or nil `multiplayer_message_received` - message table { type, data, from } `multiplayer_sync_state_received` - world table (see set_sync_state)

bridge.multiplayer.is_supported.brief: Check if multiplayer is supported on the current platform.

bridge.multiplayer.is_in_room.brief: Check if the player is in a room (connected or reconnecting).

bridge.multiplayer.is_host.brief: Check if the local player is the room host.

bridge.multiplayer.player_id.brief: The local player id in the room, nil outside of a room.

bridge.multiplayer.host_id.brief: The room host player id, nil outside of a room.

bridge.multiplayer.room_id.brief: The room code other players type to join, nil outside of a room.

bridge.multiplayer.room.brief: The current room with the shape { id, type, maxPlayers, isOpen, isVisible, hostId, properties }, nil outside of a room.

bridge.multiplayer.players.brief: The players in the current room, each with the shape { id, name, isHost, isConnected, properties }. Empty outside of a room.

bridge.multiplayer.is_invite_supported.brief: Check if the platform can share an invite link to the current room, see invite_to_room.

bridge.multiplayer.launch_room_id.brief: The room code from the invite link the game was opened with, pass it to join_room. nil when there is none or once the player has entered any room.

bridge.multiplayer.sync_state.brief: The last world - set with set_sync_state or received. Empty when there is none.

bridge.multiplayer.create_room.brief: Create a room and enter it as the host. A hidden room (the default) is for friends - only players the room code was shared with can join.

bridge.multiplayer.join_room.brief: Join a room by its code.

bridge.multiplayer.join_or_create_room.brief: Quick match - enter a visible room with the same maxPlayers and exactly the same filter, or create a visible one (its creator becomes the host). A created room also gets the filter values in its properties.

bridge.multiplayer.get_rooms.brief: Get visible open rooms with a free seat, for a room browser. Each room has the shape { id, type, maxPlayers, playerCount, filter, properties }.

bridge.multiplayer.invite_to_room.brief: Ask the platform to share a link to the current room. Whoever opens it starts the game with the room code in launch_room_id.

bridge.multiplayer.set_room_open.brief: Host only. Stop (or resume) accepting new players, e.g. once the match starts.

bridge.multiplayer.set_room_visible.brief: Host only. Show (or hide) the room in the room list and matchmaking.

bridge.multiplayer.set_room_properties.brief: Host only. Update the room properties - keys are merged, a json.null value removes the key.

bridge.multiplayer.set_player_properties.brief: Update the local player properties - keys are merged, a json.null value removes the key.

bridge.multiplayer.send.brief: Send a message to other players in the room. It arrives in the multiplayer_message_received event as { type, data, from }.

bridge.multiplayer.set_sync_state.brief: Set the local game world. When the room is entered with syncState, the host sends its world to the other players up to updatesPerSecond times a second (1-10, default 10) and they get it in the multiplayer_sync_state_received event. The server keeps the last world - a new host gets it in the same event and goes on from it. Works outside a room too, e.g. to set the starting world before create_room. Reset to an empty table when the room is left.

asobi.api.economy.brief: asobi wallets and the store over REST. A project reaches it as `client.economy`.

asobi.api.economy.get_history.brief: Fetches the transactions of one wallet.

asobi.api.economy.purchase.brief: Buys a store listing with the signed-in player's wallet.

monarch.transitions.easings.brief: Screen manager for Defold with stacked, modal, and transition-aware navigation flows.

orthographic.camera.brief: Orthographic camera functionality for the Defold game engine

orthographic.camera.follow.brief: Follow one or more game objects. When following multiple objects the camera will follow the center point between the objects.

orthographic.camera.get_zoom.brief: Get the current zoom level of the camera.

orthographic.camera.set_zoom.brief: Change the zoom level of the camera.

orthographic.camera.get_automatic_zoom.brief: Get if the camera is configured to use automatic zoom level.

orthographic.camera.set_automatic_zoom.brief: Set if the camera should use automatic zoom level.

orthographic.camera.screen_to_world.brief: Translate screen coordinates to world coordinates, based on the view and projection of the camera.

orthographic.camera.window_to_world.brief: Translate window coordinates to world coordinates, based on the view and projection of the camera.

orthographic.camera.get_display_size.brief: Get the display size (ie from game.project).

orthographic.camera.get_view.brief: Get the current view of the camera.

orthographic.camera.get_viewport.brief: Get the current viewport of the camera.

orthographic.camera.get_projection.brief: Get the current projection of the camera.

orthographic.camera.recoil.brief: Apply a recoil effect to the camera. The recoil will decay using linear interpolation.

orthographic.camera.get_offset.brief: Get the current offset of the camera (caused by shake or recoil)

orthographic.camera.deadzone.brief: If following a game object this will add a deadzone around the camera position where the camera position will not update. If the target moves to the edge of the deadzone the camera will start to follow until the target returns within the bounds of the deadzone.

orthographic.camera.bounds.brief: Limits the camera position to within the specified rectangle.

orthographic.camera.screen_to_world_boun.brief: Translate screen boundaries (corners) to world coordinates, based on the view and projection of the camera.

orthographic.camera.world_to_screen.brief: Translate world coordinates to screen coordinates, based on the view and projection of the camera. This is useful when manually culling game objects and you need to determine if a world coordinate will be visible or not. It can also be used to position gui nodes on top of game objects.

orthographic.camera.unproject.brief: Translate screen coordinates to world coordinates using the specified view and projection.

orthographic.camera.project.brief: Translate world coordinates to screen coordinates using the specified view and projection.

orthographic.camera.set_window_scaling_f.brief: Set window scaling factor (basically retina or no retina screen). There is no built-in way to detect if Defold is running on a retina or non retina screen. This information combined with the High DPI setting in game.project can be used to ensure that the zoom behaves the same way regardless of screen type and High DPI setting. You can use an extension such as DefOS to get the window scaling factor.

live_unbundler.brief: Live Update helper for splitting large archives into smaller dependency-aware chunks, and downloading and mounting them at runtime.

live_unbundler.set_log_function.brief:
Assign a project logger. Signature: function(level, message), where level is

live_unbundler.get_modules_download_prog.brief:
Byte-based progress for a module or a set of modules, with a per-resolution
breakdown in the low/high fields. Shared dependency archives are counted once
per set; an archive identical in both manifests counts toward the resolution
counted first (for RES_BOTH that is lowres — the pass that actually downloads
it). Anchored to the download queue: an archive counts as downloaded when
nothing for it is pending, so the result reaches 100 exactly when the set's
downloads drain. For by_request modules that were not requested yet, the
future queue content is predicted from the same rules enqueue_modules uses;
that prediction can dip for a moment while a shared archive is remounted to
its highres copy, it recovers on the next mount.

live_unbundler.get_download_progress.brief:
Byte-based progress of the current download session, with a per-resolution
breakdown in the low/high fields (requires manifest with file_sizes).

water.brief:
A stylized water shader: animated wave surfaces, foam, sparkles, refraction and
reflection, set through shader constants. A game object script calls `init` once with
the camera, sun and water objects, then `update(dt)` and `update_camera()` every frame.
The render script calls `render_init(self)` at the end of its `init`, after which
`self.predicates` holds the `water` predicate, and
`render_update(self, state, self.predicates, draw_options_world)` in its `update` (see
`water/render/water.render_script`). The shader needs `exclude_gles_sm100 = 1` under
`[shader]` in `game.project`. Every setter writes a shader constant the next
`render_update` uploads, and every getter returns the stored values as separate
values.

water.init.brief:
Stores the camera, sun and water objects and the time speed, then reads the camera
position and near and far planes and the sun direction once. Call it from a game
object script's `init`.

water.render_init.brief:
Adds the `water` predicate to `self.predicates`, creates the scene render target at
`self.state.width` by `self.state.height` with a color and a depth buffer, and
creates the two constant buffers `render_update` draws with, all stored on `self`.
Call it at the end of the render script's `init`, once `self.predicates` and
`self.state` are set. Afterwards `self.predicates` types as `Predicates`, which
`render_update` takes. From a `defineRenderScript` `init`, call it on the state `init`
returns, which is merged onto `self`.

water.render_update.brief:
Draws the `model` predicate into the scene render target, then draws `model` and the
water to the default render target, sampling the scene's depth and color for edge
foam and refraction. It needs `render_init` to have run on the same `self`, and
raises otherwise. Call it from the render script's `update` after the world view and
projection are set.

water.update_sun.brief:
Re-reads the sun position, which moves the light and recomputes the sun direction
from the water object, replacing any direction `set_sun_direction` wrote.

water.update_camera.brief: Re-reads the camera world position and its near and far Z planes. Call it every frame.

water.update.brief:
Advances the wave time by `dt` times the time speed `init` stored, unless the timer
is paused. Call it every frame.

water.pause.brief: Pauses or resumes the wave timer.

water.get_wave1.brief: Returns the first wave layer's direction, amplitude, wavelength and speed.

water.set_wave2.brief: Sets the second wave layer, with the same ranges as `set_wave1`.

water.get_wave2.brief: Returns the second wave layer's direction, amplitude, wavelength and speed.

water.set_wave_normal_params.brief: Sets the animated normal map that adds ripple detail to the surface.

water.get_wave_normal_params.brief: Returns the normal map tiling and animation speed.

water.set_shallow_color.brief: Sets the water color in shallow areas. The shader always uses an alpha of `1`.

water.get_shallow_color.brief: Returns the shallow water color's red, green and blue components.

water.set_deep_color.brief: Sets the water color in deep areas.

water.get_deep_color.brief: Returns the deep water color's red, green and blue components.

water.set_far_color.brief: Sets the water color far from the camera, which the surface fades to with distance.

water.get_far_color.brief: Returns the far water color's red, green and blue components.

water.set_foam_params.brief: Sets the foam's look and animation.

water.get_foam_params.brief: Returns the foam tiling, speed, normal map distortion and visibility.

water.set_density_params.brief: Sets how the color fades with distance and blends with depth.

water.get_density_params.brief: Returns the distance fade rate and the depth blending intensity.

water.set_sun_params.brief: Sets the sharpness of the sun's specular highlight.

water.get_sun_color.brief: Returns the sun color's red, green and blue components.

water.set_sun_direction.brief:
Sets the directional light direction. `init` and `update_sun` overwrite it with the
direction from the water object to the sun.

water.get_sun_direction.brief: Returns the X, Y and Z components of the sun direction.

water.get_sparkle_params.brief: Returns the sparkle tiling, speed and sharpness, and `1` when sparkles are enabled or `0` when not.

water.disable_sparkle.brief: Disables the sparkle effect, which saves eight texture samples per fragment.

water.is_sparkle_enabled.brief: Returns `true` when the sparkle effect is enabled.

water.get_sparkle_color.brief: Returns the sparkle color's red, green and blue components.

water.set_edge_foam_params.brief: Sets the foam drawn where the water meets other geometry, based on water depth.

water.get_edge_foam_params.brief: Returns the edge foam depth scale, noise strength, edge softness and opacity.

water.set_edge_foam_type.brief: Sets how the edge foam is drawn. It also prints `SET` and the type on every call.

water.get_edge_foam_type.brief: Returns the edge foam type: `0` for a solid color, `1` for a texture.

water.get_edge_foam_color.brief: Returns the edge foam color's red, green and blue components.

water.get_refraction_params.brief: Returns the refraction strength and chromatic aberration.

water.set_reflection_params.brief:
Sets the cubemap reflection. The reflection samples the cubemap bound to the water
material's `reflection_cubemap` sampler; this module binds none.

water.get_reflection_params.brief: Returns the reflection strength and fresnel power.

water.set_skybox_cubemap.brief: Prints a warning and does nothing else.

water.set_lod_params.brief: Sets the level-of-detail distances beyond which effects are simplified.

water.get_lod_params.brief: Returns the sparkle and foam level-of-detail distances.

asobi.api.auth.brief:
asobi sign-in over REST: accounts, OAuth, guest devices, linked providers and the token
pair. A project reaches it as `client.auth`.

asobi.api.auth.register.brief:
Creates an account and signs it in. On success it stores the returned tokens with
`client.set_tokens` and sets `client.player_id`.

asobi.api.auth.login.brief:
Signs an account in. On success it stores the returned tokens with `client.set_tokens`
and sets `client.player_id`.

asobi.api.auth.oauth.brief:
Signs in with a token from an OAuth provider. On success it stores the returned tokens
with `client.set_tokens` and sets `client.player_id`.

asobi.api.auth.guest.brief:
Signs a guest in with a device credential pair. On success it stores the returned tokens
with `client.set_tokens` and sets `client.player_id`.

asobi.api.auth.guest_device.brief:
Loads the saved device credential pair, or generates and saves one, and signs a guest in
with it through `guest`.

asobi.api.auth.upgrade_guest.brief:
Turns the signed-in guest into an account with a username and password. On success it
stores the returned tokens with `client.set_tokens` and sets `client.player_id`.

asobi.api.auth.link_provider.brief: Links an OAuth provider to the signed-in account.

asobi.api.auth.unlink_provider.brief: Unlinks an OAuth provider from the signed-in account.

asobi.api.auth.refresh.brief:
Exchanges the refresh token for a new token pair, which it stores with
`client.set_tokens`. The server accepts each refresh token once. An open realtime
connection re-authenticates with the new access token. `asobi.http` calls it on a 401.

asobi.api.auth.logout.brief:
Signs out, then forgets both tokens and `client.player_id` whether or not the server
answered with an error.

asobi.client.brief:
The asobi client. `create` builds a client for one asobi server, carrying its tokens and
the realtime connection, and `quick_start` signs a guest in, connects and queues for a
match in one call.

asobi.client.create.brief:
Creates a client for an asobi server, with its realtime connection. Nothing connects
until `realtime.connect` is called.

asobi.client.quick_start.brief:
Signs a guest in, connects and queues for a match in one call, registering every handler
before it connects. The sign-in runs asynchronously, so the client returns at once; use
`create` and the realtime connection directly for entity sync or custom match state.

asobi.client.Client.set_tokens.brief:
Stores a new token pair and saves the refresh token with `sys.save`, so it survives a
restart.

asobi.client.Client.clear_tokens.brief: Forgets both tokens and erases the saved refresh token.

asobi.client.Client.use_ssl.brief: Whether the client connects over `https` and `wss`.

asobi.client.Client.base_url.brief: The REST base url, without the port when it is the scheme's default.

asobi.client.Client.ws_url.brief: The realtime websocket url, `<base>/ws`, without the port when it is the scheme's default.

asobi.client.Client.access_token.brief: The access token, kept in memory only.

asobi.client.Client.refresh_token.brief:
The refresh token. `create` loads the one an earlier session saved with `sys.save`, and
`set_tokens` and `clear_tokens` save it again.

asobi.client.Client.realtime.brief: The realtime connection, created with the client.

asobi.client.Client.http.brief: The REST transport every module below sends through.

asobi.client.Client.auth.brief: Sign-in, guest devices, linked providers and the token pair.

asobi.client.QuickStartOptions.ssl.brief: Whether to connect over `https` and `wss`. Defaults to `true`.

asobi.client.QuickStartOptions.port.brief: The server's port. Defaults to `443` with `ssl`, `8084` without.

asobi.client.QuickStartOptions.mode.brief: The matchmaker mode to queue for. Defaults to `"default"`.

asobi.client.QuickStartOptions.on_queued.brief: Called when the matchmaker accepts the ticket, with `ticket_id` and `players_needed`.

asobi.client.QuickStartOptions.on_matche.brief: Called when the matchmaker places the player in a match, with its `match_id`.

asobi.client.QuickStartOptions.on_state.brief: Called with each match state snapshot.

asobi.client.QuickStartOptions.on_failed.brief:
Called when the guest sign-in fails, when the match cannot start, and on every realtime
`error`, with the failure's `reason`.

asobi.client.QuickStartOptions.on_signed.brief: Called after the guest sign-in succeeds, before the client connects.

node_repeat.brief: GUI box node texture repeat (tiling) shader helper: reads a box node's atlas animation and drives the repeat material's constants.

node_repeat.create.brief:
Reads an atlas animation's frames for a GUI box node that uses the repeat
material, and returns a handle that applies them. Call it from a GUI script.
Apply the repeat material to the node first, and disable sprite trim mode for
the atlas images: every frame must have exactly 8 UV values, or this asserts.
Walks the atlas animation's frame list, so it needs Defold 1.12.3 or later.

node_repeat.get_screen_aspect_ratio.brief:
Measures how the window is stretched relative to the GUI's design size, stores
the result in `x_ratio` and `y_ratio`, and returns it. The smaller ratio is
always `1`. Call it from a GUI script.

node_repeat.x_ratio.brief:
The horizontal stretch of the window relative to the GUI's design size, divided
by the smaller of the two stretches. Starts at `1`; `get_screen_aspect_ratio`
updates it.

node_repeat.y_ratio.brief:
The vertical stretch of the window relative to the GUI's design size, divided by
the smaller of the two stretches. Starts at `1`; `get_screen_aspect_ratio`
updates it.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.animate.brief:
Applies the first frame and the repeat factors to the node. When the
animation has more than one frame and a non-zero `fps`, starts a repeating
timer that steps through the frames.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.stop.brief: Cancels the playback timer, if one is running.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.update.brief:
Changes the repeat factors and applies them to the node. A factor left out
keeps its current value.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.frames.brief: Every frame of the animation, in playback order.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.width.brief: The animation's width, from the atlas.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.height.brief: The animation's height, from the atlas.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.fps.brief: The animation's playback rate, from the atlas.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.current_.brief: The 1-based index of the frame shown next. **⚠️ 1-based; passed to `node_repeat` unchanged.**

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.v.brief: The `uv_repeat` value: `x`/`y` the repeat factors, `z`/`w` the current frame's size.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.node.brief: The box node the animation drives.

node_repeat.NodeRepeatAnimation.handle.brief: The `timer.delay` handle driving playback. Present only while a multi-frame animation plays.

node_repeat.RepeatFrame.uv_coord.brief: The frame's UV rectangle in the texture: `x`/`y` one corner, `z`/`w` the other.

node_repeat.RepeatFrame.w.brief: The frame's width in texture pixels.

node_repeat.RepeatFrame.h.brief: The frame's height in texture pixels.

node_repeat.RepeatFrame.uv_rotated.brief: `(0, 1, 0, 0)` when the atlas stores the frame rotated clockwise, else `(1, 0, 0, 0)`.

persist.flush.brief: Flushes unsaved data from a file. If a key is specified, then only that field is flushed.

persist.save.brief: Saves data that was written to a file.

persist.load.brief:

saver.saver.brief: Persistent save helpers for Defold: typed tables, versioned slots, and atomic writes.

saver.saver.set_logger.brief:
File format enum (mirrors saver_internal.FORMAT)
Customize the logging mechanism used by Defold Saver.
You can use Defold Log library or provide a custom logger.
local log = require("log.log")
local saver = require("saver.saver")

saver.set_logger(log.get_logger("saver"))

saver.saver.init.brief:
Initialize the Saver module. Should be called at the start of your game to set up the module.
Call it after saver.set_migrations if you are using migrations.
This function loads the game state from a file and starts the autosave timer.
If the game state file does not exist, a new game state is created.
saver.init()

saver.saver.save_game_state.brief:
Save the current game state to a file. If no file name is provided, the default file name specified in the game.project file is used.
-- Save the game with default name
saver.save_game_state()

-- Save the game with custom name
saver.save_game_state("custom_save")

saver.saver.load_game_state.brief:
Load the game state from a file. If no file name is provided, the default file name specified in the game.project file is used.
local is_loaded = saver.load_game_state() -- Load the game state with default name
local is_loaded = saver.load_game_state("custom_save") -- Load the game state with custom name

saver.saver.delete_game_state.brief:
Delete the game state file. Doesn't affect the current game state.
If autosave is enabled, it will be rescheduled, so probably you want to immediately restart the game.
-- Delete the game state with default name
saver.delete_game_state()

-- Delete the game state with custom name
saver.delete_game_state("custom_save")

saver.saver.get_game_state.brief:
Returns the current game state.
local game_state = saver.get_game_state()
pprint(game_state)

saver.saver.set_game_state.brief:
Sets the current game state to the specified state.
local game_state = saver.get_game_state()
game_state.game.level = 5
saver.set_game_state(game_state)

saver.saver.bind_save_state.brief:
Binds a table reference as a part of the game state. When the game state is saved, all table references will be saved.
This is a main function to use to save your game state. You can bind multiple tables to different parts of the game state.
After binding, the table_reference will be updated with the saved data if it exists.
local game_state = {
level = 1,
money = 100
}

saver.bind_save_state("game", game_state)

-- If we have previously saved game state, the game_state will be changed to the saved data
print(game_state.level) -- 5 (if it was saved before)

saver.saver.save_file_by_path.brief:
Saves the specified data to a file at the specified path. The data format is chosen by file path extension.
local data = {
score = 100,
level = 1
}

-- Get project path works on build from the Defold Editor only
local project_path = saver.get_current_game_project_folder()
-- Use path to the resources folder
local file_path = saver.get_save_path(project_path .. "/resources/data.json")
saver.save_file_by_path(data, file_path)

saver.saver.save_binary_by_path.brief: Saves the specified data to a file at the specified path. The data format is binary.

saver.saver.load_file_by_path.brief:
Loads the data from a file at the specified path.
-- Get project path works on build from the Defold Editor only
local project_path = saver.get_current_game_project_folder()
-- Use path to the resources folder
local file_path = saver.get_save_path(project_path .. "/resources/data.json")
local data = saver.load_file_by_path(file_path)
pprint(data)
NOTE: For binary data like images, use `saver.load_binary_by_path` instead.

saver.saver.load_binary_by_path.brief: Loads the binary data from a file at the specified path.

saver.saver.delete_file_by_path.brief: Deletes the file at the specified path.

saver.saver.is_file_exists_by_path.brief:
Checks if the file exists at the specified path.
local is_project_file_exists = saver.is_file_exists_by_path(absolute_path_to_file)

saver.saver.save_file_by_name.brief:
Saves the specified data to a file with the specified name. The file is saved in the game save folder. Filename supports subfolders.
local data = {
score = 100,
level = 1
}

-- Save the data to the game save folder
saver.save_file_by_name(data, "data.json")

saver.saver.save_binary_by_name.brief: Saves the specified data to a file with the specified name. The data format is binary.

saver.saver.load_file_by_name.brief:
Loads the data from a file with the specified name. The file is loaded from the game save folder. Filename supports subfolders.
local data = saver.load_file_by_name("data.json")
pprint(data)
NOTE: For binary data like images, use saver.load_binary_by_name instead.

saver.saver.load_binary_by_name.brief: Loads the binary data from a file with the specified name. The file is loaded from the game save folder. Filename supports subfolders.

saver.saver.delete_file_by_name.brief:
Deletes the file with the specified name. The file is deleted from the game save folder. Filename supports subfolders.
saver.delete_file_by_name("data.json")

saver.saver.is_file_exists_by_name.brief: Checks if the file exists with the specified name. The file is checked in the game save folder. Filename supports subfolders.

saver.saver.get_save_path.brief:
Returns the absolute path to the game save folder. If a file name is provided, the path to the file in the game save folder is returned. Filename supports subfolders.
local folder_path = saver.get_save_path()
print(folder_path) -- "/Users/user/Library/Application Support/Defold Saver/"

local file_path = saver.get_save_path("data.json")
print(file_path) -- "/Users/user/Library/Application Support/Defold Saver/data.json"

local file_path_2 = saver.get_save_path("profiles/profile1.json")
print(file_path_2) -- "/Users/user/Library/Application Support/Defold Saver/profiles/profile1.json"

saver.saver.get_save_version.brief:
Returns the current save version of the game state. The save version is used to check if the game state is older than the current version. The save version increments when the game state is saved.
local save_version = saver.get_save_version()
print(save_version)

saver.saver.set_autosave_timer.brief:
Sets the autosave timer to the specified number of seconds. The autosave timer is used to automatically save the game state at regular intervals.
Use 0 to disable autosave.
saver.set_autosave_timer(5) -- Autosave every 5 seconds
saver.set_autosave_timer(0) -- Disable autosave

saver.saver.get_current_game_project_fol.brief:
Returns the absolute path to the current game project folder. It is useful when you need to save or load files from the game project folder at development.
Returns nil if the game project folder is not found. Used only at desktop platforms and if game started from the Defold Editor.
local project_folder = saver.get_current_game_project_folder()
print(project_folder) -- "/Users/user/projects/my_game"

saver.saver.apply_migrations.brief:
Applies the migrations set by saver.set_migrations function. It should be called after loading the game state manually with saver.init() function.
saver.apply_migrations()

saver.saver.get_value.brief: Gets the value from the saver storage. If the value does not exist, it will return the default value.

saver.saver.set_value.brief: Sets the value in the saver storage.

saver.saver.is_value_exists.brief: Checks if the value exists in the saver storage.

saver.saver.saver_config.save_folder.brief: Save folder name. Default is project name without special characters

saver.saver.saver_config.save_name.brief: Save file name, use ".json" or ".lua" extension to use these formats. Default is "game"

saver.saver.saver_config.saver_key.brief: Saver key, where saver internal data will be stored. Default is "saver"

saver.saver.saver_config.storage_key.brief: Storage key, where storage internal data will be stored. Deprecated. Default is "storage"

saver.saver.saver_config.autosave_timer.brief: Autosave timer in seconds. Default is 3 seconds

saver.saver.saver_config.lua_require_as_.brief: If true, the `require()` function will load Lua files as strings instead of Lua tables. Default is false

wrap.wrap.brief:

wrap.wrap.node.brief: Wraps each node, keyed by its name, from `wrap.node_list.new`.

wrap.wrap.go.brief: Wraps each game object, keyed by its name, from `wrap.go_list.new`.

printer.brief: A symbol-by-symbol text writer for Defold Engine. Developed for rich game dialogs.

printer.new.brief:
Creates a printer instance on a gui scene that holds a printer template. The
module reads the template's `prefab`, `prefab_icon` and `text_parent` nodes, and
places text from the top left of `text_parent`.

printer.print.brief:
Starts printing text on an instance. Wrap a style name in braces to switch style
(`{red}`), use `{/}` to return to the default style, `{n}` for a line break and
`{image:name}` for an image.

printer.instant_appear.brief:
Makes every symbol of the current text visible at once, only when the effective
style of the symbol currently appearing has `can_skip` set to `true`; otherwise the
text keeps printing.

printer.fadeout.brief: Stops printing and fades every symbol of the current text out over 0.3 seconds.

printer.clear.brief: Deletes all of the current printed text.

printer.update.brief: Advances printing and the text shake. Call it from the gui script's `update`.

printer.final.brief: Deletes the printed text and stops printing. Call it from the gui script's `final`.

printer.play_sound.brief:
Called whenever a symbol with a style `sound` appears; it does nothing until a
project replaces it with its own sound playback. A namespace import is read-only,
so assign through a cast that keeps the function free of `self`:
`(printer as { play_sound: (this: void, name: string) => void }).play_sound = (name) => { ... }`.

printer.add_styles.brief:
Adds styles to the module, shared by every instance. A style with an existing name
replaces it, and a style named `default` replaces the default style.

printer.add_source_style.brief:
Adds a source style: a `print` given this source copies the style over the default
style and uses it as the text's base style.

printer.add_word_style.brief:
Adds a word style: every occurrence of the word in printed text is wrapped in the
style, then returns to the default style. The match is case sensitive.

printer.printers.brief: A table the module creates and never reads.

printer.Printer.print.brief:
Starts printing text. Wrap a style name in braces to switch style (`{red}`), use
`{/}` to return to the default style, `{n}` for a line break and `{image:name}`
for an image.

printer.Printer.instant_appear.brief: Makes every symbol of the current text visible at once, only when the effective style of the symbol currently appearing has `can_skip` set to `true`; otherwise the text keeps printing.

printer.Printer.fadeout.brief: Stops printing and fades every symbol of the current text out over 0.3 seconds.

printer.Printer.clear.brief: Deletes all of the current printed text.

printer.Printer.update.brief: Advances printing and the text shake. Call it from the gui script's `update`.

printer.Printer.final.brief: Deletes the printed text and stops printing. Call it from the gui script's `final`.

printer.Printer.is_print.brief:
Whether the printer is printing text now. It is unset until the first `print`,
`fadeout` or `final`.

printer.PrinterStyle.font_height.brief: In pixels, the height of every symbol or image. It also sets where a new line starts.

printer.PrinterStyle.spacing.brief: In pixels, the horizontal distance between symbols.

printer.PrinterStyle.speed.brief: In seconds, the time between printing one symbol and the next.

printer.PrinterStyle.appear.brief: In seconds, how long a symbol takes to fade in from alpha 0 to 1.

printer.PrinterStyle.shaking.brief: In pixels, how far every symbol in this style shakes. `0` disables it.

printer.PrinterStyle.shake_on_write.brief: In pixels, how far the whole text shakes when a symbol in this style appears. `0` disables it.

printer.PrinterStyle.color.brief: The hex color code of every symbol in this style, for example `"#CACACA"`.

printer.PrinterStyle.waving.brief: `true` makes the symbols wave up and down.

printer.PrinterStyle.can_skip.brief: `true` lets `instant_appear` reveal text in this style at once. The default style sets it, so a style that omits it inherits it; a replacement `default` style that omits it disables `instant_appear`.

printer.PrinterStyle.sound.brief: The sound name passed to `play_sound` when a symbol appears, or `false` for none.

nakama.session.brief: Create, check, store and restore Nakama sessions from their JWT tokens.

nakama.session.is_token_expired_soon.brief:
Whether the session's access token expires within the next twenty-four hours.
Refresh the session while this is true rather than waiting for it to expire.

nakama.session.is_token_expired.brief: Whether the session's access token has already expired.

nakama.session.expired.brief:
Upstream's backwards-compatible alias of `is_token_expired`, kept because older
code calls it. New code should call `is_token_expired`.

nakama.session.is_refresh_token_expired.brief:
Whether the session's refresh token has expired. A session created without a
refresh token counts as expired, there being nothing left to refresh with.

nakama.session.create.brief:
Builds a session from an authentication response, decoding the tokens it carries
to read their expiry, username, user id and session variables.

nakama.session.store.brief: Writes a session to disk under the project title, so it survives a restart.

nakama.session.restore.brief: Reads back a session written by `store`.

nakama.session.Session.token.brief: The access token the server issued, as the JWT string it arrived as.

nakama.session.Session.expires.brief: The access token's `exp` claim, in seconds since the epoch.

nakama.session.Session.username.brief: The username the access token's `usn` claim carries.

nakama.session.Session.user_id.brief: The user id the access token's `uid` claim carries.

nakama.session.Session.vars.brief: The session variables the access token's `vrs` claim carries, if any.

nakama.session.Session.refresh_token.brief: The refresh token the server issued, if the response carried one.

nakama.session.Session.refresh_token_exp.brief: The refresh token's `exp` claim, in seconds since the epoch.

nakama.session.Session.refresh_token_use.brief: The username the refresh token's `usn` claim carries.

shutter.brief: Shutter is a library for 2D camera functionality in a Defold game engine project.

shutter.activate.brief:
Installs a camera's viewport, view matrix and projection matrix into the render
context. Call it from a render script before drawing the world.

shutter.deactivate.brief:
Restores the viewport and matrices Defold's GUI system expects, sized to the
current window. Call it before drawing GUI.

shutter.force_update.brief:
Recalculates a camera's viewport, view matrix and projection matrix immediately.
The shutter.script game object already does this once per frame; call it directly
only after changing a camera property mid-frame.

shutter.get_viewport.brief:
Calculates the camera's viewport in window coordinates, scaled from the
game.project display size and, under center behavior, shrunk and centered to
preserve the display ratio.

shutter.get_view.brief:
Calculates the camera's view matrix from the inverse of its game object's world
transform.

shutter.get_projection.brief:
Calculates the camera's orthographic projection matrix, sized from the display
under center and stretch behavior and from the window under expand behavior.

shutter.get_frustum.brief:
Returns the camera's frustum, the product of its last calculated projection and
view matrices.

shutter.get_distance.brief:
Converts a screen distance into the world distance an object must travel to cover
it, accounting for the camera's zoom and, under center and stretch behavior, for
the viewport no longer mapping to physical screen coordinates.

shutter.shake.brief:
Starts a camera shake animation, cancelling and restarting any shake already
running on this camera.

shutter.cancel_shake.brief:
Stops a running camera shake and returns the shaken object to where it started.
Does nothing if no shake is running.

shutter.screen_to_world.brief:
Converts a screen position to its world position through the inverse of the
camera's frustum.

shutter.world_to_screen.brief: Converts a world position to its screen position through the camera's frustum.

shutter.camera_table.brief:
Every live camera, keyed by the id of the game object it lives on. The
shutter.script file writes to it; read from it rather than manipulating it
directly.

shutter.center_behavior.brief:
Keeps the projection fixed and shrinks the viewport to preserve the display
ratio, letterboxing or pillarboxing the remainder.

shutter.expand_behavior.brief:
Keeps the viewport filling the window and widens the projection as the window
grows, showing more of the game world rather than scaling it.

shutter.stretch_behavior.brief:
Keeps both the viewport and the projection filling the window, so the game world
distorts with the window ratio.

shutter.ShutterCamera.viewport_x_adjuste.brief: Viewport left edge after the window scale and any letterboxing margin.

shutter.ShutterCamera.viewport_y_adjuste.brief: Viewport bottom edge after the window scale and any pillarboxing margin.

shutter.ShutterCamera.shake_origin.brief:
Where the shaken object sat before the shake began, and `nil` while no shake
is running. `cancel_shake` restores the object to it.

fake_real_glass.brief: A multipass glass rendering library for Defold with screen-space double refraction, thickness-based distortion, optional color absorption and local cubemap reflection probes. Supports lighting from Defold light components and configurable reflection modes that update probes every frame, capture once or use pre-rendered cubemaps. Includes a reusable Lua render module, glass materials and example scenes with glass spheres, a wine glass and planar mirror reflections. Integrates with custom render pipelines and requires Defold 1.14.0 or newer.

fake_real_glass.create.brief:
Create the per-render-script state for the fake glass pipeline.

This allocates Lua-side state immediately. Screen-sized render targets are
created by `resize()` and recreated automatically when sizes change.

The returned table is intended to be stored by one render script instance.
It tracks probe settings, render targets, and the constant buffer used when
drawing visible glass objects.

fake_real_glass.resize.brief:
Resize screen-sized render targets to match the current window size.

Call this from `init()` and when the window size changes.

If probe rendering is enabled, this also ensures the cubemap exists,
but does not force it to be redrawn immediately.

fake_real_glass.final.brief:
Release all render targets owned by the module.

Call this from the host render script's `final()` function to avoid leaking
the scene capture, back-face capture, and probe-face render targets.

fake_real_glass.on_message.brief:
Handle probe-control messages sent to `@render:`.

Returns `true` if the message belonged to this module and was handled.
That lets the host render script early-return without processing the same
message twice.

fake_real_glass.draw.brief:
Run the fake glass passes for the current frame.

The host render script should:
1. draw its normal opaque world to the default framebuffer
2. call this function before GUI rendering

This function may:
1. re-render the six probe faces
2. capture the opaque scene into `scene_rt`
3. capture the glass back faces into `backface_rt`
4. draw the visible front-face glass to the default framebuffer

wrap.gui_scene.brief:
The base class of a GUI scene: one screen of an applet, with its own hidden root box
node, the GUI objects created in it, the modals registered on it, and the transitions it
plays when it is shown and replaced. A game subclasses it with `extend`, assigns hooks
to the subclass, and hands it to an applet's `register_scene` or `show_scene`.

wrap.gui_scene.new.brief: Returns a new, not yet set up scene of the base class.

wrap.gui_scene.extend.brief:
Returns a new subclass: a table indexing the base class, with its own `new`. Assign
hooks such as `init` and `on_ready` to it, and pass it to an applet. `F` types the
fields and methods a game adds to it.

wrap.gui_scene.__name.brief:
The class name, the value `register_scene` and `show_scene` read to tell a class from
a plain table.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.register_modal.brief:
Registers a modal built from a plain table of hooks and fields, whose keys are copied
onto a fresh `wrap.gui_object.extend()` once, at registration.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.unregister_modal.brief: Removes the modal registered under a name.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.open_modal.brief:
Creates the modal registered under a name with `new_object`. Its props are a copy of
the registered props with the given ones copied over them, and its settings the same.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.new_object.brief: Creates an object whose class needs settings, as the first form does.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.setup.brief:
Sets the scene up in an applet and runs `init`. `show_scene` calls it on each scene
it shows; a game does not.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.is_alive.brief:
Returns whether the scene is set up and not finalized: `nil` until `setup` has run
`init`, so also during `init`, then `true` until `bg_final` makes it `false`.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.is_ready.brief:
Returns whether the scene's transition in has finished and it is not yet
transitioning out, the only state in which it receives messages and input.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.set_transitions.brief: Sets the transitions the scene plays, replacing any set before.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.transition_in.brief:
Plays the transition in, if one is set, then makes the scene ready and runs
`on_ready`. Does nothing unless the scene is newly set up. `show_scene` calls it.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.set_transition_i.brief:
Resumes the transition in where it waits for its animation. The transition in calls
it when done; at this tag it resumes whatever state the scene is in.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.transition_out.brief:
Plays the transition out, if one is set, then finalizes the scene with `bg_final`.
Does nothing unless the scene is ready. `show_scene` calls it on the scene it
replaces.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.set_transition_o.brief:
Resumes the transition out where it waits for its animation. The transition out
calls it when done; at this tag it resumes whatever state the scene is in.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.on_ready.brief: Runs once the transition in has finished, from `transition_in`. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.init.brief: Runs once `setup` has created `root`, from `show_scene`. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.update.brief: Runs each frame from `bg_update` while the scene is alive. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.final.brief: Runs once from `bg_final`, before the objects and `root` are deleted. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.on_message.brief: Runs from `bg_on_message` while the scene is ready. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.on_input.brief: Runs from `bg_on_input` when no object consumed the input. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.bg_update.brief:
Runs `update`, then each object's `bg_update`, unless the scene is not alive. The
applet's `update` calls it each frame, for the scene transitioning out too.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.bg_final.brief:
Finalizes the scene, unless it is not alive: marks it finalized, runs `final`,
deletes each object, then deletes `root` and the nodes under it. The transition out
and the applet's `final` call it.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.bg_on_message.brief:
Passes a message to `on_message` while the scene is ready. The applet's `on_message`
calls it.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.bg_on_input.brief:
Offers input to each object's `bg_on_input`, the newest first, then to `on_input` if
none consumed it. Returns `false` unless the scene is ready. The applet's `on_input`
calls it.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.fade_in.brief: Returns a transition that sets the root's alpha to `0` and animates it to `1`.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.fade_out.brief: Returns a transition that animates the root's alpha to `0`.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.slide_in_top.brief:
Returns a transition that moves the root up by the applet's height and animates it
down to `0`.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.slide_in_bottom.brief:
Returns a transition that moves the root down by the applet's height and animates it
up to `0`.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.slide_in_right.brief:
Returns a transition that moves the root right by the applet's width and animates it
left to `0`.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.slide_in_left.brief:
Returns a transition that moves the root left by the applet's width and animates it
right to `0`.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.slide_out_top.brief: Returns a transition that animates the root up by the applet's height.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.slide_out_bottom.brief: Returns a transition that animates the root down by the applet's height.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.slide_out_right.brief: Returns a transition that animates the root right by the applet's width.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.slide_out_left.brief: Returns a transition that animates the root left by the applet's width.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.app.brief: The applet showing the scene, set by `setup`.

wrap.gui_scene.GuiScene.root.brief:
The scene's root, a box node `setup` creates hidden under the applet's root. Every
object created in the scene has its own root under it, and the built-in transitions
animate it.

wrap.gui_scene.Transitions.transition_in.brief: Played by `transition_in` before the scene is ready.

wrap.gui_scene.Transitions.transition_ou.brief: Played by `transition_out` before the scene is finalized.

illumination.brief:
Forward shading lighting for 3D games, with ambient and directional light, point and
spot lights, and linear or radial fog. Add `illumination.go` to the scene as the
sunlight source, add `light_point.go` or `light_spot.go` for each light, and set
`/illumination/materials/model.material` on the meshes. The lighting data reaches the
shader as a texture, so no render script is needed. The module's functions toggle the
debug meshes and set lights and the environment by hand.

illumination.set_debug.brief: Shows or hides the debug meshes of the sun and the light sources.

illumination.is_debug.brief: Returns whether the debug meshes show.

illumination.set_environment.brief:
Patches the environment with the fields given and leaves the others as they are. The
fog fields apply only while the stored fog type, including one set in the same call,
is not `FOG_TYPE_NONE`, and `fog_color` also posts `clear_color` to `@render:`. The
bundled `illumination.go` patches each field from its own properties on its first
update and whenever that property changes, overwriting a value set here. Raises until
the bundled `illumination.go` has run its script's `init`.

illumination.set_light.brief:
Adds, updates or removes a light source by hand, for lights that are not
`light_point.go` or `light_spot.go`. `position`, `color`, `radius` and `cutoff` are
required, `specular` and `smoothness` default to `1`, and each position axis must lie
within -2048 to 2048. `undefined`, or a light whose `color.w`, `radius` or `cutoff` is
`0` or below, removes the light. `url` keys the light, so pass the same value on every
call for the same light. It receives a `debug` message carrying `is_enabled` when the
light is added or removed and on every `set_debug`. Adding or updating a light raises
until the bundled `illumination.go` has run its script's `init`.

illumination.FOG_TYPE_LINEAR.brief: Fog along the camera's view direction.

illumination.Environment.fog_type.brief: The fog type. The fog fields below apply only while the fog type is not `FOG_TYPE_NONE`.

illumination.Environment.ambient_color.brief: The ambient light color, its `w` the ambient strength.

illumination.Environment.sunlight_color.brief: The directional light color, its `w` the sunlight brightness.

illumination.Environment.sunlight_direct.brief: The direction the sunlight shines, normalized by upstream.

illumination.Environment.sunlight_specul.brief: The sunlight's specular component, from `0` to `1`.

illumination.Environment.fog_color.brief: The fog color, its `w` the fog's full strength. Also posted as `clear_color` to `@render:`.

illumination.Environment.fog_min.brief: The distance at which the fog begins. Values below `0` are raised to `0`.

illumination.Environment.fog_max.brief: The distance at which the fog reaches full strength. Values below `fog_min` are raised to it.

illumination.Light.position.brief: The light's world position. Each axis is encoded within -2048 to 2048.

illumination.Light.color.brief: The light color, multiplied with the diffuse color. Its `w` is the brightness.

illumination.Light.radius.brief: The light radius. Upstream rounds it up and caps it at `255`.

illumination.Light.cutoff.brief:
The spotlight cutoff, from `0` to `1`: `0.3` is like a flashlight, `0.5` half of the
sphere, and `1` no cutoff.

illumination.Light.direction.brief: The direction a spotlight shines. Read only while `cutoff` is below `1`.

illumination.Light.specular.brief: The light's specular component, from `0` to `1`. Defaults to `1`.

illumination.Light.smoothness.brief:
The light's attenuation, from `0` to `1`: `0` fills the radius evenly and `1` fades
from the center to the edge. Defaults to `1`.
