defgraph.brief:
Builds a world map as a graph of nodes and routes that can change at any time, draws
it for debugging, and moves game objects along it with a built-in pathfinder. Add
nodes with `map_add_node` and join them with `map_add_route`, start each game object
with `move_initialize`, then call `move_player` from its `update` and apply the
position and rotation it returns.

defgraph.map_set_properties.brief:
Sets the module's path and movement settings, which every `move_initialize` call
falls back to for a setting it is not given. A `nil` keeps a setting's current
value, and each starts at the default stated on it.

defgraph.map_add_node.brief:
Adds a node at a position and returns its id. The position's `z` is ignored. A node
with no route takes no part in routing, so remove one that is no longer used.

defgraph.map_update_node_position.brief:
Moves an existing node, and the routes attached to it with it. An unknown id fails
an assert.

defgraph.map_remove_node.brief: Removes a node and every route attached to it. An unknown id fails an assert.

defgraph.map_add_route.brief:
Adds a route between two nodes, both ways unless `is_one_way` is `true`. A route
from a node to itself is ignored, and an unknown id fails an assert. A one-way route
is a little cheaper to path through when the other way is never needed.

defgraph.map_remove_route.brief:
Removes the route between two nodes, both ways unless `is_remove_one_way` is `true`.
An unknown id fails an assert.

defgraph.debug_set_properties.brief:
Sets the colors and the scale the `debug_draw_*` functions draw with. A `nil` keeps
a value's current setting, and each starts at the default stated on it.

defgraph.debug_draw_map_nodes.brief:
Draws every node for one frame, by posting `draw_line` and, for the ids,
`draw_text` to `@render:`. A node with no route is drawn as a triangle, a dead end
as a cross and an intersection as a square. Call it every frame to keep it shown.

defgraph.debug_draw_map_routes.brief:
Draws every route for one frame, by posting `draw_line` to `@render:`: two-way
routes in one color, and one-way routes in another with a square near the end they
run to. Call it every frame to keep it shown.

defgraph.debug_draw_player_move.brief:
Draws the rest of a game object's path for one frame, by posting `draw_line` to
`@render:`. Nothing is drawn while the game object stands still for want of a
route. Call it every frame to keep it shown.

defgraph.move_initialize.brief:
Starts a game object moving from its position through a list of destination nodes,
and returns the movement data `move_player` takes. Each setting it is not given
falls back to the value `map_set_properties` set. To change the destinations, call
it again and replace the old movement data with the result.

defgraph.move_player.brief:
Moves a game object one step along its path toward its current destination, and
returns the movement data and the result of the move:
`const [data, result] = defgraph.move_player(go.get_position(), speed * dt, move)`.
Keep the returned movement data in place of the one passed in. When the map has
changed since the last call, the path is found again first. `result.rotation` is
`undefined` unless `move_initialize` was given an `initial_face_vector`.

defgraph.ROUTETYPE.brief:
How `move_initialize` takes a game object through more than one destination.
`ONETIME` visits them in order and stops at the last, `SHUFFLE` visits them in
random order without stopping, and `CYCLE` visits them in order and starts over
after the last. With one destination they all behave the same.

defgraph.MoveData.destination_list.brief: The destination node ids, the same list `move_initialize` was given.

defgraph.MoveData.destination_index.brief:
The 1-based index of the current destination in `destination_list`.
**⚠️ 1-based; passed to `defgraph` unchanged.**

defgraph.MoveData.route_type.brief: The `ROUTETYPE` the game object moves by.

defgraph.MoveData.path_index.brief:
The 1-based index of the next point on the path, or `0` while the game object
stands still because the map has no route or `destination_list` is empty.
**⚠️ 1-based; passed to `defgraph` unchanged.**

defgraph.MoveResult.rotation.brief:
The game object's next rotation around z, relative to the `initial_face_vector`
passed to `move_initialize`. `undefined` when `move_initialize` was given none.

defgraph.MoveResult.is_reached.brief:
Whether the game object is at its destination. With more than one destination it
reads `true` on reaching each one, then `false` again while `destination_id` moves
on to the next.

defgraph.MoveResult.destination_id.brief: The node id of the current destination.

operator.operator.brief:
Shared settings and math helpers for the Operator camera controller. The camera itself
is driven by the properties and messages of `operator/operator/operator.script`
(`activate`, `follow_point`, `manual_control` and the rest), which are not members of
this module. The settings fields are plain module fields; assigning one goes through a
cast, since a namespace import is read-only:
`(operator as { flight_look_easing: (this: void, x: number) => number }).flight_look_easing = (x) => x`.

operator.operator.lerp.brief:
Linearly interpolates from vector `a` to vector `b`, returning `a + (b - a) * t` as a
new vector. `t` is not clamped, so a value outside `0` to `1` extrapolates.

operator.operator.angle_between.brief:
Returns the angle between two vectors, in degrees from `0` to `180`. A vector of zero
length gives NaN.

operator.operator.project_on_plane.brief:
Projects a vector onto the plane through the origin with the given normal, returning
`v - plane_normal * vmath.dot(plane_normal, v)`. The normal must have unit length for
the result to lie on the plane.

operator.operator.quat_from_euler.brief:
Converts Euler angles in degrees to a rotation, composed as `z * y * x` from the
rotations about each axis.

operator.operator.euler_from_quat.brief:
Converts a rotation to Euler angles in degrees, about the `x`, `y` and `z` axes. It
reads them back in the order `y * x * z`, so it reverses `quat_from_euler` when the
`z` angle is `0`. At an `x` angle near 90 or -90 degrees the `z` angle is `0`.

operator.operator.normalized_target_angl.brief:
Returns `target`, shifted by one full turn when that makes the turn from `original`
no more than 180 degrees, so an animation from `original` takes the short way round.

operator.operator.normalized_target_eule.brief:
Applies `normalized_target_angle` to each of the `x`, `y` and `z` angles, returning a
new vector.

operator.operator.clamp_angle.brief:
Brings an angle beyond 360 or -360 degrees back by one full turn, then clamps it
between `min` and `max`.

operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_SINE.brief: Sine ease-in-out: maps a progress from `0` to `1` to an eased progress from `0` to `1`.

operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_CUBIC.brief: Cubic ease-in-out: maps a progress from `0` to `1` to an eased progress from `0` to `1`.

operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_QUINT.brief:
Quintic ease-in-out: maps a progress from `0` to `1` to an eased progress from `0` to
`1`.

operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_CIRC.brief:
Circular ease-in-out: maps a progress from `0` to `1` to an eased progress from `0` to
`1`.

operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_QUAD.brief:
Quadratic ease-in-out: maps a progress from `0` to `1` to an eased progress from `0` to
`1`. It is the default `flight_look_easing`.

operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_QUART.brief:
Quartic ease-in-out: maps a progress from `0` to `1` to an eased progress from `0` to
`1`.

operator.operator.EASING_INOUT_EXPO.brief:
Exponential ease-in-out: maps a progress from `0` to `1` to an eased progress from `0`
to `1`.

operator.operator.get_active_operator.brief:
Returns the url of the active operator's game object, or `undefined` when no operator
is active.

operator.operator.set_debug.brief:
Turns debug mode on or off for every operator and checkpoint: on, they show their
camera and checkpoint meshes and draw the active bezier path.

operator.operator.is_debug.brief: Returns whether debug mode is on. Starts `false`.

operator.operator.camera_collisions_grou.brief:
The collision groups tested by the raycast from the operator anchor to the camera, so
the camera stays in front of obstacles. Read on every raycast. Starts as
`[hash("default")]`.

operator.operator.flight_bezier_samples_.brief:
The number of bezier segments an operator samples a flight path with, which sets how
accurate its uniform position is. Read each time an operator starts flying to the next
motion point. `16` is usually enough; starts at `32`.

operator.operator.flight_look_easing.brief:
The easing function that turns the camera between motion points, taking the progress
from `0` to `1` and returning the eased progress. Starts as `EASING_INOUT_QUAD`; any of
the `EASING_INOUT_*` functions, or a project's own, can replace it.

ink.Story.deserialize.brief:

light_and_shadows.light.brief:
The light sources manager. It keeps the list of point light sources and the camera
position, and each frame writes the sorted sources and the camera values into
`light_and_shadows.constants`. `light_setting.script` calls `set_color` and `update`,
and a scene controller calls `set_position` as its camera moves. Assigning a new value
to a field goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only.

light_and_shadows.light.set_color.brief:
Sets the base light uniform constants in `light_and_shadows.constants`. An omitted
value leaves its constant as it is. It also posts `clear_color` to `@render:` with
`clear_color`, or `fog_color` when that is omitted.

light_and_shadows.light.set_position.brief: Sets the camera rotation, the point the camera looks at, and the camera position.

light_and_shadows.light.reset.brief:
Clears the light sources sent to the shader and restores the module's default
ambient, fog color and fog constants.

light_and_shadows.light.update.brief:
Prepares the constants for the render script: updates each source's position and
spotlight direction from its game object, sorts the sources by distance from the
point the camera looks at into `light_and_shadows.constants.lights`, attenuates
their power, and copies the camera values. Call it from `update`.

light_and_shadows.light.list.brief: Every point light source, keyed by its game object id. `update` reads it every frame.

light_and_shadows.light.cam_look_at.brief: The point the camera looks at, set by `set_position`. Light sources are sorted by their distance from it.

light_and_shadows.light.cam_position.brief: The camera world position, set by `set_position`.

light_and_shadows.light.cam_view.brief: The camera rotation, set by `set_position`. A source with `rotate` set turns to it.

light_and_shadows.light.top_v.brief: The up vector, rotated by a game object's world rotation to give a spotlight's direction.

light_and_shadows.light.cam_z.brief: The camera Z coordinate, the distance from the focus point that depth of field needs. Set it here or with `set_position`'s `cam_z`.

light_and_shadows.light.attenuation_coef.brief: Divides a source's squared distance from the camera focus point before it scales the source's power.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.valu.brief: The color in `x`, `y`, `z`. `w` is the power `update` attenuates by distance; `bulb.script` sets it to `1 / power`.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.curr.brief: The color sent to the shader, its `w` attenuated by distance. `update` creates it from nothing when it is absent.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.posi.brief: The world position. `w` carries the spotlight smoothness, from `0` (soft) to `1` (hard).

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.dire.brief: The spotlight direction. `w` is the cone angle in radians; `0` or less turns the spotlight off.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.num.brief: A positive number keeps the source out of the distance sort and always visible; the default is `-1`.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.stat.brief: When `true`, `update` never reads the game object's world position again.
When `true`, `update` never reads the game object's rotation for the spotlight direction again.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.rota.brief: When `true`, `update` rotates the game object to the camera rotation, as a billboard.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.y_of.brief: Added to the world Y position each frame.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.id.brief: The game object id, as `bulb.script` stores it.

light_and_shadows.light.LightSource.time.brief: A timer `bulb.script` stores; `update` does not read it.

operator.bezier.brief:
Linear, quadratic and cubic bezier curves through vector or number points, with a
uniform position along the curve's length. The Operator camera moves along these
curves, and a project can use them for its own paths.

operator.bezier.new.brief:
Creates a bezier instance from 2 to 4 number points: 2 give a straight line, 3 a
quadratic curve and 4 a cubic curve. Any other count fails an assert. The default
length function is `vmath.length`, which rejects numbers, so a `length_func` such as
`math.abs` is required; the default lerp function, `vmath.lerp`, takes numbers.

operator.bezier.position.brief:
Returns the classic position along the curve at a progress. `time` is not clamped,
so a value outside `0` to `1` extrapolates.

operator.bezier.uniform_position.brief:
Returns the uniform position along the curve: the point at that fraction of the
curve's length. `time` is clamped between `0` and `1`, and the accuracy depends on
the `samples_count` given to `new`.

operator.bezier.Bezier.position.brief:
Returns the classic position along the curve at a progress. `time` is not clamped,
so a value outside `0` to `1` extrapolates.

operator.bezier.Bezier.uniform_position.brief:
Returns the uniform position along the curve: the point at that fraction of the
curve's length. `time` is clamped between `0` and `1`, and the accuracy depends on
the `samples_count` given to `new`.

sentinel.init.brief:
Starts the client. Call it as early as possible. Sentinel keeps the table it is
given, filling in defaults and its `tags` and `extra`; `set_tag` and `set_extra`
write into it.

sentinel.add_breadcrumb.brief:
Records something that happened, sent with every later event. Sentinel adds a
`timestamp` to the table and keeps the last 10. Does nothing before `init`.

sentinel.set_tag.brief: Sets a tag sent with every later event. Does nothing before `init`.

sentinel.set_extra.brief: Sets extra data sent with every later event. Does nothing before `init`.

sentinel.capture_exception.brief:
Sends an error to Sentry. With `config.set_error_handler` on, every uncaught error
is already sent through this. Raises before `init`. At most 10 events are sent per
300 seconds; a throttled event goes to `callback` as an error.

sentinel.capture_message.brief:
Sends a message to Sentry. Raises before `init`. At most 10 events are sent per
300 seconds; a throttled event goes to `callback` as an error.

sentinel.Config.dsn.brief:
Where events are sent. `init` asserts it is a string that parses as
`{PROTOCOL}://{PUBLIC_KEY}@{HOST}/{PATH}{PROJECT_ID}`.

sentinel.Config.debug.brief: Print what Sentinel sends. Defaults to `false`.

sentinel.Config.dry_run.brief: Build events without sending them; each callback receives the id `"(dry run)"`. Defaults to `false`.

sentinel.Config.gameanalytics.brief:
Also report each captured exception to GameAnalytics when that extension is
present. Every exception then needs a `traceback`, or `capture_exception` raises.
Defaults to `false`.

sentinel.Config.send_timeout.brief: HTTP request timeout in seconds. Defaults to `30`.

sentinel.Config.set_error_handler.brief:
Install a Lua error handler that captures every uncaught error. It takes the
single `sys.set_error_handler` slot, replacing any handler set before `init`.
Defaults to `true`.

sentinel.Config.load_previous_crash.brief: Submit the crash dump a previous session left, from inside `init`. Defaults to `true`.

sentinel.Config.release.brief: The release id sent with every event.

sentinel.Config.dist.brief: The distribution, to tell builds or deployment variants of one release apart.

sentinel.Config.environment.brief: A freeform environment name, e.g. `"staging"` or `"prod"`.

sentinel.Config.extra.brief: Extra data sent with every event.

sentinel.Config.user.brief:
User information sent with every event. The table is JSON-encoded and sent as
given, nested tables included.

sentinel.Config.on_soft_crash.brief:
Called after an uncaught error is captured; only installed with
`set_error_handler`. The first return value is concatenated into a log line, so
returning nothing raises inside the error handler.

sentinel.Config.on_hard_crash.brief:
Called from `init` after a previous session's crash dump is captured. The first
return value is concatenated into a log line, so returning nothing raises out of
`init`.

sentinel.CrashInfo.source.brief: `"lua"` or `"js"` for a soft crash, `"crash"` for a hard one.

sentinel.CrashInfo.message.brief: The error message. On a hard crash, the JSON-encoded crash dump extra data.

sentinel.CrashInfo.traceback.brief: The traceback. On a hard crash, the JSON-encoded crash dump backtrace.

sentinel.CrashInfo.fatal.brief: `true` on a hard crash, absent on a soft one.

sentinel.ExceptionInfo.traceback.brief: Sent as the exception value. Required when `config.gameanalytics` is on and the extension is present.

sentinel.ExceptionInfo.fatal.brief: Sends the event at level `"fatal"` instead of `"error"`.

sentinel.ExceptionInfo.tags.brief: Tags for this event, merged over the global ones.

sentinel.ExceptionInfo.extra.brief: Extra data for this event, merged over the global ones.

sentinel.ExceptionInfo.callback.brief:
Receives the event id on success, or the error when the request fails or the
event is throttled.

sentinel.MessageInfo.tags.brief: Tags for this event, merged over the global ones.

sentinel.MessageInfo.extra.brief: Extra data for this event, merged over the global ones.

sentinel.MessageInfo.callback.brief:
Receives the event id on success, or the error when the request fails or the
event is throttled.

flow.navigation.gui.brief: The gui_script adapter that renders the current Flow screen and animates transitions between screens.

flow.navigation.gui.new.brief:
Create a new GUI adapter instance bound to the given navigation router.
Registers listeners for "changed", "transition_begin", and "transition_complete"
so the adapter stays in sync with navigation state automatically.

flow.navigation.gui.destroy.brief:
Remove all navigation listeners and clean up the adapter.
Call this in gui_script final() to prevent leaking event handlers.

flow.navigation.gui.invalidate.brief: Invalidate the adapter so the next build_tree() call regenerates the tree.

flow.navigation.gui.needs_rebuild.brief: Return true when the adapter's tree needs to be rebuilt.

flow.navigation.gui.clear_rebuild_flag.brief: Clear the rebuild flag. Called after build_tree() has been invoked.

flow.navigation.gui.save_scroll_state.brief:
Save the current scroll offsets from a UI tree into the navigation params.
Typically called just before a tree rebuild so that scroll position is preserved.

flow.navigation.gui.build_tree.brief:
Build (or rebuild) the UI element tree for the current navigation state.
When a transition is active, renders both from and to trees and applies
_alpha or _offset_x according to the transition type and eased progress.

Transition types:
"fade" — cross-fade: from_tree._alpha fades out, to_tree._alpha fades in
"slide_left" — to slides in from the right: from moves left, to comes from right
"slide_right" — to slides in from the left: from moves right, to comes from left

Returns nil and clears adapter.tree when the stack is empty.

flow.navigation.gui.update.brief:
Advance the active transition by dt seconds.
Updates transition.progress and requests an adapter rebuild each frame.
When progress reaches 1.0, calls navigation.complete_transition() to
signal that the transition is done and clear the busy flag.

nakama.socket.on_channel_message.brief: Registers the function to call when a message arrives on a joined chat channel.

nakama.socket.CHANNELTYPE_DIRECT_MESSAGE.brief: A private channel for one-to-one chat.

wrap.gui_object.brief:
The base class of a GUI object: a part of a scene with its own hidden root box node, its
own child objects, and the props and settings it is created with. A game subclasses it
with `extend`, assigns hooks to the subclass, and creates instances with a scene's or
another object's `new_object`.

wrap.gui_object.new.brief: Returns a new, not yet set up instance of the base class.

wrap.gui_object.extend.brief:
Returns a new subclass: a table indexing the base class, with its own `new`. Assign
hooks such as `init` and `update` to it, and pass it to `new_object`. `P` and `S` type
the props and settings its instances are created with, and `F` the fields and methods
a game adds to it.

wrap.gui_object.__name.brief: The class name, the value `register_modal` reads to tell a class from a plain table.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.setup.brief:
Sets the object up in a scene and runs `init`. `new_object` calls it on each new
instance; a game does not.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.is_alive.brief:
Returns whether the object is set up and not deleted: `nil` until `setup` has run
`init`, so also during `init`, then `true` until `delete` makes it `false`.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.new_box.brief: Creates a box node under the object's root, from `wrap.node.Node.new_box`.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.new_text.brief: Creates a text node under the object's root, from `wrap.node.Node.new_text`.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.new_pie.brief: Creates a pie node under the object's root, from `wrap.node.Node.new_pie`.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.new_particlefx.brief: Creates a particle fx node under the object's root, from `wrap.node.Node.new_particlefx`.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.new_object.brief: Creates a child object whose class needs settings, as the first form does.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.init.brief: Runs once `setup` has created `root`, from `new_object`. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.update.brief: Runs each frame from `bg_update` while the object is alive. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.final.brief:
Runs once from `delete`, before the child objects and `root` are deleted. A no-op to
replace.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.on_input.brief: Runs from `bg_on_input` when no child object consumed the input. A no-op to replace.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.bg_update.brief:
Runs `update`, then each child object's `update`, unless the object is not alive.
The scene calls it each frame. At this tag it calls a child's `update` rather than
its `bg_update`, so a child's own children are not updated.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.delete.brief:
Deletes the object, unless it is not alive: marks it deleted, runs `final`, deletes
each child object, then deletes `root` and the nodes under it.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.bg_on_input.brief:
Offers input to each child object's `bg_on_input`, the newest first, then to
`on_input` if none consumed it. Returns `false` when the object is not alive.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.scene.brief: The scene the object was created in, set by `setup`.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.root.brief:
The object's root, a box node `setup` creates hidden under its scene's root. Every
node the `new_*` methods create is its child.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.props.brief: The props the object was created with, or `{}` when it was given none.

wrap.gui_object.GuiObject.settings.brief: The settings the object was created with, or `{}` when it was given none.

wrap.gui_applet.brief:
A GUI applet: a node that shows one scene at a time, playing the old scene's transition
out while the new one transitions in. A GUI script creates it with `new`, and calls its
`update`, `final`, `on_message` and `on_input` from its own, which drive the scenes.

wrap.gui_applet.new.brief:
Creates an applet on a node and shows a scene built from a plain table of hooks and
fields, copied onto a fresh `wrap.gui_scene.extend()`.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.register_scene.brief:
Registers a scene built from a plain table of hooks and fields, whose keys are copied
onto a fresh `wrap.gui_scene.extend()` once, at registration.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.unregister_sce.brief: Removes the scene registered under a name.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.show_scene.brief:
Shows a scene built from a plain table of hooks and fields, as the first form does.
The keys are copied onto a fresh `wrap.gui_scene.extend()`, which is the scene shown.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.get_size.brief: Returns the size of the applet's root node, from `wrap.node.Node.get_size`.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.update.brief:
Runs `bg_update` on the scene transitioning out, if any, then on the current scene.
Call it from the GUI script's `update`.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.final.brief: Finalizes the current scene with `bg_final`. Call it from the GUI script's `final`.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.on_message.brief:
Passes a message to the current scene's `bg_on_message`. Call it from the GUI
script's `on_message`.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.on_input.brief:
Passes input to the current scene's `bg_on_input`. Call it from the GUI script's
`on_input`, and return what it returns.

wrap.gui_applet.GuiApplet.root.brief: The wrapped node the applet was created on. Each scene's root is created under it.

asobi.http.brief:
The asobi REST transport. Each verb sends a JSON request to the client's server with its
access token, refreshes the token pair once and retries on a 401 outside `/auth/`, and
calls back with the decoded body or an error. A project reaches it as `client.http`, and
every `asobi.api.*` module sends through it.

asobi.http.get.brief: Sends a `GET` to the client's `base_url` plus `path`.

asobi.http.post.brief: Sends a `POST` with a JSON body to the client's `base_url` plus `path`.

asobi.http.put.brief: Sends a `PUT` with a JSON body to the client's `base_url` plus `path`.

asobi.http.delete.brief:
Sends a `DELETE` to the client's `base_url` plus `path`, with a JSON body when one is
given.

asobi.http._request.brief:
Internal. Sends one request and, on a 401 outside `/auth/` while the client holds a
refresh token, refreshes once and replays it: every verb calls it.

asobi.http._refresh_and_retry.brief:
Internal. Refreshes the token pair through `client.auth.refresh` and replays the request,
or calls back with `auth_expired`: `_request` calls it.

asobi.http._error.brief: Internal. Shapes a failed response's body into an `HttpError`: `_handle_response` calls it.

asobi.http._is_auth_path.brief: Internal. Whether a path is an `/auth/` route, which never refreshes: `_request` calls it.

asobi.http._headers.brief:
Internal. The JSON content type and, while the client holds an access token, its bearer
header: `_request` calls it.

asobi.http._urlencode.brief:
Internal. Url-encodes a value after `tostring`: `_build_url` and `asobi.api.auth`'s
`unlink_provider` call it.

asobi.http._build_url.brief: Internal. Joins the client's `base_url`, the path and the query string: every verb calls it.

asobi.http._handle_response.brief:
Internal. Decodes a response's body and calls back with it, or with an error for a status
of 400 or more or a body that is not JSON: `_request` calls it.

asobi.http.HttpError.status_code.brief: The HTTP status code, `401` when the token refresh after a 401 failed.

asobi.http.HttpError.error.brief:
The server's message, `HTTP <status>` when it sent none, `auth_expired` when the token
refresh after a 401 failed, or `invalid_response` when the body was not JSON.

asobi.http.HttpError.code.brief:
The server's machine-readable error code, empty when it sent none. Absent when the token
refresh after a 401 failed, and when the body was not JSON.

asobi.http.HttpError.details.brief: The details the server sent with the error.

asobi.http.HttpError.fields.brief: The per-field errors a form-validation route sends.

asobi.http.HttpError.raw.brief: The first 200 characters of a body that was not JSON.

crazygames.loading_stop.brief: The loadingStop() function has to be called when the loading is complete and eventually the gameplay starts.

crazygames.hide_invite_button.brief: Hide the invite button when it is no longer necessary.

crazygames.update_room.brief: Update the current multiplayer room. The table can contain roomId (string), isJoinable (boolean), and inviteParams (a table of string, number, or boolean values). Only supplied fields are updated.

crazygames.left_room.brief: Notify CrazyGames that the player has left the current multiplayer room.

crazygames.add_join_room_listener.brief: Register a listener for requests to join a multiplayer room. Registering again replaces the previous listener.

crazygames.remove_join_room_listener.brief: Remove the currently registered join-room listener.

crazygames.clear_data.brief: Remove all stored game data from the CrazyGames data module.

crazygames.get_item.brief: Get a stored value from the CrazyGames data module.

crazygames.remove_item.brief: Remove a stored value from the CrazyGames data module.

crazygames.set_item.brief: Store a value in the CrazyGames data module.

crazygames.get_system_info.brief: Get information about the user's locale, country, device, operating system, browser, and CrazyGames application type.

crazygames.list_friends.brief: Retrieve one page of the current user's CrazyGames friends. Only one list_friends request may be active at a time. The callback receives nil if the request fails.

crazygames.submit_score.brief: Submit an encrypted score and its plain numeric value to a CrazyGames leaderboard. Leaderboards must be enabled and configured for the game.

crazygames.is_user_account_available.brief: Before using any user account features, you should always ensure that the user account system is available.

crazygames.get_user.brief: Retrieve the user currently logged in CrazyGames. If the user is not logged in CrazyGames, the callback receives nil. Will call the provided callback with the logged in user account.

crazygames.get_user_token.brief: The user token is in JWT format and contains the userId of the player that is currently logged in to CrazyGames, as well as other useful information. crazygames.show_auth_prompt.brief: By calling this method, the log in or register popup will be displayed on CrazyGames. The user can log in their existing account, or create a new account. Will call the provided callback on log in.

crazygames.set_auth_listener.brief: You can register a user auth listener that is triggered when the player logs in to CrazyGames. A log out doesn't trigger the auth listener, since the entire page is refreshed when the player logs out.

crazygames.remove_auth_listener.brief: Remove any previously set auth listener.

crazygames.show_account_link_prompt.brief: Show an account linking prompt to link a CrazyGames account to the in-game account. Will call the provided callback with a response table containing either response = "yes" or response = "no". The response is nil if the prompt fails.

crypt.brief: Functions and constants for interacting with various hash and encode/decode algorithms

facebook.brief: Functions and constants for interacting with Facebook APIs

facebook.login_with_permissions.brief:
Login to Facebook and request a set of publish permissions.
The user is prompted to authorize the application using the login dialog of the specific platform. Even if the user is already logged in to Facebook this function can still be used to request additional publish permissions.
A comprehensive list of permissions can be found in the [Facebook permissions](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/permissions) documentation, as well as in their [guide to best practices for login management](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/best-practices).

facebook.login_with_tracking_preference.brief:
iOS ONLY. Login to Facebook and request a set of permissions. Allows developers to signal that a login is limited in terms of tracking users.
The user is prompted to authorize the application using the login dialog of the specific platform. Even if the user is already logged in to Facebook this function can still be used to request additional publish permissions.
A comprehensive list of permissions can be found in the [Facebook permissions](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/permissions) documentation, as well as in their [guide to best practices for login management](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/best-practices). For Limited Login the list of permissions can be found in the [Permissions in Limited Login](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/limited-login/permissions) documentation.

facebook.set_default_audience.brief:
iOS ONLY. The audience that should be able to see the publications. Should be called before `facebook.login_with_tracking_preference()`; Can be any of
- `facebook.AUDIENCE_NONE`
- `facebook.AUDIENCE_ONLYME`
- `facebook.AUDIENCE_FRIENDS`
- `facebook.AUDIENCE_EVERYONE`

facebook.get_current_authentication_toke.brief:
iOS ONLY. Get the current AuthenticationToken.
This function returns the currently stored authentication token after a previous successful login. If it returns nil no access token exists and you need to perform a login to get the wanted permissions.

facebook.get_current_profile.brief: iOS ONLY. Get the users [FBSDKProfile.currentProfile](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/limited-login/ios/). [Reading From Profile Helper Class](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/limited-login/permissions/profile-helper)

facebook.init.brief: Initialize Facebook SDK (if facebook.autoinit is 0 in game.project)

facebook.access_token.brief:
Get the current Facebook access token.
This function returns the currently stored access token after a previous successful login. If it returns nil no access token exists and you need to perform a login to get the wanted permissions.

facebook.permissions.brief:
Get the currently granted permissions.
This function returns a table with all the currently granted permission strings.

facebook.post_event.brief:
Post an event to Facebook Analytics
This function will post an event to Facebook Analytics where it can be used in the Facebook Insights system.

facebook.enable_event_usage.brief:
Enable event usage with Facebook Analytics This function will enable event usage for Facebook Analytics which means that Facebook will be able to use event data for ad-tracking.
Event usage cannot be controlled and is always enabled for the Facebook Canvas platform, therefore this function has no effect on Facebook Canvas.

facebook.disable_event_usage.brief:
Disable event usage with Facebook Analytics This function will disable event usage for Facebook Analytics which means that Facebook won't be able to use event data for ad-tracking. Events will still be sent to Facebook for insights.
Event usage cannot be controlled and is always enabled for the Facebook Canvas platform, therefore this function has no effect on Facebook Canvas.

facebook.enable_advertiser_tracking.brief: Enable advertiser tracking This function will set AdvertiserTrackingEnabled (the 'ATE' flag) to true on iOS, to inform Audience Network to use the data to deliver personalized ads for users on iOS 14 and above.

facebook.disable_advertiser_tracking.brief: Disable advertiser tracking This function will set AdvertiserTrackingEnabled (the 'ATE' flag) to false on iOS, to inform Audience Network not to use the data to deliver personalized ads for users on iOS 14 and above.

facebook.show_dialog.brief:
Show facebook web dialog
Display a Facebook web dialog of the type specified in the `dialog` parameter.

The `param` table should be set up according to the requirements of each dialog type. Note that some parameters are mandatory. Below is the list of available dialogs and where to find Facebook's developer documentation on parameters and response data.

`"apprequests"`
Shows a Game Request dialog. Game Requests allows players to invite their friends to play a game. Available parameters
- [type:string] `title`
- [type:string] `message`
- [type:number] `action_type`
- [type:number] `filters`
- [type:string] `data`
- [type:string] `object_id`
- [type:table] `suggestions`
- [type:table] `recipients`
- [type:string] `to`

On success, the "result" table parameter passed to the callback function will include the following fields
- [type:string] `request_id`
- [type:table] `to`

[Details for each parameter](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/games/services/gamerequests/v2.6#dialogparameters)

`"feed"`
The Feed Dialog allows people to publish individual stories to their timeline.

- [type:string] `caption`
- [type:string] `description`
- [type:string] `picture`
- [type:string] `link`
- [type:table] `people_ids`
- [type:string] `place_id`
- [type:string] `ref`

On success, the "result" table parameter passed to the callback function will include the following fields
- [type:string] `post_id`

[Details for each parameter](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/reference/feed-dialog/v2.6#params)

`"appinvite"`
The App Invite dialog is available only on iOS and Android. Note that the `url` parameter corresponds to the appLinkURL (iOS) and setAppLinkUrl (Android) properties.
- [type:string] `url`
- [type:string] `preview_image`
[Details for each parameter](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/reference/ios/current/class/FBSDKAppInviteContent)

facebook.EVENT_ACHIEVED_LEVEL.brief: Log this event when the user has achieved a level

facebook.EVENT_ADDED_PAYMENT_INFO.brief: Log this event when the user has entered their payment info

facebook.EVENT_ADDED_TO_CART.brief: Log this event when the user has added an item to their cart The value_to_sum passed to facebook.post_event should be the item's price.

facebook.EVENT_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST.brief: Log this event when the user has added an item to their wish list The value_to_sum passed to facebook.post_event should be the item's price.

facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_REGISTRATION.brief: Log this event when a user has completed registration with the app

facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_TUTORIAL.brief: Log this event when the user has completed a tutorial in the app

facebook.EVENT_INITIATED_CHECKOUT.brief: Log this event when the user has entered the checkout process The value_to_sum passed to facebook.post_event should be the total price in the cart.

facebook.EVENT_PURCHASED.brief: Log this event when the user has completed a purchase. The value_to_sum passed to facebook.post_event should be the numeric rating.

facebook.EVENT_RATED.brief: Log this event when the user has rated an item in the app

facebook.EVENT_SEARCHED.brief: Log this event when a user has performed a search within the app

facebook.EVENT_SPENT_CREDITS.brief: Log this event when the user has spent app credits The value_to_sum passed to facebook.post_event should be the number of credits spent.

facebook.EVENT_TIME_BETWEEN_SESSIONS.brief: Log this event when measuring the time between user sessions

facebook.EVENT_UNLOCKED_ACHIEVEMENT.brief: Log this event when the user has unlocked an achievement in the app

facebook.EVENT_VIEWED_CONTENT.brief: Log this event when a user has viewed a form of content in the app

facebook.PARAM_CONTENT_ID.brief:
Parameter key used to specify an ID for the content being logged about
The parameter key could be an EAN, article identifier, etc., depending on the nature of the app.

facebook.PARAM_CONTENT_TYPE.brief:
Parameter key used to specify a generic content type/family for the logged event
The key is an arbitrary type/family (e.g. "music", "photo", "video") depending on the nature of the app.

facebook.PARAM_CURRENCY.brief:
Parameter key used to specify currency used with logged event
Use a currency value key, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP" etc. See See ISO-4217 for specific values.

facebook.PARAM_DESCRIPTION.brief:
Parameter key used to specify a description appropriate to the event being logged
Use this for app specific event description, for instance the name of the achievement unlocked in the facebook.EVENT_UNLOCKED_ACHIEVEMENT event.

facebook.PARAM_LEVEL.brief: Parameter key used to specify the level achieved

facebook.PARAM_MAX_RATING_VALUE.brief:
Parameter key used to specify the maximum rating available
Set to specify the max rating available for the facebook.EVENT_RATED event. E.g., "5" or "10".

facebook.PARAM_NUM_ITEMS.brief:
Parameter key used to specify how many items are being processed
Set to specify the number of items being processed for an facebook.EVENT_INITIATED_CHECKOUT or facebook.EVENT_PURCHASED event.

facebook.PARAM_PAYMENT_INFO_AVAILABLE.brief:
Parameter key used to specify whether payment info is available
Set to specify if payment info is available for the facebook.EVENT_INITIATED_CHECKOUT event.

facebook.PARAM_REGISTRATION_METHOD.brief:
Parameter key used to specify method user has used to register for the app
Set to specify what registation method a user used for the app, e.g. "Facebook", "email", "Twitter", etc.

facebook.PARAM_SEARCH_STRING.brief:
Parameter key used to specify user search string
Set this to the the string that the user provided for a search operation.

facebook.PARAM_SOURCE_APPLICATION.brief: Parameter key used to specify source application package

facebook.PARAM_SUCCESS.brief:
Parameter key used to specify activity success
Set this key to indicate whether the activity being logged about was successful or not.

facebook.AUDIENCE_NONE.brief: Publish permission to reach no audience

facebook.AUDIENCE_ONLYME.brief: Publish permission to reach only me (private to current user)

facebook.AUDIENCE_FRIENDS.brief: Publish permission to reach user friends

gpgs.achievement_unlock.brief: Unlocks an achievement for the current player.

gpgs.achievement_set.brief: Sets an achievement to have at least the given number of steps completed.

gpgs.achievement_increment.brief: Increments an achievement by the given number of steps.

gpgs.achievement_get.brief:
Get information about all achievement's state asynchronously. Result return to callback previously set by `gpgs.set_callback` with `message_id == gpgs.MSG_GET_ACHIEVEMENTS`. Result is an array of JSON strings. Decode each string with `json.decode()` to get a table containing the following fields
- `id` - achievement id (from GP console)
- `name` - achievement name
- `description` - achievement description
- `xp` - how much experience points will be added when achievement will be unlocked
- `steps` - current step of incremental achievement
- `total_steps` - total amount of steps of incremental achievement
- `unlocked` - set to `true` if achievement is unlocked. Otherwise field is missed.
- `hidden` - set to `true if achievement is hidden. Otherwise field is missed.
- `revealed` - set to `true` if achievement is revealed. Otherwise field is missed.

gpgs.event_increment.brief: Increments an event specified by `eventId` by the given number of steps

gpgs.event_get.brief:
Get information about all events asynchronously. Result returns to callback previously set by `gpgs.set_callback` with `message_id == gpgs.MSG_GET_EVENTS`. Result is an array of JSON strings. Decode each string with `json.decode()` to get a table containing the following fields
- `id` - event id
- `formatted_value` - sum of all increments have been made to this event
- `value` - the number of increments this user has made to this event
- `description` - event's description
- `image` - URI that can be used to load the event's image icon
- `name` - event's name
- `visible` - whether the event should be displayed to the user in any event related UIs

iac.brief: Functions and constants for doing inter-app communication. Supported on iOS and Android.

iac.set_listener.brief: Sets the listener function for inter-app communication events.

iap.brief: Functions and constants for doing in-app purchases. Supported on iOS, Android (Google Play and Amazon) and Facebook Canvas platforms.

iap.finish.brief: Explicitly finish a product transaction. Calling iap.finish is required on a successful transaction if `auto_finish_transactions` is disabled in project settings. Calling this function with `auto_finish_transactions` set will be ignored and a warning is printed. The `transaction.state` field must equal `iap.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED`.

iap.acknowledge.brief: Acknowledge a transaction. Calling iap.acknowledge is required on a successful transaction on Google Play unless iap.finish is called. The transaction.state field must equal iap.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED.

iap.list.brief: Get a list of all avaliable iap products.

iap.set_listener.brief: Set the callback function to receive purchase transaction events.

iap.REASON_ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED.brief: the item is already owned by the user

iap.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASING.brief: transaction purchasing state This is an intermediate mode followed by TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED. Store provider support dependent.

iap.TRANS_STATE_RESTORED.brief: transaction restored state This is only available on store providers supporting restoring purchases.

iap.TRANS_STATE_UNVERIFIED.brief: transaction unverified state, requires verification of purchase

imgui.brief: Functions and constants for interacting with Dear ImGUI

imgui.begin_popup_context_item.brief:
BeginPopupContextItem.
If id is omitted, uses the last item ID (same as ImGui helper behavior). Lua - call with no arguments to use the last item; passing nil is not accepted.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_DEFAULTHIDE.brief: TABLECOLUMN_DEFAULTHIDE Default as a hidden/disabled column.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_DEFAULTSORT.brief: TABLECOLUMN_DEFAULTSORT Default as a sorting column.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_WIDTHSTRETCH.brief: TABLECOLUMN_WIDTHSTRETCH Column will stretch. Preferable with horizontal scrolling disabled (default if table sizing policy is _SizingStretchSame or _SizingStretchProp).

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_WIDTHFIXED.brief: TABLECOLUMN_WIDTHFIXED Column will not stretch. Preferable with horizontal scrolling enabled (default if table sizing policy is _SizingFixedFit and table is resizable).

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_NOREORDER.brief: TABLECOLUMN_NOREORDER Disable manual reordering this column, this will also prevent other columns from crossing over this column.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_NOHIDE.brief: TABLECOLUMN_NOHIDE Disable ability to hide/disable this column.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_NOCLIP.brief: TABLECOLUMN_NOCLIP Disable clipping for this column (all NoClip columns will render in a same draw command).

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_NOSORT.brief: TABLECOLUMN_NOSORT Disable ability to sort on this field (even if ImGuiTableFlags_Sortable is set on the table).

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_NOSORTASCENDING.brief: TABLECOLUMN_NOSORTASCENDING Disable ability to sort in the ascending direction.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_NOSORTDESCENDING.brief: TABLECOLUMN_NOSORTDESCENDING Disable ability to sort in the descending direction.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_NOHEADERWIDTH.brief: TABLECOLUMN_NOHEADERWIDTH Disable header text width contribution to automatic column width.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_PREFERSORTASCENDING.brief: TABLECOLUMN_PREFERSORTASCENDING Make the initial sort direction Ascending when first sorting on this column (default).

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_PREFERSORTDESCENDING.brief: TABLECOLUMN_PREFERSORTDESCENDING Make the initial sort direction Descending when first sorting on this column.

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_INDENTENABLE.brief: TABLECOLUMN_INDENTENABLE Use current Indent value when entering cell (default for column 0).

imgui.TABLECOLUMN_INDENTDISABLE.brief: TABLECOLUMN_INDENTDISABLE Ignore current Indent value when entering cell (default for columns > 0). Indentation changes _within_ the cell will still be honored.

imgui.TABLE_REORDERABLE.brief: TABLE_REORDERABLE Enable reordering columns in header row (need calling TableSetupColumn() + TableHeadersRow() to display headers)

imgui.TABLE_HIDEABLE.brief: TABLE_HIDEABLE Enable hiding/disabling columns in context menu.

imgui.TABLE_SORTABLE.brief: TABLE_SORTABLE Enable sorting. Call TableGetSortSpecs() to obtain sort specs. Also see ImGuiTableFlags_SortMulti and ImGuiTableFlags_SortTristate.

imgui.TABLE_NOSAVEDSETTINGS.brief: TABLE_NOSAVEDSETTINGS Disable persisting columns order, width and sort settings in the .ini file.

imgui.TABLE_CONTEXTMENUINBODY.brief: TABLE_CONTEXTMENUINBODY Right-click on columns body/contents will display table context menu. By default it is available in TableHeadersRow().

imgui.TABLE_ROWBG.brief: TABLE_ROWBG Set each RowBg color with ImGuiCol_TableRowBg or ImGuiCol_TableRowBgAlt (equivalent of calling TableSetBgColor with ImGuiTableBgFlags_RowBg0 on each row manually)

imgui.TABLE_BORDERSINNERH.brief: TABLE_BORDERSINNERH Draw horizontal borders between rows.

imgui.TABLE_BORDERSOUTERH.brief: TABLE_BORDERSOUTERH Draw horizontal borders at the top and bottom.

imgui.TABLE_BORDERSINNERV.brief: TABLE_BORDERSINNERV Draw vertical borders between columns.

imgui.TABLE_BORDERSOUTERV.brief: TABLE_BORDERSOUTERV Draw vertical borders on the left and right sides.

imgui.TABLE_NOBORDERSINBODY.brief: TABLE_NOBORDERSINBODY [ALPHA] Disable vertical borders in columns Body (borders will always appears in Headers). -> May move to style

imgui.TABLE_NOBORDERSINBODYUNTILRESIZE.brief: TABLE_NOBORDERSINBODYUNTILRESIZE [ALPHA] Disable vertical borders in columns Body until hovered for resize (borders will always appears in Headers). -> May move to style

imgui.TABLE_SIZINGFIXEDFIT.brief: TABLE_SIZINGFIXEDFIT Columns default to _WidthFixed or _WidthAuto (if resizable or not resizable), matching contents width.

imgui.TABLE_SIZINGFIXEDSAME.brief: TABLE_SIZINGFIXEDSAME Columns default to _WidthFixed or _WidthAuto (if resizable or not resizable), matching the maximum contents width of all columns. Implicitly enable ImGuiTableFlags_NoKeepColumnsVisible.

imgui.TABLE_SIZINGSTRETCHPROP.brief: TABLE_SIZINGSTRETCHPROP Columns default to _WidthStretch with default weights proportional to each columns contents widths.

imgui.TABLE_SIZINGSTRETCHSAME.brief: TABLE_SIZINGSTRETCHSAME Columns default to _WidthStretch with default weights all equal, unless overriden by TableSetupColumn().

imgui.TABLE_NOHOSTEXTENDX.brief: TABLE_NOHOSTEXTENDX Make outer width auto-fit to columns, overriding outer_size.x value. Only available when ScrollX/ScrollY are disabled and Stretch columns are not used.

imgui.TABLE_NOHOSTEXTENDY.brief: TABLE_NOHOSTEXTENDY Make outer height stop exactly at outer_size.y (prevent auto-extending table past the limit). Only available when ScrollX/ScrollY are disabled. Data below the limit will be clipped and not visible.

imgui.TABLE_NOKEEPCOLUMNSVISIBLE.brief: TABLE_NOKEEPCOLUMNSVISIBLE Disable keeping column always minimally visible when ScrollX is off and table gets too small. Not recommended if columns are resizable.

imgui.TABLE_PRECISEWIDTHS.brief: TABLE_PRECISEWIDTHS Disable distributing remainder width to stretched columns (width allocation on a 100-wide table with 3 columns: Without this flag: 33,33,34. With this flag: 33,33,33). With larger number of columns, resizing will appear to be less smooth.

imgui.TABLE_NOCLIP.brief: TABLE_NOCLIP Disable clipping rectangle for every individual columns (reduce draw command count, items will be able to overflow into other columns). Generally incompatible with TableSetupScrollFreeze().

imgui.TABLE_PADOUTERX.brief: TABLE_PADOUTERX Default if BordersOuterV is on. Enable outer-most padding. Generally desirable if you have headers.

imgui.TABLE_NOPADOUTERX.brief: TABLE_NOPADOUTERX Default if BordersOuterV is off. Disable outer-most padding.

imgui.TABLE_NOPADINNERX.brief: TABLE_NOPADINNERX Disable inner padding between columns (double inner padding if BordersOuterV is on, single inner padding if BordersOuterV is off).

imgui.TABLE_SCROLLX.brief: TABLE_SCROLLX Enable horizontal scrolling. Require 'outer_size' parameter of BeginTable() to specify the container size. Changes default sizing policy. Because this create a child window, ScrollY is currently generally recommended when using ScrollX.

imgui.TABLE_SCROLLY.brief: TABLE_SCROLLY Enable vertical scrolling. Require 'outer_size' parameter of BeginTable() to specify the container size.

imgui.TABLE_SORTMULTI.brief: TABLE_SORTMULTI Hold shift when clicking headers to sort on multiple column. TableGetSortSpecs() may return specs where (SpecsCount > 1).

imgui.TABLE_SORTTRISTATE.brief: TABLE_SORTTRISTATE Allow no sorting, disable default sorting. TableGetSortSpecs() may return specs where (SpecsCount == 0).

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NORESIZE.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NORESIZE Disable user resizing with the lower-right grip

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOMOVE.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOMOVE Disable user moving the window

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOSCROLLBAR.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOSCROLLBAR Disable scrollbars (window can still scroll with mouse or programmatically)

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOSCROLLWITHMOUSE.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOSCROLLWITHMOUSE Disable user vertically scrolling with mouse wheel. On child window, mouse wheel will be forwarded to the parent unless NoScrollbar is also set.

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOCOLLAPSE.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOCOLLAPSE Disable user collapsing window by double-clicking on it

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_ALWAYSAUTORESIZE.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_ALWAYSAUTORESIZE Resize every window to its content every frame

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOBACKGROUND.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOBACKGROUND Disable drawing background color (WindowBg, etc.) and outside border. Similar as using SetNextWindowBgAlpha(0.0f).

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOSAVEDSETTINGS.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOSAVEDSETTINGS Never load/save settings in .ini file

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOMOUSEINPUTS.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOMOUSEINPUTS Disable catching mouse, hovering test with pass through.

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_HORIZONTALSCROLLBAR.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_HORIZONTALSCROLLBAR prior to calling Begin() to specify width. Read code in imgui_demo in the "Horizontal Scrolling" section.

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOFOCUSONAPPEARING.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOFOCUSONAPPEARING Disable taking focus when transitioning from hidden to visible state

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NOBRINGTOFRONTONFOCUS.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NOBRINGTOFRONTONFOCUS Disable bringing window to front when taking focus (e.g. clicking on it or programmatically giving it focus)

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_ALWAYSVERTICALSCROLLBA.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_ALWAYSVERTICALSCROLLBAR Always show vertical scrollbar (even if ContentSize.y < Size.y)

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_ALWAYSHORIZONTALSCROLL.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_ALWAYSHORIZONTALSCROLLBAR Always show horizontal scrollbar (even if ContentSize.x < Size.x)

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_ALWAYSUSEWINDOWPADDING.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_ALWAYSUSEWINDOWPADDING Ensure child windows without border uses style.WindowPadding (ignored by default for non-bordered child windows, because more convenient)

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NONAVINPUTS.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NONAVINPUTS No gamepad/keyboard navigation within the window

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_NONAVFOCUS.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_NONAVFOCUS No focusing toward this window with gamepad/keyboard navigation (e.g. skipped by CTRL+TAB)

imgui.WINDOWFLAGS_UNSAVEDDOCUMENT.brief: WINDOWFLAGS_UNSAVEDDOCUMENT Append '*' to title without affecting the ID, as a convenience to avoid using the ### operator. When used in a tab/docking context, tab is selected on closure and closure is deferred by one frame to allow code to cancel the closure (with a confirmation popup, etc.) without flicker.

imgui.POPUPFLAGS_MOUSEBUTTONLEFT.brief: POPUPFLAGS_MOUSEBUTTONLEFT // For BeginPopupContext*(): open on Left Mouse release. Guaranteed to always be == 0 (same as ImGuiMouseButton_Left)

imgui.POPUPFLAGS_MOUSEBUTTONRIGHT.brief: POPUPFLAGS_MOUSEBUTTONRIGHT // For BeginPopupContext*(): open on Right Mouse release. Guaranteed to always be == 1 (same as ImGuiMouseButton_Right)

imgui.POPUPFLAGS_MOUSEBUTTONMIDDLE.brief: POPUPFLAGS_MOUSEBUTTONMIDDLE // For BeginPopupContext*(): open on Middle Mouse release. Guaranteed to always be == 2 (same as ImGuiMouseButton_Middle)

imgui.POPUPFLAGS_NOOPENOVEREXISTINGPOPUP.brief: POPUPFLAGS_NOOPENOVEREXISTINGPOPUP For OpenPopup*(), BeginPopupContext*(): don't open if there's already a popup at the same level of the popup stack

imgui.POPUPFLAGS_NOOPENOVERITEMS.brief: POPUPFLAGS_NOOPENOVERITEMS For BeginPopupContextWindow(): don't return true when hovering items, only when hovering empty space

imgui.POPUPFLAGS_ANYPOPUPID.brief: POPUPFLAGS_ANYPOPUPID For IsPopupOpen(): ignore the ImGuiID parameter and test for any popup.

imgui.POPUPFLAGS_ANYPOPUPLEVEL.brief: POPUPFLAGS_ANYPOPUPLEVEL For IsPopupOpen(): search/test at any level of the popup stack (default test in the current level)

imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOPREVIEWTOOLTIP.brief: DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOPREVIEWTOOLTIP By default, a successful call to BeginDragDropSource opens a tooltip so you can display a preview or description of the source contents. This flag disable this behavior.

imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENODISABLEHOVER.brief: DROPFLAGS_SOURCENODISABLEHOVER By default, when dragging we clear data so that IsItemHovered() will return false, to avoid subsequent user code submitting tooltips. This flag disable this behavior so you can still call IsItemHovered() on the source item.

imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOHOLDTOOPENOTHERS.brief: DROPFLAGS_SOURCENOHOLDTOOPENOTHERS Disable the behavior that allows to open tree nodes and collapsing header by holding over them while dragging a source item.

imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEALLOWNULLID.brief: DROPFLAGS_SOURCEALLOWNULLID Allow items such as Text(), Image() that have no unique identifier to be used as drag source, by manufacturing a temporary identifier based on their window-relative position. This is extremely unusual within the dear imgui ecosystem and so we made it explicit.

imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEEXTERN.brief: DROPFLAGS_SOURCEEXTERN External source (from outside of dear imgui), won't attempt to read current item/window info. Will always return true. Only one Extern source can be active simultaneously.

imgui.DROPFLAGS_SOURCEAUTOEXPIREPAYLOAD.brief: DROPFLAGS_SOURCEAUTOEXPIREPAYLOAD Automatically expire the payload if the source cease to be submitted (otherwise payloads are persisting while being dragged)

imgui.DROPFLAGS_ACCEPTBEFOREDELIVERY.brief: DROPFLAGS_ACCEPTBEFOREDELIVERY AcceptDragDropPayload() will returns true even before the mouse button is released. You can then call IsDelivery() to test if the payload needs to be delivered.

imgui.DROPFLAGS_ACCEPTNODRAWDEFAULTRECT.brief: DROPFLAGS_ACCEPTNODRAWDEFAULTRECT Do not draw the default highlight rectangle when hovering over target.

imgui.DROPFLAGS_ACCEPTNOPREVIEWTOOLTIP.brief: DROPFLAGS_ACCEPTNOPREVIEWTOOLTIP Request hiding the BeginDragDropSource tooltip from the BeginDragDropTarget site.

imgui.DROPFLAGS_ACCEPTPEEKONLY.brief: DROPFLAGS_ACCEPTPEEKONLY For peeking ahead and inspecting the payload before delivery.

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_AUTOSELECTALL.brief: INPUTFLAGS_AUTOSELECTALL Select entire text when first taking mouse focus

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_ENTERRETURNSTRUE.brief: INPUTFLAGS_ENTERRETURNSTRUE Return 'true' when Enter is pressed (as opposed to every time the value was modified). Consider looking at the IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit() function.

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKCOMPLETION.brief: INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKCOMPLETION Callback on pressing TAB (for completion handling)

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKHISTORY.brief: INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKHISTORY Callback on pressing Up/Down arrows (for history handling)

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKALWAYS.brief: INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKALWAYS Callback on each iteration. User code may query cursor position, modify text buffer.

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKCHARFILTER.brief: INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKCHARFILTER Callback on character inputs to replace or discard them. Modify 'EventChar' to replace or discard, or return 1 in callback to discard.

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_ALLOWTABINPUT.brief: INPUTFLAGS_ALLOWTABINPUT Pressing TAB input a '\t' character into the text field

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_CTRLENTERFORNEWLINE.brief: INPUTFLAGS_CTRLENTERFORNEWLINE In multi-line mode, unfocus with Enter, add new line with Ctrl+Enter (default is opposite: unfocus with Ctrl+Enter, add line with Enter).

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_NOHORIZONTALSCROLL.brief: INPUTFLAGS_NOHORIZONTALSCROLL Disable following the cursor horizontally

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_PASSWORD.brief: INPUTFLAGS_PASSWORD Password mode, display all characters as '*'

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_NOUNDOREDO.brief: INPUTFLAGS_NOUNDOREDO Disable undo/redo. Note that input text owns the text data while active, if you want to provide your own undo/redo stack you need e.g. to call ClearActiveID().

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKRESIZE.brief: INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKRESIZE Callback on buffer capacity changes request (beyond 'buf_size' parameter value), allowing the string to grow. Notify when the string wants to be resized (for string types which hold a cache of their Size). You will be provided a new BufSize in the callback and NEED to honor it. (see misc/cpp/imgui_stdlib.h for an example of using this)

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKEDIT.brief: INPUTFLAGS_CALLBACKEDIT Callback on any edit (note that InputText() already returns true on edit, the callback is useful mainly to manipulate the underlying buffer while focus is active)

imgui.INPUTFLAGS_ESCAPECLEARSALL.brief: INPUTFLAGS_ESCAPECLEARSALL Callback on any edit (note that InputText() already returns true on edit, the callback is useful mainly to manipulate the underlying buffer while focus is active)

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NOPICKER.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NOPICKER // ColorEdit: disable picker when clicking on color square.

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NOOPTIONS.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NOOPTIONS // ColorEdit: disable toggling options menu when right-clicking on inputs/small preview.

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NOSMALLPREVIEW.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NOSMALLPREVIEW // ColorEdit, ColorPicker: disable color square preview next to the inputs. (e.g. to show only the inputs)

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NOINPUTS.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NOINPUTS // ColorEdit, ColorPicker: disable inputs sliders/text widgets (e.g. to show only the small preview color square).

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NOTOOLTIP.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NOTOOLTIP // ColorEdit, ColorPicker, ColorButton: disable tooltip when hovering the preview.

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NOLABEL.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NOLABEL // ColorEdit, ColorPicker: disable display of inline text label (the label is still forwarded to the tooltip and picker).

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NOSIDEPREVIEW.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NOSIDEPREVIEW // ColorPicker: disable bigger color preview on right side of the picker, use small color square preview instead.

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NODRAGDROP.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NODRAGDROP // ColorEdit: disable drag and drop target. ColorButton: disable drag and drop source.

imgui.COLOREDITFLAGS_NOBORDER.brief: COLOREDITFLAGS_NOBORDER // ColorButton: disable border (which is enforced by default)

kaiads.set_listener.brief: Listen to events from the KaiAds SDK.

kaiads.show.brief: Show an ad. You must have called preload() and received a callback that the ad was preloaded before attempting to show an ad.

kaiads.PRELOAD_ERROR.brief: Event sent when an error occurred while trying to preload an ad

kaiads.PRELOAD_OK.brief: Event sent when an ad was successfully preloaded

levelplay.brief: Functions and constants for Unity LevelPlay mediation on Android and iOS.

levelplay.set_callback.brief: Sets the callback used for all LevelPlay events. Pass nil to remove it.

levelplay.init.brief: Initializes LevelPlay. Configure privacy before calling this function. Create ad objects only after EVENT_INIT_SUCCEEDED.

levelplay.get_sdk_version.brief: Returns the native LevelPlay SDK version.

levelplay.set_gdpr_consent.brief: Passes the user's GDPR consent choice to LevelPlay and supported mediated networks. It does not display a consent form or read another extension's private state. For a custom or non-compatible CMP, call it before init with the collected choice. LevelPlay SDK 7.7.0 and newer automatically reads Google UMP and compatible Google Additional Consent signals, so do not also pass the same choice with this function in that setup.

levelplay.set_ccpa.brief: Passes a US privacy "do not sell or share" choice. True means the user opted out. Call before init.

levelplay.set_coppa.brief: Sets whether the user is child-directed for COPPA treatment. True flags the user as child-directed. Call before init.

levelplay.set_metadata.brief: Sets an SDK or mediated-network metadata value. Set network-required values before init.

levelplay.set_meta_limited_data_use.brief: Configures Meta Audience Network Limited Data Use before init. This calls Meta's SDK directly and returns false if the Meta adapter is not linked or initialization already started.

levelplay.set_meta_advertiser_tracking.brief: Sets Meta Audience Network's iOS advertiser-tracking flag before init. Returns false on Android, when Meta is not linked, or after initialization starts.

levelplay.set_dynamic_user_id.brief: Sets the dynamic user ID used by server-to-server rewarded callbacks. The value must contain 1–64 alphanumeric characters. Call before showing the rewarded ad it should apply to.

levelplay.set_adapters_debug.brief: Enables or disables mediated-network debug logging. Disable it in production.

levelplay.validate_integration.brief: Runs the native LevelPlay integration validator.

levelplay.launch_test_suite.brief: Opens the LevelPlay integration test suite after initialization succeeds. Enable the is_test_suite metadata before init and call this before creating ad objects or invoking other LevelPlay SDK operations.

levelplay.request_tracking_authorization.brief: Requests App Tracking Transparency authorization on iOS 14 or newer. Request it before init when mediation partners should receive the IDFA. The result is sent through MSG_TRACKING. It is a no-op on Android and unsupported iOS versions.

levelplay.get_tracking_authorization_sta.brief: Returns the current App Tracking Transparency state on iOS, or nil when unsupported.

levelplay.create_interstitial_ad.brief: Creates a reusable interstitial ad object after successful initialization. Its ad-unit ID and optional bid floor are fixed for the object's lifetime. Create it once, then use the returned handle for multiple load/show cycles with the same ad-unit ID and creation configuration.

levelplay.destroy_interstitial_ad.brief: Permanently releases an interstitial ad object, invalidates its handle, and stops callbacks for it. Do not destroy between ordinary impressions or during load/display when terminal callbacks are still required.

levelplay.destroy_rewarded_ad.brief: Permanently releases a rewarded ad object, invalidates its handle, and stops callbacks for it. Do not destroy between ordinary impressions, and never destroy a displayed rewarded ad before its reward and close callbacks are received.

levelplay.load_rewarded_ad.brief: Loads the next rewarded impression into an existing object. After reward and close callbacks complete, call this again on the same handle instead of creating another object.

levelplay.is_rewarded_ad_ready.brief: Returns whether the rewarded object has an ad ready to display.

levelplay.show_rewarded_ad.brief: Shows one loaded rewarded impression. The optional placement is a dashboard presentation point, not an ad object, and can be selected separately on every show.

levelplay.is_rewarded_placement_capped.brief: Returns whether the named rewarded placement has reached its configured cap.

levelplay.get_reward.brief: Returns the configured reward for the object's default placement or for the supplied placement.

pad.get_pack_state.brief: Requests download state and details for the specified asset pack. This is an asynchronous function and will send a `PACK_STATE_UPDATED` event once the new state is available.

pad.get_pack_location.brief: Returns the location of the specified asset pack on the device or an empty string if this pack is not downloaded.

pad.get_pack_bytes_downloaded.brief: Returns the total number of bytes already downloaded for the pack. Note that you must have called the `get_pack_state()` function first and wait for a `PACK_STATE_UPDATED` event before calling this function.

pad.get_pack_error_code.brief: Returns the error code for the pack, if Play has failed to download the pack. Note that you must have called the `get_pack_state()` function first and wait for a `PACK_STATE_UPDATED` event before calling this function.

pad.get_pack_status.brief: Returns the download status of the pack. Note that you must have called the `get_pack_state()` function first and wait for a `PACK_STATE_UPDATED` event before calling this function.

pad.get_pack_total_bytes_to_download.brief: Returns the total size of the pack in bytes. Note that you must have called the `get_pack_state()` function first and wait for a `PACK_STATE_UPDATED` event before calling this function.

pad.get_pack_transfer_progress_percentag.brief: Returns the percentage of the asset pack already transferred to the app. Note that you must have called the `get_pack_state()` function first and wait for a `PACK_STATE_UPDATED` event before calling this function.

pad.show_confirmation_dialog.brief: Shows a dialog that asks the user for consent to download packs Shows a dialog that asks the user for consent to download packs that are currently in either the AssetPackStatus.REQUIRES_USER_CONFIRMATION state or the AssetPackStatus.WAITING_FOR_WIFI state. pad.ERRORCODE_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE.brief: Asset pack download failed due to insufficient storage.

pad.ERRORCODE_INTERNAL_ERROR.brief: Unknown error downloading an asset pack.

pad.ERRORCODE_NETWORK_UNRESTRICTED.brief: Returned if AssetPackManager.showCellularDataConfirmation(Activity) is called but no asset packs are waiting for Wi-Fi.

pad.ERRORCODE_PACK_UNAVAILABLE.brief: The requested asset pack isn't available.

pad.ERRORCODE_PLAY_STORE_NOT_FOUND.brief: The Play Store app is either not installed or not the official version.

pad.ERRORCODE_UNRECOGNIZED_INSTALLATION.brief: The installed app version is not recognized by Play.

IP addresses can be in IPv4 or IPv6 format - auth_data Sets the HTTP POST data, that will be forwarded to the authentication service, to the provided data. - auth_parameters The HTTP GET parameters that will be forwarded to the authentication service to the provided parameters. - auth_type The type of the "Custom Authentication" service that will be used. See AUTH_* enums

Local game_id = "1234" local room_options = { is_visible = false, is_open = false, supress_room_events = false, max_players = 4, player_ttl = 0, empty_room_ttl = 0, lobby_type = realtime.LOBBYTYPE_DEFAULT, lobby_name = "", publish_user_id = "", direct_mode = realtime.DIRECTMODE_NONE, props_listed_in_lobby = {}, custom_room_properties = {}, } local join_options = { custom_room_properties = {}, max_players = 0, matchmaking_mode = realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_FILL_ROOM, lobby_name = "", lobby_type = realtime.LOBBYTYPE_DEFAULT, sql_lobby_filter = "", expected_users = {}, }

realtime.AUTH_STEAM.brief: Authenticates users by their Steam Account. Pass L"ticket=[ticket]" to setParameters().

realtime.AUTH_FACEBOOK.brief: Authenticates users by their Facebook Account. Pass L"token=[token]" to setParameters().

realtime.AUTH_OCULUS.brief: Authenticates users by their Oculus Account. Pass L"userid=[userid]&nonce=[nonce]" to setParameters().

realtime.AUTH_PLAYSTATION_4.brief: Authenticates users by their PSN Account. Pass L"token=[token]&env=[env]&userName=[userName]" to setParameters().

realtime.AUTH_XBOX.brief: Authenticates users by their XBox Network Account. Pass the XSTS token to setData().

realtime.AUTH_VIVEPORT.brief: Authenticates users by their HTC Viveport Account and user token. Pass L"userToken=[userToken]" to setParameters().

realtime.AUTH_NINTENDO_SWITCH.brief: Authenticates users by their Nintendo Account. Pass L"token=[token]&appversion=[appversion]" to setParameters(). The appversion is optional.

realtime.AUTH_PLAYSTATION_5.brief: Authenticates users by their PSN Account. Pass L"token=[token]&env=[env]&userName=[userName]" to setParameters().

realtime.AUTH_EPIC.brief: Authenticates users by their Epic Online Services (EOS) Account. Pass L"token=[token]&ownershipToken=[ownershipToken]" to setParameters(). The ownershipToken is optional.

realtime.AUTH_FACEBOOK_GAMING.brief: Authenticates users by their Facebook Account. Pass L"token=[token]" to setParameters().

realtime.SERVER_TYPE_NAME_SERVER.brief: Photon Cloud and for self-hosted Photon 5 or higher Server instances

realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_FILL_ROOM.brief: Fills up rooms (oldest first) to get players together as fast as possible. Default. Makes most sense with MaxPlayers > 0 and games that can only start with more players.

realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_SERIAL_MATCHING.brief: Distributes players across available rooms sequentially but takes filters into account. Without filters, rooms get players evenly distributed.

realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_RANDOM_MATCHING.brief: Joins a (fully) random room. Expected properties must match, but aside from this, any available room might be selected.

realtime.LOBBYTYPE_DEFAULT.brief: This lobby type is used unless another lobby type is specified. Room lists will be sent and Client::opJoinRandomRoom() can filter by matching properties.

realtime.LOBBYTYPE_SQL_LOBBY.brief: This lobby type lists rooms like type DEFAULT but SQL-like "where" clauses for filtering can be used with Client::opJoinRandomRoom(). This allows 'bigger', 'less', 'or' and 'and' combinations.

realtime.LOBBYTYPE_ASYNC_RANDOM_LOBBY.brief: This lobby does not send room lists. It is only used for Client::opJoinRandomRoom(). It keeps rooms available for matchmaking for a while even when there are only inactive users left.

realtime.DIRECTMODE_NONE.brief: Do not create any 2p2 connections between the clients. This is the default.

realtime.DIRECTMODE_ALL_TO_OTHERS.brief: Each client establishes a direct connection with every other client inside the room.

realtime.DIRECTMODE_MASTER_TO_OTHERS.brief: The master client establishes a direct connection with every other client inside the room. All other clients only establish a direct connection with the master client but not with each other.

realtime.DIRECTMODE_ALL_TO_ALL.brief: Each client establishes a direct connection with every client inside the room, including itself.

realtime.DIRECTMODE_MASTER_TO_ALL.brief: The master client establishes a direct connection with every client inside the room, including itself. All other clients only establish a direct connection with the master client but not with each other.

playables.brief: Functions for interacting with the YouTube Playables SDK.

playables.is_in_playables_env.brief: Returns whether the SDK reports that the game is running in the Playables environment. Returns false if the SDK is not loaded.

playables.get_sdk_version.brief: Returns the loaded YouTube Playables SDK version, or nil if it is unavailable.

playables.game_ready.brief: Notifies YouTube that the loading screen is gone and the game is ready for players to interact with. The extension automatically calls firstFrameReady() during initialization.

playables.load_data.brief: Loads serialized game data from YouTube. Only one load request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another load_data() request.

playables.save_data.brief: Saves valid UTF-8 text to YouTube, with a maximum size of 3 MiB. Invalid UTF-8 returns false and an error through the callback before the SDK is called. Base64-encode binary data such as sys.serialize() output before saving. Only one save request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another save_data() request.

playables.is_audio_enabled.brief: Returns whether game audio is enabled in the player's YouTube settings. Use this to initialize the game audio state.

playables.on_audio_enabled_change.brief: Registers a callback for YouTube audio-setting changes. Before the callback runs, the extension automatically mutes the master sound group when audio is disabled, or unmutes it when audio is enabled and the game is not paused. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback.

playables.on_pause.brief: Registers a callback for YouTube pause events. The extension automatically mutes the master sound group before the callback runs. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback. A paused game is not guaranteed to resume.

playables.on_resume.brief: Registers a callback for YouTube resume events. Before the callback runs, the extension automatically unmutes the master sound group if YouTube audio is enabled, or keeps it muted if audio is disabled. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback.

playables.get_language.brief: Gets the language in the player's YouTube settings as a BCP-47 language tag. Only one request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another get_language() request.

playables.send_score.brief: Sends an integer score to YouTube. Use one consistent score dimension across the game. Only one request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another send_score() request.

playables.open_yt_content.brief: Requests that YouTube open a video or another Playable. The content type is optional and defaults to CONTENT_TYPE_VIDEO. Only one request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another open_yt_content() request.

playables.request_interstitial_ad.brief: Requests an interstitial ad. Success does not guarantee that an ad was shown. Do not use this API to grant rewards. Only one interstitial request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another request_interstitial_ad() request. Keep handling YouTube audio, pause, and resume events during ads.

playables.request_rewarded_ad.brief: Requests a rewarded ad. Grant a reward only when reward_earned is true. Only one rewarded request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another request_rewarded_ad() request. Keep handling YouTube audio, pause, and resume events during ads.

playables.log_error.brief: Reports an error occurrence to YouTube. Takes no arguments and returns no value. Reporting is best-effort and rate-limited, so delivery is not guaranteed.

playables.log_warning.brief: Reports a warning occurrence to YouTube. Takes no arguments and returns no value. Reporting is best-effort and rate-limited, so delivery is not guaranteed.
