daabbcc.UPDATE_PARTIALREBUILD.brief: Partial rebuild. Recommended for lots of moving AABBs.

daabbcc.BitsHit.category_bits.brief: The category bits the AABB was inserted with.

daabbcc.SortedHit.distance.brief: Distance from the query or ray origin.

fontscale.brief: Reads the operating system's font-scale (text size) setting.

fontscale.get.brief: Returns the OS font-scale factor, where `1` is the default text size.

ainpc.brief: AI NPCs for Defold through the Player2 desktop app: chat completions, spawned NPCs to talk to, and a stream of their responses.

ainpc.chat_completion.brief:
Requests a chat completion. A string is sent as one user message: the
extension pastes it into `{"messages":[{"content":"<text>","role":"user"}]}`
without escaping, so text holding a quote, a backslash or a newline makes
invalid JSON. Pass a body with a `messages` list to send arbitrary text.

ainpc.npc_spawn.brief: Spawns an NPC from a body given as a table or as JSON text.

ainpc.npc_chat.brief: Sends a message to a spawned NPC, given as a body or as text.

ainpc.npc_responses.brief: Opens the stream of NPC responses for a game.

ainpc.stop_npc_responses.brief:
Stops a stream opened by {@link ainpc.npc_responses}. An id that names
no open stream is ignored.

openal.brief: 3D positional audio for Defold through OpenAL: WAV sound sources with position, pitch, gain and looping, heard from one listener.

openal.init.brief:
Opens the default audio device and creates the context every other call
works through. Call it once, before creating sources.

openal.get_info.brief: Reads which OpenAL implementation is running.

openal.set_distance_model.brief: Sets the model every source's attenuation with distance is calculated by.

openal.new_source.brief:
Creates a sound source and loads a WAV file into it. Only a mono sound is
positioned; a stereo one plays as if it were at the listener.

openal.remove_source.brief:
Destroys a source and frees its sound. Reading or writing the source's
properties afterwards is an error.

openal.doppler_factor.brief: Scales the Doppler effect; a higher value makes it more noticeable. A value that is not positive is ignored.

openal.speed_of_sound.brief: The speed of sound the Doppler effect is calculated with. A value that is not positive is ignored.

openal.listener.brief: The point every sound is heard from.

openal.Info.renderer.brief: The renderer the implementation plays through.

openal.Info.extensions.brief: The OpenAL extensions the implementation supports, separated by spaces.

openal.Source.rewind.brief: Moves playback back to the start of the sound.

openal.Source.dx.brief: X component of the direction the sound cone points in.

openal.Source.max_distance.brief: The distance past which the source no longer attenuates under a clamped distance model, `1000` by default.

openal.Source.rolloff_factor.brief: How fast the source attenuates with distance.

openal.Source.reference_distance.brief: The distance at which the volume drops by half before `rolloff_factor` and `max_distance` apply, `50` by default.

openal.Source.min_gain.brief: The lowest gain the source attenuates to.

openal.Source.max_gain.brief: The highest gain the source plays at.

openal.Source.cone_outer_gain.brief: The gain outside the sound cone.

openal.Source.cone_inner_angle.brief: Inner angle of the sound cone, in degrees.

openal.Source.cone_outer_angle.brief: Outer angle of the sound cone, in degrees.

openal.Source.time.brief: Playback position in seconds; setting it seeks.

openal.Source.is_looping.brief: Whether the sound repeats indefinitely, `false` by default.

openal.Source.is_relative.brief: Whether the position is relative to the listener, `false` by default.

openal.Listener.orientation_at_x.brief: X component of the "at" vector, the direction the listener faces.

detour.brief: Recast/Detour navigation meshes: path queries and crowd agents.

detour.NavMesh.find_path.brief:
Finds a path between the points of the mesh nearest to `start` and
`finish`. When `finish` cannot be reached, the path ends at the
reachable point nearest to it; when no path is found, the table is empty.

detour.NavMesh.set_area_cost.brief:
Sets the cost of crossing each area. The defaults are `1` for areas 0, 2
and 3, `10` for area 1, `2` for area 4 and `1.5` for area 5.

detour.NavMesh.set_include_flags.brief:
Sets the polygon flags a path may cross. The default is every flag but
`0x10`, which marks disabled polygons.

detour.NavMesh.create_crowd.brief:
Prepares the mesh's crowd for up to 128 agents. Calling it again resets
the same crowd.

detour.NavMesh.delete.brief: Frees the mesh and its crowd. Neither can be used after it.

detour.PathPoint.position.brief: Where the corner lies on the mesh.

detour.PathPoint.area.brief: Area id of the polygon the corner lies on.

detour.PathPoint.start.brief: `true` on the corner the path starts from.

detour.PathPoint.end.brief: `true` on the corner the path ends at.

detour.PathPoint.offmesh.brief: `true` on a corner that starts an off-mesh connection.

detour.Crowd.add_agent.brief: Adds an agent at a position on the mesh.

detour.Crowd.remove_agent.brief: Removes an agent from the crowd.

detour.Crowd.set_target.brief: Sends agents toward the point of the mesh nearest to `target`.

detour.Crowd.reset_target.brief: Stops agents moving toward their target.

detour.Crowd.update.brief: Moves every agent by one step of the simulation.

detour.CrowdAgent.position.brief: Where the agent is after the update.

detour.CrowdAgent.velocity.brief: The agent's velocity after the update.

detour.CrowdAgent.state.brief: `"walk"` on the mesh, `"offmesh"` on an off-mesh connection, else `"invalid"`.

wave.brief: Wave simulation that floats, pitches and rolls game objects on a water surface.

wave.init.brief:
Initialize the wave simulation. Call it once before any other wave
function, with the same parameters the water shader uses.

wave.add_gameobject.brief:
Add a floating game object to the wave simulation.

The model must face -Z in its unrotated state: wave sampling, pitch, roll
and movement all assume it. To face another way at runtime, call
`set_yaw` after registration, or pass the matching `forward`.

wave.update_wave1.brief:
Live-update the wave 1 parameters. Call it in sync with the water
shader's wave 1 update to keep visuals and physics aligned.

wave.update_wave2.brief:
Live-update the wave 2 parameters. Call it in sync with the water
shader's wave 2 update to keep visuals and physics aligned.

wave.get_wave1_height.brief:
Sample the wave 1 height at a world position, at the simulation's
current time.

wave.get_wave2_height.brief:
Sample the wave 2 height at a world position, at the simulation's
current time.

wave.set_yaw.brief:
Override the yaw (heading) of a floater, for steering such as a boat
turning.

wave.move.brief:
Begin moving a floater forward at up to `max_speed`, accelerating by
`speed_factor` per second.

wave.stop.brief:
Stop a floater. Its target speed becomes `0` and it decelerates smoothly
by its speed factor.

wave.pause.brief: Pause or resume the wave update loop without removing entities.

wave.is_pause.brief: Whether the wave update loop is paused.

wave.shutdown.brief:
Shut down the wave simulation and free all resources. The extension
finalizer calls it automatically; call it yourself only to
reinitialize.

tile_raycast.brief: Ray Casting in tiled worlds using DDA algorithm.

tile_raycast.setup.brief: Sets up the tile map to cast rays through, replacing any previous one.

tile_raycast.cast.brief:
Casts a ray through the tile map and reports the first target tile it
hits. A miss returns `false` alone, so check `hit` before reading the
other values. Before `setup`, it logs an error and returns nothing.

tile_raycast.set_at.brief:
Returns the tile ID at a tile coordinate. The extension registers its
reader under this name and its writer as {@link tile_raycast.get_at}, the
reverse of what its documentation describes.

tile_raycast.get_at.brief:
Sets the tile ID at a tile coordinate. The extension registers its
writer under this name and its reader as {@link tile_raycast.set_at}, the
reverse of what its documentation describes.

tile_raycast.reset.brief: Clears all tile and tile map data.

tile_raycast.LEFT.brief: The ray hit the left side of the tile.

tile_raycast.RIGHT.brief: The ray hit the right side of the tile.

tile_raycast.TOP.brief: The ray hit the top side of the tile.

tile_raycast.BOTTOM.brief: The ray hit the bottom side of the tile.

png.brief: Encode raw pixels into PNG bytes and decode PNG bytes into a Defold buffer, powered by LodePNG.

png.encode_rgb.brief: Encodes raw RGB pixels (3 bytes per pixel) into PNG bytes.

png.encode_rgba.brief: Encodes raw RGBA pixels (4 bytes per pixel) into PNG bytes.

png.decode_rgb.brief:
Decodes a valid PNG into an RGB buffer with one uint8 `pixels` stream of
three components per pixel. The decoded rows are flipped vertically to
match Defold's buffer orientation. The extension ignores LodePNG's decode
error, so a corrupt PNG may crash the engine instead of returning nils.
Three nils mean the buffer could not be created or failed validation, so
check the buffer before reading the dimensions.

png.decode_rgba.brief:
Decodes a valid PNG into an RGBA buffer with one uint8 `pixels` stream of
four components per pixel. The decoded rows are flipped vertically to
match Defold's buffer orientation. The extension ignores LodePNG's decode
error, so a corrupt PNG may crash the engine instead of returning nils.
Three nils mean the buffer could not be created or failed validation, so
check the buffer before reading the dimensions.

png.info.brief: Reads the header of PNG bytes without decoding the pixels.

png.RGBA.brief: LodePNG color type: red, green, blue and alpha, as {@link png.info} reports it.

png.RGB.brief: LodePNG color type: red, green and blue, as {@link png.info} reports it.

png.GREY.brief: LodePNG color type: greyscale, as {@link png.info} reports it.

png.GREY_ALPHA.brief: LodePNG color type: greyscale and alpha, as {@link png.info} reports it.

png.PALETTE.brief: LodePNG color type: palette, as {@link png.info} reports it.

astar.delete_map.brief: Delete a map by its ID. This will free the memory used by the map.

astar.setup.brief: Initial setup. You have to setup the astar before calling any other methods.

astar.set_map.brief:
Set your map data.
* Setting new map data reset the current cache.

astar.set_costs.brief:
Set costs for walkable tiles on your `world` table. This table keys determine the walkable area.
Table's sum must be the `astar.DIRECTION_FOUR` or `astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT`.

astar.solve_near.brief: Finds the neighbours according to a given cost.

astar.reset_cache.brief: If your state space is huge, occasionally call `astar.reset_cache()` to free unused memory.

astar.get_at.brief: Returns the value from the map array by coordinates.

astar.set_at.brief: Set your value to the map array by coordinates.

astar.use_zero.brief:
Toggle start index 0 or 1 for tables and tile positions.
If set to `false`, [astar.solve](#astarsolvestart_x-start_y-end_x-end_y), [astar.solve_near](#astarsolve_nearstart_x-start_y-max_cost), [astar.get_at](#astarget_atx-y), [astar.set_at](#astarset_atx-y-value) methods expect positions start with 1 and returns table indexes from **1**.
Default is `false` = 1

astar.NO_SOLUTION.brief: Represents a result where no path is found.

astar.START_END_SAME.brief: Represents a result where the start and end points are the same.

applovin.brief: Functions and constants for interacting with AppLovin SDK.

applovin.initialize.brief: Initialize the AppLovin SDK with the provided SDK key.

applovin.set_callback.brief: Sets a callback function for receiving events from the SDK. Call `applovin.set_callback(nil)` to remove callback

applovin.is_initialized.brief: Checks if the AppLovin SDK has been initialized.

applovin.set_has_user_consent.brief: Sets whether the user has provided consent for interest-based advertising.

applovin.has_user_consent.brief: Checks if the user has provided consent for interest-based advertising.

applovin.set_is_age_restricted_user.brief: Sets whether the user is considered to be in an age-restricted category.

applovin.is_age_restricted_user.brief: Checks if the user is considered to be in an age-restricted category.

applovin.set_do_not_sell.brief: Sets whether the user has chosen to opt out of the sale of their personal information.

applovin.is_do_not_sell.brief: Checks if the user has chosen to opt out of the sale of their personal information.

applovin.set_terms_and_privacy_policy_fl.brief: Enables or disables the MAX Terms and Privacy Policy Flow.

applovin.set_privacy_policy_url.brief: Sets the privacy policy URL for MAX Terms and Privacy Policy Flow.

applovin.set_terms_of_service_url.brief: Sets terms of service URL for MAX Terms and Privacy Policy Flow.

applovin.set_consent_flow_debug_user_geo.brief: Sets the user geography for debugging purposes in the consent flow.

applovin.show_cmp_for_existing_user.brief: Shows the integrated consent management platform (CMP) flow for existing users.

applovin.has_supported_cmp.brief: Checks if a supported consent management platform is integrated.

applovin.is_tablet.brief: Checks if the current device is a tablet.

applovin.set_user_id.brief: Set internal user ID before initializing the SDK.

applovin.set_muted.brief: Sets whether ads from certain mediated SDK networks should be muted.

applovin.is_muted.brief: Checks if ads are set to be muted.

applovin.is_verbose_logging_enabled.brief: Checks if verbose logging is enabled.

applovin.set_creative_debugger_enabled.brief: Enables or disables the creative debugger.

applovin.set_test_device_advertising_ids.brief: Enables devices to receive test ads.

applovin.load_interstitial.brief: Loads an interstitial ad for the given ad unit ID.

applovin.is_interstitial_ready.brief: Checks if an interstitial ad is ready to be shown.

applovin.show_interstitial.brief: Shows an interstitial ad for the given ad unit ID and the placement name.

applovin.set_interstitial_extra_paramete.brief: Sets extra parameters for an interstitial ad.

applovin.load_rewarded_ad.brief: Loads a rewarded ad for the given ad unit ID.

applovin.is_rewarded_ad_ready.brief: Checks if a rewarded ad is ready to be shown.

iapm.finish.brief: Consume a product transaction. Call this only for consumable products and only after content delivery succeeds. Calling this function with `auto_finish_transactions` enabled is ignored and a warning is printed. The `transaction.state` field must equal `iapm.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED`. Calling this for a transaction whose `type` is `subs` is ignored.

Prefer the `iap.public_key` game.project setting so the key is available while pending purchases are processed.

splitmix64.random.brief: When called without arguments, returns a uniform pseudo-random real number in the range [0,1). When called with an integer number m, splitmix64.random returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range [1, m]. When called with two integer numbers m and n, splitmix64.random returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range [m, n].

splitmix64.randomseed.brief: Sets x as the "seed" for the pseudo-random generator: equal seeds produce equal sequences of numbers. Accepts a number or a string (decimal representation of uint64) for full 64-bit precision.

splitmix64.state.brief: Returns the current internal state x as a string. Use this to save/restore state or pass to randomseed for full 64-bit precision (Lua double cannot represent all uint64 values).

splitmix64.randomchoice.brief: Returns a random value from array t. If the array is empty an error is raised.

If all weights are 0 or a weight is negative, an error is raised.

splitmix64.new_instance.brief: Creates a new RNG instance with independent state. Optional seed (number or string) for reproducibility.

ump.brief: Google User Messaging Platform consent API for Android. The table is absent on other platforms.

ump.request_consent_info_update.brief:
Request fresh consent information and show a consent form if required.
Call on every launch. The callback runs on the Defold update thread after
the update and any required form finish unless defer_form is true. In
deferred mode the callback runs after the information update, before any
form opens; call show_consent_form_if_required to finish the flow.
A successful callback means no UMP error, not consent to personalized ads.

ump.show_consent_form_if_required.brief:
Continue a successful deferred consent-information update. Check
was_consent_form_required() to decide whether to show an application
notice first. Call only once, after that notice has closed. The callback
runs after the required form closes or fails, or immediately if no form
is required. Advertising must wait for this callback.

ump.show_privacy_options_form.brief:
Open the UMP privacy-options form in response to user input. Check
is_privacy_options_required() first. A successful callback means the form
closed without an error, not that the user granted consent.

ump.is_privacy_options_required.brief: Whether UMP requires a privacy-options entry point. Returns false before consent information is available.

ump.can_request_ads.brief:
UMP ad-request eligibility. Check after the current update callback.
Before then, this can reflect consent stored from an earlier session.

ump.get_consent_status.brief:
Google consent status: 0 unknown, 1 not required, 2 required, 3 obtained.
Returns -1 before the consent-information object exists. Status 3 does
not distinguish personalized from non-personalized advertising.

ump.get_request_state.brief:
Diagnostic state of the latest consent information update and form.
Prefer the request callback to polling this value.

ump.was_consent_form_required.brief:
Whether the latest successful information update found a required normal
consent form. Resets when a new update starts. May remain true if that
form later fails.

ump.get_privacy_options_state.brief: Diagnostic state of the latest privacy-options form.

ump.get_gdpr_applies.brief:
Read IABTCF_gdprApplies from Android default preferences after a
successful UMP update. This is a GDPR applicability signal, not a country
code or vendor consent.

ump.get_purpose_consents.brief:
Read the raw IABTCF_PurposeConsents bit string from Android default
preferences. Call after a successful UMP update or privacy-options
callback. The third character represents TCF Purpose 3 consent.

ump.reset_consent_information.brief:
Clear UMP consent information for testing if its object has been created.
Start a new request afterward. Diagnostic request/form states are not
reset by this call.

ump.initialize_mobile_ads_sdk.brief:
Legacy, nonfunctional export. Its required Java method is absent from
this extension. Do not call it. If using the Defold AdMob extension,
call admob.initialize() after the UMP flow instead.

ump.REQUEST_STATE_UPDATING.brief: 0; initial state or consent information update in progress.

ump.REQUEST_STATE_COMPLETE.brief: 1; update and form step finished without a UMP error.

ump.REQUEST_STATE_FORM_PENDING.brief: 3; update succeeded and the form step is waiting or in progress.

ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_DISMISSED.brief: 2; privacy-options form closed without a UMP error.

ump.GDPR_APPLIES_UNKNOWN.brief: -1; IAB TCF GDPR applicability value missing or invalid.

ump.GDPR_APPLIES_NO.brief: 0; IAB TCF value says GDPR does not apply.

ump.GDPR_APPLIES_YES.brief: 1; IAB TCF value says GDPR applies.

voronoi.brief: Creates bounded two-dimensional Voronoi diagrams using jc_voronoi 0.10.0.

voronoi.create.brief: Creates a reusable Voronoi diagram context for a rectangular area.

voronoi.destroy.brief: Releases a diagram context. Do not use the context after destroying it.

voronoi.generate.brief: Replaces the diagram with sites generated from a flat list of x/y coordinates. Duplicate sites may be removed.

voronoi.relax.brief: Moves every input point toward the average of its site and cell vertices, then regenerates the diagram.

voronoi.get_sites.brief: Returns every generated site. A site contains p, index, boundary, edges, and the convenience field area. The p field is { x, y }; index is the 1-based original input index; boundary reports whether the cell touches the clipping boundary; and edges contains counter-clockwise edge tables.

voronoi.get_num_sites.brief: Returns diagram.numsites, the number of unique generated sites. This may be smaller than the input count when points are duplicated.

voronoi.get_site.brief: Returns the generated site for a 1-based original input index. The site has the same fields as entries returned by get_sites().

voronoi.get_num_vertices.brief: Returns diagram.numvertices, the number of unique Voronoi vertices.

voronoi.get_vertices.brief: Returns all unique Voronoi vertices as { x, y } point tables. Edge vertex indices refer to this array.

voronoi.get_edges.brief: Returns every diagram edge. Each edge contains sites, pos, and vertices. sites contains two 1-based input indices, with 0 denoting the clipping boundary. pos contains two { x, y } endpoints. vertices contains two 1-based indices into get_vertices(), with 0 denoting an invalid endpoint.

voronoi.get_delauney_edges.brief: Returns the Delauney edges produced by the upstream jcv_delauney iterator. Each entry contains edge, sites, and pos fields matching jcv_delauney_edge. The upstream spelling "delauney" is preserved in the Lua function name.

voronoi.get_debug_image.brief: Rasterizes the current diagram into an RGB buffer matching the context dimensions.

wavedash.ready_for_events.brief: Signal that the game is ready to receive events.

wavedash.request_fullscreen_async.brief: Request fullscreen mode. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'requestFullscreen' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.toggle_fullscreen_async.brief: Toggle fullscreen mode. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'toggleFullscreen' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.get_user_language.brief: Get the current user's preferred language code, such as "en" or "pt-BR". Compare it with the LANGUAGE_CODE_* constants.

wavedash.get_user_jwt_async.brief: Request a user JWT. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'getUserJwt' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.get_or_create_leaderboard_async.brief: Get or create a leaderboard. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'getOrCreateLeaderboard' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.get_my_leaderboard_entries_asyn.brief: Get the current user's leaderboard entries. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'getMyLeaderboardEntries' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.list_leaderboard_entries_around.brief: List leaderboard entries around a user. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'listLeaderboardEntriesAroundUser' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.list_leaderboard_entries_async.brief: List leaderboard entries. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'listLeaderboardEntries' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.upload_leaderboard_score_async.brief:
Upload a leaderboard score. Pass ugc_id to attach a UGC item, such as a replay, to the entry. Pass metadata to attach small key/value data to the entry: string keys with string, number or boolean values.
This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'uploadLeaderboardScore' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.delete_ugc_item_async.brief: Delete a UGC item. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'deleteUGCItem' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.list_ugc_items_async.brief: List UGC items. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'listUGCItems' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.delete_remote_file_async.brief: Delete a remote file. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'deleteRemoteFile' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.download_remote_file_async.brief: Download a remote file. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'downloadRemoteFile' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.upload_remote_file_async.brief: Upload a remote file. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'uploadRemoteFile' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.list_remote_directory_async.brief: List a remote directory. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'listRemoteDirectory' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.download_remote_directory_async.brief: Download a remote directory. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'downloadRemoteDirectory' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.write_local_file_async.brief: Write a local file. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'writeLocalFile' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.read_local_file_async.brief: Read a local file. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'readLocalFile' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.request_stats_async.brief: Request stats. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'requestStats' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.get_p2p_max_payload_size.brief: Get the maximum P2P payload size.

wavedash.get_p2p_max_incoming_messages.brief: Get the maximum number of incoming P2P messages.

wavedash.get_p2p_outgoing_message_buffer.brief: Get the P2P outgoing message buffer.

wavedash.read_p2p_message_from_channel.brief: Read a P2P message from a channel.

wavedash.drain_p2p_channel_to_buffer.brief: Drain a P2P channel to a buffer.

wavedash.create_lobby_async.brief: Create a lobby. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'createLobby' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.join_lobby_async.brief: Join a lobby. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'joinLobby' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.list_available_lobbies_async.brief: List available lobbies. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'listAvailableLobbies' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.get_num_lobby_users.brief: Get the number of lobby users.

wavedash.set_lobby_data.brief: Set lobby data. Passing nil deletes the key.

wavedash.leave_lobby_async.brief: Leave a lobby. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'leaveLobby' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.invite_user_to_lobby_async.brief: Invite a user to a lobby. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'inviteUserToLobby' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.get_lobby_invite_link_async.brief: Get a lobby invite link. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'getLobbyInviteLink' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.update_user_presence_async.brief: Update user presence. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'updateUserPresence' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.ensure_gameplay_jwt_async.brief: Ensure a gameplay JWT is available. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'ensureGameplayJwt' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.is_entitled_async.brief: Returns whether the player owns the given paid content. This is a UX hint, not a security check — Wavedash re-verifies ownership when serving the paid files. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'isEntitled' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.get_entitlements_async.brief: Returns every paid content identifier the player owns for this game. This is a UX hint, not a security check — Wavedash re-verifies ownership when serving the paid files. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'getEntitlements' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.trigger_paywall_async.brief: Open the Wavedash paywall for the given paid content. Resolves immediately with data true if the player already owns it; otherwise resolves with whether the purchase completed. Handle the purchase itself in the PurchaseCompleted event, which also covers purchases made outside the game. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'triggerPaywall' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.get_unfulfilled_purchases_async.brief: Consumable purchases the game hasn't fulfilled, oldest first, each shaped like the PurchaseCompleted payload. These already arrive as PurchaseCompleted events at launch, but each purchase fires once per session: use this to retry one whose fulfill_purchase_async call failed. This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'getUnfulfilledPurchases' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.fulfill_purchase_async.brief: Mark a consumable purchase fulfilled once the grant is saved, so it stops being redelivered. A game's backend can do the same with POST /api/purchases/{purchaseId}/fulfill and the purchase's receiptJwt; both are idempotent, so calling either or both is safe. Resolves with a status in data: FULFILLED, ALREADY_FULFILLED (also success), or NOT_FOUND (unknown or refunded: don't grant it). This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'fulfillPurchase' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine.

wavedash.EVENT_ENTITLEMENTS_GRANTED.brief: Deprecated: handle EVENT_PURCHASE_COMPLETED instead, which also covers consumables.

wavedash.EVENT_PURCHASE_COMPLETED.brief: Fired once per purchase made while the game is running (in-game paywall, game page, gift, another tab), plus, at launch, once per consumable still unfulfilled. Payload: { purchaseId, contentIdentifier, type, fulfilled, purchasedAt, receiptJwt }. Durables arrive with fulfilled true, already granted. For a consumable, grant it, then call fulfill_purchase_async(purchaseId); until then it's redelivered every launch, so dedupe on purchaseId if you persist grants.

wavedash.PURCHASE_TYPE_DURABLE.brief: type field on the EVENT_PURCHASE_COMPLETED payload for content purchased once that never expires.

wavedash.PURCHASE_TYPE_CONSUMABLE.brief: type field on the EVENT_PURCHASE_COMPLETED payload for content that can be purchased repeatedly and is fulfilled by the game.

wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_FULFILL.brief: fulfill_purchase_async status: marked fulfilled by this call.

wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_ALREADY.brief: fulfill_purchase_async status: also success. The game or its backend fulfilled it earlier, or it's a durable.

wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_NOT_FOU.brief: fulfill_purchase_async status: unknown purchase, or it was refunded. Don't grant it.

webrtc.create_channel.brief: Creates a datachannel with a specified peer and type

webrtc.send_message.brief: Sends a message to a peer by a channel

webrtc.TYPE_UNRELIABLE.brief: An unreliable DataChannel connection with unordered packets

webrtc.TYPE_UNRELIABLE_ORDERED.brief: An unreliable DataChannel connection with ordered packets

webrtc.TYPE_RELIABLE.brief: A reliable DataChannel connection with ordered packets

webrtc.EVENT_CHANNEL_OPENED.brief: An event called when a new DataChannel is opened

webrtc.EVENT_CHANNEL_CLOSED.brief: An event called when a new DataChannel is closed

webrtc.EVENT_SIGNALING_DATA.brief: An event called when webrtc generates new signaling data

xmath.brief: Mathematical operations for vectors, quaternions, and matrices

xmath.mul.brief: Multiply a vector by a scalar.

xmath.div.brief: Divide a vector by a scalar.

xmath.cross.brief: Calculate the cross product of two vectors.

xmath.mul_per_elem.brief: Perform element-wise multiplication between two vectors.

xmath.rotate.brief: Rotate a vector by a quaternion.

xmath.vector.brief: Set the value of a vector to (0, 0, 0) or (0, 0, 0, 1).

xmath.conj.brief: Calculate the conjugate of a quaternion.

xmath.quat_axis_angle.brief: Set the value of a quaternion from an axis and an angle.

xmath.quat_basis.brief: Set the value of a quaternion from x, y, and z base unit vectors.

xmath.quat_from_to.brief: Set the value of a quaternion to rotate from one vector to another.

xmath.quat_rotation_x.brief: Set the value of a quaternion for rotation around the x-axis.

xmath.quat_rotation_y.brief: Set the value of a quaternion for rotation around the y-axis.

xmath.quat_rotation_z.brief: Set the value of a quaternion for rotation around the z-axis.

xmath.quat.brief: Set the value of a quaternion to (0, 0, 0, 1).

xmath.euler_to_quat.brief: Set the value of a quaternion from Euler angles (in degrees, YZX rotation order).

xmath.lerp.brief: Linearly interpolate between two numbers, vectors, or quaternions. For numbers, pass (t, n1, n2) and returns the interpolated number. For vectors/quaternions, pass (v_in_place, t, v1, v2) to modify v_in_place.

xmath.slerp.brief: Spherically interpolate between two vectors or quaternions.

xmath.matrix.brief: Set the value of a matrix to the identity matrix or copy another matrix.

xmath.matrix_axis_angle.brief: Set the value of a matrix for rotation around an axis by an angle.

xmath.matrix_from_quat.brief: Set the value of a matrix from a quaternion.

xmath.matrix_frustum.brief: Set the value of a frustum matrix from given values.

xmath.matrix_inv.brief: Calculate the inverse of a matrix.

xmath.matrix_look_at.brief: Set the value of a matrix from supplied look-at parameters.

xmath.matrix4_orthographic.brief: Set the value of an orthographic projection matrix.

xmath.matrix_ortho_inv.brief: The resulting matrix is the inverse of the supplied matrix.

xmath.matrix4_perspective.brief: Set the value of a perspective projection matrix.

xmath.matrix_rotation_x.brief: Set the value of a matrix for rotation around the x-axis.

xmath.matrix_rotation_y.brief: Set the value of a matrix for rotation around the y-axis.

xmath.matrix_rotation_z.brief: Set the value of a matrix for rotation around the z-axis.

xmath.matrix_translation.brief: Set the value of a matrix for translation.

xmath.quat_matrix4.brief: Set the value of a quaternion from a matrix4.

xmath.matrix4_compose.brief: Set the value of a matrix from translation, rotation and scale.

xmath.matrix4_scale.brief: Set the value of a matrix from scale. Can take a vector3, a single number for uniform scale, or 3 numbers for x, y, z scale.

xmath.clamp.brief: Clamp input value in range [min, max]. For numbers, pass (value, min, max) and returns the clamped number. For vectors, pass (v_in_place, value, min, max) to modify v_in_place. min and max can be numbers or matching vector types.

xoshiro256.brief: Functions for interacting with the Xoshiro256 native extension

xoshiro256.seed.brief: Create state for the pseudo-random generator: equal seeds produce equal sequences of numbers. Accepts a number or a string (decimal representation of uint64, max 20 digits in the string) if full 64-bit precision required. State is seeded using splitmix64 algorithm.

xoshiro256.random.brief: When called without arguments, returns a uniform pseudo-random real number in the range [0,1). When called with an integer number m, returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range [1, m]. When called with two integer numbers m and n, returns a uniform pseudo-random integer in the range [m, n].

xoshiro256.float_range.brief: Generates a random number in floating range [m, n)

xoshiro256.clone.brief: Creates and returns an independent copy of the state

xoshiro256.to_string.brief: Convert state to string. Used for saving the state. String is formed as 4 uint64 values separated by ':', e.g. "s0:s1:s2:s3".

xoshiro256.from_string.brief: Convert previously saved string back to state.
